Head of Revenue Operations

Location: San Francisco

Employment Type: Full time

Building Open Superintelligence Infrastructure

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack - from frontier agentic models to the infra that enables anyone to create, train, and deploy them. We aggregate and orchestrate global compute into a single control plane and pair it with the full RL post-training stack: environments, secure sandboxes, verifiable evals, and our async RL trainer. We enable researchers, startups and enterprises to run end-to-end reinforcement learning at frontier scale, adapting models to real tools, workflows, and deployment contexts.

We recently raised $15mm in funding (total of $20mm raised) led by Founders Fund, with participation from Menlo Ventures and prominent angels including Andrej Karpathy (Eureka AI, Tesla, OpenAI), Tri Dao (Together AI), Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis), Clem Delangue (Huggingface), Emad Mostaque (Stability AI) and many others.

Your Role

Own the end-to-end revenue operations engine across Sales, Growth, and Customer teams. You will design the systems, data models, and processes that make revenue predictable and GTM execution surgical. Own CRM architecture, forecasting, compensation design, deal desk, and analytics. Turn noisy signals across compute usage, post-training work, and pipeline into clear decisions and repeatable motion. This is a foundational role for someone who wants to be the backbone of how Prime Intellect goes from deals to durable revenue.

Responsibilities

  • Own GTM systems across the funnel - CRM, marketing automation, product analytics, billing, and data warehouse.
  • Design and maintain CRM architecture so that pipeline, stages, and fields reflect reality and support accurate forecasting.
  • Build and standardize reporting for leadership: pipeline health, conversion rates, cohort performance, NRR, GRR, compute GMV.
  • Partner with Head of Enterprise Sales and AEs on territory design, quota setting, compensation plans, and performance tracking.
  • Run deal desk for complex deals - pricing structure, approvals, non-standard terms.
  • Connect product usage and compute consumption data to revenue metrics for usage-based and hybrid models.
  • Define and implement lead routing, SLAs, and handoffs between Marketing, Sales, TAM, and Solutions.
  • Automate repetitive GTM workflows so Sales and CS can focus on customers, not admin.
  • Create and maintain a single source of truth for revenue data across tools and teams.
  • Partner with Finance on revenue recognition, forecasting assumptions, and board reporting inputs.
  • Evaluate and manage the GTM tech stack - select tools, own vendor relationships, ensure adoption.
  • Build documentation and playbooks for how we run revenue operations as the team scales.

What We Are Looking For

  • 5+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or Growth Operations at B2B SaaS or infrastructure companies.
  • Deep hands-on CRM experience (HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar) where you owned data model, workflows, and reporting.
  • Strong analytical skill set - SQL or BI tools, cohort analysis, funnel modeling, forecasting.
  • Experience partnering closely with Sales leadership on pipeline reviews, forecasting, and compensation design.

Minted seeks a Software Engineering Manager to lead the Shopping Portfolio’s Marketing Enablement team engineers, building consumer-facing e-commerce experiences. Job Description: Chief Development & Communications Officer

Organization: The Housing Collective

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

Location: Hybrid | In Bridgeport, CT office 2-3 days per week

About The Housing Collective:

The Housing Collective is a Connecticut-based nonprofit organization dedicated to ending homelessness and ensuring equitable access to safe, affordable housing for all. Through innovative programs and collaborative partnerships, we strive to create lasting solutions to housing challenges across the state. As a backbone organization, HC operates at the intersection of policy, practice, community voice, and investment—aligning systems, not just delivering programs. HC partners with more than 200 organizations statewide and is recognized as a leading voice in housing and homelessness systems change in Connecticut.

HC maintains an annual budget of approximately$15 millionand advances systems change through a diversified revenue model that includesgovernment funding, philanthropic support, individual and corporate giving, and earned revenue. HC’s work spans multiple initiatives and regions and requires sophisticated revenue strategy, strong external positioning, and disciplined cross-functional execution.

Position Overview:

The Chief Development & Communications Officer (CDCO) oversees a multi-million-dollar annual revenue portfolio spanning public and private sources. They are a senior executive responsible for strategically positioning The Housing Collective to grow, sustain, and future-proof revenue across all funding streams, including government grants and contracts, philanthropic funding, individual and corporate giving, and fee-for-service business development.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and serving on the Senior Leadership Team, the CDCO works alongside organizational leadership to co-design enterprise-wide revenue strategies and leads the outreach, engagement, and cultivation of funders and donors in support of those strategies.

The CDCO provides executive leadership over Development and Communications, ensuring that fund development strategy, external positioning, and narrative are tightly aligned with HC’s long-term goals. The role holds annual budget authority for the Development & Communications Department and is accountable for revenue performance across all funding sources.

The Housing Collective is at a pivotal moment of organizational growth and evolution. While HC has built scale and impact through public funding to support its work, the external funding landscape is shifting rapidly, and the organization is intentionally building the infrastructure, strategies, and relationships needed to significantly expand private philanthropy, individual giving, and fee-for-service revenue. The CDCO will play a critical role in designing and scaling this next phase of HC’s revenue model—strengthening financial resilience, diversifying funding sources, and positioning the organization for long-term sustainability and impact.

Key Responsibilities

Revenue Strategy, Funder Engagement & Growth

  • Work in close partnership with the CEO and Senior Leadership Team to design and refine HC’s revenue strategy, aligning funding priorities with organizational strategy and systems-change goals.
  • Serve as a key thought partner to initiative leaders, translating program strategy into fundable narratives and investment pathways without directing program execution.
  • Lead execution of agreed-upon revenue strategies across funding streams.
  • Design and lead outreach, engagement, and cultivation strategies for public, philanthropic, corporate, and individual funders, building durable, long-term relationships.
  • Personally engage with key funders, donors, and partners, and support the CEO and senior leaders in high-level relationship management and solicitation.
  • Develop and manage fund development revenue forecasting, pipeline visibility, and performance tracking to inform executive and Board decision-making.
  • Ensure HC’s revenue model is diversified, resilient, and positioned for sustainable growth in a dynamic funding environment.

Government, Philanthropic & Grant Strategy (Pre-Award)

  • Collaborate with the CEO, Chief Initiative Officer(s), and program leadership to shape government and philanthropic funding strategies, including funder targeting, positioning, and sequencing.
  • Lead the pre-award fund development process, including grant writing oversight, proposal development workflows, internal coordination, and submission timelines.
  • Ensure proposals accurately reflect agreed-upon program priorities while advancing HC’s broader organizational positioning and revenue strategy.
  • In partnership with the Finance team, monitor revenue performance, budget alignment, and compliance risk across funding streams.
  • Partner closely with the Finance team, which assumes responsibility for post-award grant and contract management, to ensure clear handoffs, aligned budgets, compliance, and timely reporting.
  • Establish clear cross-functional workflows across Development, Finance, and program teams.

Individual Giving, Corporate Partnerships & Board Engagement

  • Help build a strong culture of shared accountability for fund development at the Board and executive level.
  • Design and lead HC’s individual giving and major donor strategy, including campaign design, cultivation pathways, and stewardship frameworks.
  • Lead strategy for corporate and financial institution partnerships, aligning revenue opportunities with HC’s mission and external positioning.
  • Enable and support executive and Board participation in fund development.
  • Serve as the primary staff lead for a Board committee related to development and/or external affairs, partnering with trustees to advance fundraising, donor engagement, and external advocacy.

Communications, Narrative & External Positioning

  • Provide executive oversight of HC’s Communications Department, ensuring alignment between communications, revenue strategy, and organizational positioning.
  • Ensure communications strategy strengthens HC’s positioning with funders, policymakers, and field leaders at the state and national level.
  • Directly supervise the Communications Director, who manages day-to-day communications operations and HC’s external public relations and strategic communications contract.
  • Collaborate closely with the CEO, who serves as HC’s primary external spokesperson, to support messaging and preparation tied to organizational growth and funder engagement.

Team Leadership & Department Management

  • Lead the Development & Communications team with a focus on strategy, systems, and execution excellence.
  • Directly supervise a Development Associate, providing coaching, performance management, and workload prioritization.
  • Design and scale the Development & Communications Department over time, including potential future roles such as Development Manager and Development Director, and Grant Writer.
  • Build and maintain clear internal workflows that define responsibilities across Development, Finance, and program teams and support effective collaboration.

Transition & Organizational Continuity

  • Participate in a structured transition period with the outgoing Chief Philanthropy and Communications Officer to ensure continuity of relationships, institutional knowledge, and strategic momentum.
  • Maintain confidence among funders, partners, Board members, and staff during a period of leadership transition.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 18–24 months, the Chief Development & Communications Officer will have strengthened HC’s revenue infrastructure, expanded private and philanthropic funding, launched or scaled fee-for-service revenue, and embedded fund development as a shared leadership and Board priority—positioning the organization for long-term resilience and impact.

NOTE: Candidates with deep development experience who are continuing to build their communications leadership skills are strongly encouraged to apply.

Job Description

Business & Revenue Operations Lead

San Francisco, CAAbout Metriport

Metriport is an open-source data intelligence platform that helps healthcare organizations access and exchange patient data in real-time. We integrate with all major US healthcare IT systems and tap into comprehensive medical data for 300+ million individuals.

We've found product-market fit with multi-million ARR, 100+ customers (including Strive Health, Circle Medical, and Brightside Health), backing from top VCs, and years of runway. We're ready to scale. We're a tight-knit, high-performing team of mostly former founders (including two YC alumni). We're engineering-heavy, operate with minimal bureaucracy and high autonomy, and hire based on competence, not prestige. We push hard—founders work six days a week from our SF office—but give everyone freedom to craft their schedule. We measure output and we're committed to sustainable intensity.

The Role

This isn’t a standard FP&A role where you sit behind a spreadsheet and wait for instructions. As our first dedicated Finance hire on the BizOps team, you will manage our entire financial stack end-to-end. You will be responsible for the integrity of our books, the efficiency of our revenue collection, the automation of our internal financial operations, and more.

If you need "perfect information" to make progress, or if you think any task is "beneath" your background, this is not the right fit. We need a Swiss Army Knife who can lead a board-level financial review in the morning and troubleshoot a HubSpot-to-Stripe sync in the afternoon.

What You’ll Own

  • The Financial Stack: End-to-end management of banking, invoicing, bookkeeping, and FP&A.

  • The Close: Own month-end and year-end close, ensuring books are pristine by the 15th of each month.

  • Operations & RevOps: Heavily support the Sales team by driving RevOps efforts and integrating systems (e.g., HubSpot to Stripe, Stripe to QuickBooks).

  • Reporting: Track and improve our collections rate, budget vs. actuals (BVA), and departmental purchase request turnaround.

  • External Relations: Serve as the professional face of Metriport to accountants, investors, vendors, and customers.

Requirements

  • Experience: 5+ years in Investment Banking, MBB Consulting, or a high-growth startup (Seed to Series B).

  • Process Ownership. You have 2+ years of experience creating processes from scratch and better existing processes in a professional work setting.

  • Education: Degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field.

  • Technical Mastery: Expert-level Excel and Google Sheets skills. Powerpoint skills that can distill complex data into clear narratives.

  • Ambiguity Tolerance: You thrive in fast-paced environments and know how to drive projects to completion without a playbook.

  • Location: Based in San Francisco (or willing to relocate) with a 5-day-a-week in-office presence.

  • The "Metriport" Mindset: Low ego, high ownership. You ask "Why can't this be done in 3 days?" instead of 3 weeks.

Bonus Points

  • Automation: Experience automating workflows via Zapier or Python script.

  • Familiarity With Finance Tech: Proficiency with QuickBooks, Brex or Ramp, Stripe, and CRMs.

  • Domain: Experience in the Healthcare IT or Healthtech space.

How We Measure Success

  • Are the books closed by the 15th?

  • Is our collections rate exceeding our target threshold?

  • How tight is the delta between our budget and our actuals?

  • Are you reducing the "work about work" by implementing better processes?

Metriport provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Compensation Range: $140K - $175K

This leader will solid-line report to our Chief Revenue Officer and dotted line to the Chief Strategy and Operations Officer.

  • Own and set the vision for the Revenue Operations function, fostering a culture of collaboration and data-driven decision making, prioritizing an achievable roadmap for each squad.

  • Oversee all deal operations including RFP management, deal execution, etc
  • Drive GTM strategies across all customer segments and Partner sales motions; collaborating cross-functionally to ensure sales, marketing and customer success processes are efficient, aligned and following best in class practices.

About You
  • 10+ years of relevant experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations and/or Strategic Sales roles for high growth SaaS products including several years as a manager of senior leaders.
  • Proven experience building a scalable Revenue Operations strategy for companies growing from $50MM to $100M+ in ARR.
  • Strong Executive presence and ability to influence and work cross functionally with C-Level executives.
  • Established history of driving multiple complex projects at the same time to on-time completion in a fast-moving environment.
  • Strong quantitative skills and are highly data fluent - you’re able to develop and communicate penetrating insights that inform how we organize and scale our revenue teams.
  • Operate as an inclusive leader with a proven history of building and developing diverse & inclusive teams, and attracting, retaining and developing your leadership team.
  • Have demonstrated leadership & interpersonal capability in driving cross-functional execution, leading global change management initiatives through ambiguity, and proven ability to influence across organizational boundaries.
  • Are customer obsessed and operate with a focus on delivering exceptional customer experiences.
  • Have experience at scaling Enterprise SaaS companies with go-to-market models and partners.
  • Expert in the Salesforce ecosystem and GTM tools.
  • Have the ability to uplevel and build out the capabilities of teams and improve real-time insights & analytics, processes and automation.
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred
Location and Travel
  • Location:  Bay Area required.  Expectation to be in Mountain View / San Francisco offices on a regular basis. 
  • Travel:  Expected to travel occasionally to visit our GTM and Rev Ops teams, to attend Sales events and certain Customer events.

Compensation for this position consists of a maximum $240,000 salary + meaningful equity.

 

Actual compensation offered will vary based on a number of factors including prior experience and location. Equity value is subject to company valuation and vesting requirements.

If you share our passion for building a sustainable, intelligent, and efficient world, you’re in the right place. Established in 2017 and headquartered in Mountain View, California, we're a series C start-up, with teams in Mountain View, San Francisco (California), Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca (Romania), Paris (France), Munich (Germany), London (UK), Pune (India), and Sydney (Australia).  So join us, and let’s build this!

Aera Technology respects the privacy of your data.  Please take the time to read our European GDPR privacy candidate notice available here

 

Benefits:

 

At Aera Technology, we strive to support our Aeranauts and their loved ones through different stages of life with a variety of attractive benefits, and great perks. In addition to offering a competitive salary and company stock options, we have other great benefits available. You’ll find comprehensive medical, vision and dental plans, a 401K plan, flexible paid time off, generous parental leave, and much more. We believe in a flexible working environment, to allow our Aeranauts to perform at their best, ensuring a healthy work-life balance.   • Delivered measurable revenue growth and market share gains, supported by clear examples of strategic client wins
  • Elevated the capability and performance of the leadership team and broader revenue organization
  • Positioned HCMG as the most forward‑thinking and effective media partner in the Connecticut market

Required Experience

  • Proven senior revenue leadership experience within media, advertising, ad tech, SaaS, or closely related industries (required)
  • Demonstrated success building and scaling multi‑channel revenue organizations, ideally within complex or evolving business models
  • Track record of driving growth through both strategy and execution, including go‑to‑market transformation

Core Capabilities

  • Deep understanding of modern revenue models, including digital advertising, performance marketing, and integrated client solutions
  • Strong perspective on the application of AI and automation within sales organizations, with evidence of practical implementation

  • Exceptional leadership presence, with a track record of attracting, developing, and retaining high‑performing teams
  • Highly client‑centric mindset, with a belief that sustainable revenue growth is driven by delivering measurable client value

Additional Requirements

Why This Role, Why Now

There are CRO roles focused on optimization. This is a role focused on reinvention.

  • CTInsider.com is an unmatched audience asset, reaching more Connecticut residents than any other local news source
  • You will have true authority to reshape the commercial model, not just incrementally improve it
  • The AI‑enabled sales infrastructure is being built now—you will define how it works and how it wins
  • The outcomes of this role directly support local journalism and community impact

About the Team

You will lead 9 direct reports across four core functions:

  • Sales Directors overseeing key segments and client relationships
  • SDR team driving top‑of‑funnel activity
  • Revenue Operations managing systems, data, and performance infrastructure
  • Marketing leading brand, content, and demand generation

The foundation is strong. The opportunity is to elevate, align, and accelerate.

Ready to reshape local media in Connecticut?

We are looking for revenue leaders who are ready to move beyond legacy models and build what comes next.

If that is you, let’s talk.

About Hearst Newspapers

With 2,500 employees across the nation, HNP represents a network of 24 daily and 52 weekly publications, including the San Francisco Chronicle, Houston Chronicle, San Antonio Express‑News and Albany Times Union, several top digital‑only news and lifestyle sites, marketing services businesses, and entertainment businesses such as King Features Syndicate. Base pay range

$110,000.00/yr - $143,000.00/yr

The realities (read this before applying)

  • Priorities shift; you’ll need to adapt quickly and make tradeoffs.
  • You’ll build v1 fast, iterate, and improve continuously.
  • You won’t have perfect inputs, perfect tooling, or unlimited resources—yet you’ll still be expected to deliver outcomes.
  • You’ll own work outside of the job description to keep the business moving.

If you want a narrow scope and want to build off pre‑existing infrastructure, this role will be frustrating. If you like building, iterating, and shipping fast, you’ll thrive.

Ramp & readiness systems

  • Build and run onboarding and internal certification programs for BDRs, AEs, and SEs with clear readiness standards.
  • Create repeatable coaching loops: call reviews, role plays, skill drills, and deal support—especially for early‑tenure reps.
  • Define “what good looks like” for each role at each stage (a practical readiness framework).

Seller efficiency and time‑to‑value enablement

  • Deliver in‑the‑flow assets that make reps effective faster: discovery checklists, demo narratives, stakeholder meeting agendas, objection‑handling guides, mutual plan templates, proposal/value summaries, and negotiation “trade” frameworks.
  • Reduce reliance on live training by building scalable enablement that reps can actually use day‑to‑day.

Qualification & execution operating system

  • Establish SPICED as the shared operating system across GTM teams: common language, consistent deal narratives, and customer‑centric execution.
  • Define how SPICED is used day‑to‑day: discovery expectations, deal reviews, handoffs, and “what must be true” by stage.
  • Use MEDDPICCR as a complementary enterprise‑grade qualification and deal inspection framework—especially for complex, multi‑stakeholder opportunities.
  • Embed SPICED (and MEDDPICCR where appropriate) into:
    • Coaching scorecards and call review standards
    • Stage expectations and deal review prompts
    • Handoff checklists (BDR→AE, AE→SE, Sales→CS)
    • CRM reinforcement (fields/prompts/templates), in partnership with RevOps

Enterprise‑ready selling enablement

  • Enable reps to run complex enterprise deals with repeatable plays:
    • Stakeholder mapping + multi‑threading standards
    • Decision process + decision criteria discovery
    • Mutual action plans tied to critical events
    • Security/procurement readiness support (templates, FAQs, talk tracks)
    • Negotiation discipline (“trade, don’t discount”)
  • Tailor enablement by segment/motion while keeping the system simple.

AI‑forward enablement engine

  • Use AI to accelerate enablement creation, iteration, and delivery (e.g., turning top call transcripts into draft playbooks, talk tracks, onboarding modules).
  • Build a repeatable workflow: synthesize → curate → QA → publish → reinforce.
  • Operate responsibly with customer/prospect data (approved tools and safeguards).

Revenue Operations support

You will directly contribute to making our GTM process real in the CRM and in weekly execution:

  • Partner with RevOps to operationalize and drive adoption of:
    • Stage definitions and exit criteria
    • Required fields/standards that support SPICED consistency and forecasting hygiene
    • Pipeline/deal inspection rhythms (clean, lightweight, consistent)
    • Handoff standards and operational follow‑through (Sales → Implementation → CS)
  • Translate process changes into training, reinforcement, and measurable adoption—without adding unnecessary friction.
  • Support enablement for Sales→Implementation→CS continuity where it improves outcomes (handoff quality, expectation‑setting, value framing, renewal readiness inputs).
  • High‑ownership operating model in a lean team.
  • Comfortably flex into adjacent needs when required (enablement ops, rollout/change management, documentation, special projects) while staying anchored to enablement outcomes.

Early priorities (first ~90 days)

  • Accelerate ramp for new BDRs/AEs/SEs through clearer readiness standards, coaching cadence, and practical certifications.
  • Ship a small set of high‑usage, stage‑based assets that improve seller efficiency fast.
  • Standardize SPICED usage across GTM (and align MEDDPICCR for complex enterprise deals).
  • Tighten core sales operations adoption in HubSpot (stages/fields/handoffs/inspection), in partnership with RevOps.
  • Establish lightweight measurement for enablement impact (ramp and execution signals).

What We’re Looking For

Must-haves

  • Experience enabling enterprise/complex sales cycles (multi‑stakeholder deals, mutual action plans, decision process/criteria, and security/procurement workflows).
  • Proven ability to improve time‑to‑productivity through onboarding, certifications, coaching, and behavior change.
  • Strong data fluency (can diagnose performance gaps, prioritize, and measure impact).
  • AI‑forward operator (uses AI to accelerate output with strong QA discipline).
  • Comfortable owning enablement and partnering deeply on Revenue Operations (process adoption, CRM reinforcement, inspection rhythms).

Healthie powers virtual‑first care delivery while improving access to healthcare and enabling better healthcare outcomes through technology.

Leveraging Healthie, our customers deliver care to millions of patients, across the full spectrum of healthcare services—from preventative health and wellness to complex chronic care management. We believe that the future of healthcare delivery is virtual‑first, longitudinal, and collaborative.

Revenue Operations is a core strategic function at Healthie. The role is focused on building the revenue engine that enables us to scale efficiently, predictably, and intelligently. As we scale toward $100MM+ in ARR, our operating model depends on best‑in‑class revenue infrastructure, rigorous data discipline, and systems that enable speed without breaking trust.

We’re hiring a Director of Revenue Operations to own and evolve Healthie’s end‑to‑end revenue systems, analytics, and operating cadence. This leader will be responsible for creating a true single source of truth across our go‑to‑market tech stack, enabling Sales, Business Development, Customer Management, Customer Support, Marketing, Finance, and Product to operate off shared data, shared definitions, and shared incentives. This includes clear ownership of revenue data models, forecasting methodology, GTM tooling, and operating rhythms, in close partnership with GTM teams, Finance, and Product.

This is a hands‑on leadership role for someone who has built RevOps functions through scale, thrives in ambiguity, and can balance near‑term execution with long‑term architectural thinking. You will inherit and scale a strong RevOps foundation, including a team of three. This role is not starting from zero – it is about leveling up the system, the team, and the operating rigor required for $100MM+ ARR.

In the near term, this role will focus on scaling forecasting accuracy, standardizing revenue and usage definitions, enabling CX teams with leading indicators, and supporting new product launches with clean, scalable RevOps infrastructure.

You will report to the Senior Director of Growth & Operations (who focuses on strategic planning and cross‑functional alignment) and work closely with Finance, Product, Growth (BD, Sales, PP Growth, CX, Marketing), and Engineering.

Analytics, Forecasting & Insight

  • Build and maintain executive‑level dashboards for pipeline, growth, churn, and efficiency metrics
  • Surface insights that drive better decisions, not just more charts
  • Answer questions like “where is growth actually coming from?” and “what breaks at $100MM ARR?”

Quote‑to‑Cash, Expansion & Customer Lifecycle

  • Own the full quote‑to‑cash process across PLG, sales‑assisted, and enterprise deals
  • Partner deeply with Finance on pricing, discounting, revenue recognition inputs, and forecasting
  • Build expansion, renewals, churn, and customer success workflows natively in Salesforce
  • Design and maintain custom objects for subscriptions, add‑ons, usage, expansion events, and lifecycle milestones
  • Ensure Product usage data meaningfully informs CS, expansion, and GTM decision‑making
  • Pull data directly from Salesforce, Stripe, and analytics tools into Excel and Google Sheets
  • Build models for forecasting, pricing scenarios, territory design, and GTM efficiency
  • Translate messy system data into clear narratives for executives
  • Operate comfortably in spreadsheets, SQL‑adjacent thinking, and BI layers
  • Lead and develop a growing RevOps team (systems, analytics, enablement)
  • Set clear ownership, operating rhythms, and quality bars
  • Build playbooks that reduce heroics and increase leverage
  • Be a calm, trusted partner to GTM leaders during periods of change

  • 30% – Cross‑Functional Collaboration & Architecture Design: GTM tech stack build, systems roadmap, growth modeling

  • Our Quote‑to‑Cash system is clean across SFDC and PandaDoc
  • Handoffs between teams are clean and no information is dropped

This role uniquely combines strategic leadership with hands‑on operational excellence.   • Serve as the strategic thought partner to the CRO and executive leadership team, providing data‑driven insights, scenario modeling, and operational recommendations that inform strategic decisions on market expansion, product prioritization, and go‑to‑market investments

  • Proven track record building and scaling revenue operations functions in high‑growth B2B technology companies, ideally with experience supporting organizations generating $500M+ in annual revenue
  • Demonstrated success implementing and optimizing enterprise CRM platforms (Salesforce expertise required), revenue intelligence tools, sales engagement platforms, and revenue analytics solutions at scale
  • Deep expertise in sales forecasting methodologies, pipeline management frameworks, revenue recognition principles, and financial planning processes that drive accurate revenue predictability

  • Strong background in data analytics, business intelligence, and revenue reporting, with ability to translate complex data into actionable insights and executive‑ready presentations

We are seeking an experienced Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) to lead and scale all revenue-generating functions across sales, channels, partnerships, marketing alignment, and customer lifecycle performance. Revenue Strategy & Growth

Sales, Partnerships & Channels

Updated: Nov 20, 2024 - The Chief Revenue Officer is tasked with blending traditional philanthropic fundraising techniques with innovative strategies from the corporate and startup sectors, fostering a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization to achieve set revenue targets. This role involves reimagining fundraising events to connect with younger, diverse audiences and enhance awareness about the importance of quality journalism, managing a major donor portfolio, and overseeing data management with tools like Salesforce. Additionally, the officer explores new content delivery methods in journalism and collaborates with various organizations to create joint funding opportunities while also enhancing marketing materials to better convey the organization's value proposition.

A Review of Professional Skills and Functions for Chief Revenue Officer

1. Chief Revenue Officer Duties

  • Liquidity Management: Manage relationships with liquidity providers in the digital asset space.
  • Liquidity Provisioning: Manage liquidity provisioning for the exchange.
  • Product Development: Build complex products consisting of digital assets (Stablecoins/Cryptocurrencies/Tokenized Commodities).
  • Structured Product Experience: Experience in structured products, indices, creating and marketing investment products.
  • Revenue Strategy: Experience creating and executing on revenue models, GTM strategy, own the process.
  • Global Sales Management: Manage global relationships, revenue pipeline, and sales team leadership.
  • OTC Trading Leadership: Manage OTC trading desk and widely viewed as a strong developer of others.
  • Sales Analysis: Develop matrices for analyzing sales performance and regularly measure and analyze productivity and effectiveness of sales efforts.
  • Product Strategy: Setting direction for product road map and pricing strategies, understanding and creating market positioning and competitive advantages, and determining budget trade-offs to continually improve and develop sustainable results.
  • Team Leadership: Hire, train, and retain a highly skilled, diverse, and effective team.
  • Financial Oversight: Own the PandL and ensure that the organization and its leaders are delivering 'investable plans' for each planning cycle (short, mid, and long-term).
  • Fundraising Leadership: Act as a lead fundraiser, securing capital from multiple sources (e.g., corporations, foundations, social good investors, private markets).
  • Strategic Planning and Forecasting: Create a sustainable strategy for future growth and deliver accurate revenue projections that include year-over-year growth.
  • Revenue Strategy Development: Build a cohesive short, medium, and long-term revenue strategy for the CAVO platform that encompasses and aligns the Marketing, Sales, and Client Experience teams.
  • Goal and Metric Setting: Set top-down goals and metrics based on both internal goals and market opportunities.
  • Sales Process Optimization: Create a strategy to implement predictable, repeatable, and scalable sales processes using data analytics, and manage a consistent pipeline and forecasting methodology.
  • Market Strategy Partnership: Partner with product and development teams to develop the Company’s go-to-market strategy for each Line of Business (LOB) across all LOBs and markets including payers and providers.
  • Value Proposition Development: Continuously develop and refine value propositions and differentiated positioning.
  • Team Building and Training: Fill management gaps by building and training individuals and teams in Marketing, Sales, and Client Experience.
  • Market Opportunity Analysis: Determine if there are additional market opportunities outside of existing channels.
  • Marketing Strategy Formulation: Marketing strategy across payer and provider for existing and new product lines.
  • Solution Integration Strategy: Strategically tie all of the Company’s offerings to a comprehensive solution and message.
  • Enterprise Sales Closure: Ability to close enterprise deals within and across payers and providers.
  • Strategic Partnership Development: Determine and close strategic partnership opportunities.
  • Channel Partnership Leadership: Lead and establish channel partnerships including Government markets.

3. Chief Revenue Officer Responsibilities

  • Revenue Evaluation: Evaluate revenue opportunities in the renewable energy sector across multiple product lines and geographic markets from initial review until close, focusing on a high level of customer satisfaction.
  • Revenue Pipeline Management: Drive the entire revenue pipeline through effective strategic planning and execution, inclusive of defining markets, setting processes for developing potential customer leads, effectively articulating the Brightcore value proposition, training and equipping staff with the required knowledge to focus on priority business, and converting opportunities into revenue.
  • Resource Deployment: Effectively deploy resources across the revenue team in an organized, efficient manner that drives growth and provides scalability through process and training.
  • Team Development: Grow and develop the size and capacity of the business development team by defining roles and responsibilities.
  • Performance Culture Driving: Drive a performance-based culture through the definition of, measurement of, and accountability of key performance indicators.
  • Customer Development Balance: Effectively balance a long-term, customer development perspective while also striving to drive quarterly revenue results.
  • Sales Methodology Execution: Identify, develop, and execute sales methodologies and ingrain culture across the revenue team.
  • Offering Definition: Work with leadership and the product teams to define offerings based on identified customer needs.
  • Marketing Leadership: Lead the marketing team to help create leads and generate pipeline opportunities for the business development team.
  • Marketing Strategy Refinement: Determine and refine a marketing strategy across all marketing channels.
  • Relationship Management: Ensure relationships with the appropriate decision-makers for both clients and prospects.
  • Company Representation: Represent the Company in media and marketing events.

4. Chief Revenue Officer Job Summary

  • Commercial Transformation: Full autonomy to transform the commercial landscape of the company
  • Sales Process Introduction: Introduce sales processes and sales science to a performing sales team
  • Strategy Collaboration: Collaborate with COO and CEO to define commercial strategy
  • Marketing Leadership: Inherit marketing function and introduce digital marketing
  • Sales Leadership: Lead from the front on substantial sales execution
  • Strategy Development: Introduce sales strategy and people strategy including account management and new business sales
  • Talent Management: Hiring and ramping up new salespeople taking into account the velocity of company growth and revenue goals
  • Sales Monitoring: Keeping track of and exceeding sales quota
  • Cycle Management: Keeping the average sales cycle under control and working with the sales team to shorten it
  • Revenue Enhancement: Work with the sales team to increase the average revenue per account
  • Lead Acceleration: Work with the marketing team to increase the lead velocity rate
  • Revenue Retention: Work with the customer success team to increase annual net revenue retention
  • Brand Management: Establish and maintain brand touchpoints including website and social media channels

5. Chief Revenue Officer Accountabilities

  • Develop Business Plans: Work with leadership to develop the annual business plan and growth targets.
  • Strategic Development: Develop both short-term results and long-term growth strategy.
  • Organizational Growth: Build and grow the sales organization.
  • Process Implementation: Develop and implement sales management processes - pipeline, account planning, materials, and proposals.
  • Revenue Maximization: Identify and maximize multiple revenue channels.
  • Technology Implementation: Identify and implement new revenue-generating technologies.
  • Performance Accountability: Create accountability within the company by developing appropriate metrics and performance expectations for their team.
  • Financial Achievement: Meet and exceed financial goals.
  • Industry Knowledge: Understand and keep up to date with industry and competitive landscape knowledge.
  • Compensation Strategy: Work with the CEO to continuously review and revise performance compensation programs to reward the right behaviors and the achievement of Imagine’s and the client’s desired outcomes.
  • Cultural Integration: Effectively marry the cultures of Imagine and add-on acquisitions, drawing from the best elements of each.
  • Product Collaboration: Partner with the product teams to define differentiated offerings and positioning.
  • Culture Promotion: Build on Imagine’s unique legacy by always promoting a culture of growth, collaboration, leading-edge client engagements, and meritocracy throughout the organization.

6. Chief Revenue Officer Functions

  • Traditional and Innovative Fundraising: Embracing traditional philanthropic fundraising methods while also leveraging best practices and innovative strategies from the corporate world and startup sector.
  • Rethinking Fundraising Events: Rethinking events and traditional fundraising approaches (for example, inewsource has had prior success with small, highly targeted gatherings of influencers in nontraditional settings).
  • Audience Engagement: Connecting inewsource with younger and more diverse audiences and building awareness as to the critical need for good journalism now and into the future.
  • Industry Scanning: Constantly scanning the journalism landscape for new ideas and use of tools to emulate in delivering content in broadcasting or on the internet.
  • Innovative Asset Utilization: Thinking creatively about inewsource’s assets and capabilities to pilot new and innovative ways to translate those into revenue as well as trading/in-kind for other resources.
  • Partnership Development: Partnering with other organizations (including other nonprofit entities) to develop joint funding and sponsorship opportunities.
  • Cultural Philanthropy: Instilling a culture of philanthropy that spans across the organization and board, assisting every team member to support revenue goals however they can.
  • Revenue Target Management: Setting appropriate short and long-term revenue targets and taking responsibility for achieving those goals.
  • Donor Portfolio Management: Managing a personal portfolio of major donors and prospects.
  • Data Management Oversight: Overseeing data management efforts in Salesforce, providing reports and updates to the CEO, Board, and staff.
  • Marketing Improvement Recommendations: Making recommendations on ways to improve customer pitch and marketing materials to showcase Imagine’s value proposition and competitive positioning, potentially including case studies, website enhancements, email marketing campaigns, etc.

7. Chief Revenue Officer Job Description

  • Scale Development: Scale and multiply the development function of the organization to increase the impact of its work.
  • Lead Fundraising Management: Lead the strategic direction and overall management of the organization's fundraising and revenue-generating operations across a range of funding sources, including government partners.
  • Executive Leadership Collaboration: Serve on Code for America's executive leadership team (CXO), collaborating with the CEO and other senior leaders to help drive the organization's vision, strategy, and cultural development.
  • Develop Funding Strategies: Partner with the CEO and other senior leaders to develop funding strategies that shape and fuel the organization's existing and new initiatives.
  • Enhance Organization Visibility: Serve as an external face of the organization, in collaboration with the CEO and other team members, to enhance Code for America's revenue generation, impact, visibility, brand recognition, and credibility.
  • Liaison to the Board: Act as a liaison to the Board, presenting key development updates and ensuring that the Board has the information necessary to meet its fiduciary responsibilities.
  • Culture Building: Serve as a culture builder and carrier for the organization.
  • Drive Revenue Strategies: Drive fundraising and revenue strategies that lead to organizational sustainability and growth, ensuring the engagement of Code for America's existing donor base.
  • Cultivate Supporters: Cultivate new supporters among government, corporate, foundation, and individual funding communities, with an emphasis on securing unrestricted support where possible.
  • Fund Programs: Fund new and ongoing programs, such as Clear My Record, GetCalFresh, GetYourRefund, and Code for America's Brigade Network.
  • Execute Campaigns: Assess and execute the organization or program-wide campaigns.
  • Manage Resource Allocation: Manage resource spending and allocation, operating within the approved budget, ensuring maximum resource utilization, and maintaining a positive financial position.

8. Chief Revenue Officer Overview

  • Major Gifts Program Development: Develop and support the implementation of a major gifts program to secure new funders while continuing to support and cultivate the existing donor network.
  • Fundraising Systems Maintenance: Oversee the maintenance and improvement of fundraising systems and processes to ensure the organization's donors are properly stewarded and reporting is timely and accurate.
  • Board Collaboration: Work closely with Board members to leverage their networks and relationships to meet revenue goals.
  • Process and Standards Creation: Collaboratively approach to create processes and standards that support the Code for America's fundraising.
  • Gift Acceptance Policy Integration: Assure that Code for America's gift acceptance policy is integrated into donor identification, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Team Hiring and Mentoring: Hire, retain, and mentor a high-performing, diverse development team with a commitment to strong staff engagement, equity, and inclusivity.
  • Performance-Based Culture Leadership: Track record of leading a performance-based culture that motivates employees to excellence and promotes accountability.
  • Staff Management and Motivation: Manage and motivate staff to achieve annual fundraising and revenue goals, holding team members to a high standard of excellence and accountability.
  • Team Development and Mentoring: Develop and mentor individual team members to ensure individuals are achieving impact for Code for America and developing as professionals.
  • Marketing to Sales Conversion: Be responsible for ensuring that marketing activations are converted into sales.
  • Data Analysis for Strategic Decisions: Seek and analyze data from a variety of sources to support decisions and align others with the organization's overall strategy and take smart risks.
  • Talent Recruitment and Management: Attract and recruit top talent, motivate the team, delegate effectively, celebrate diversity within the team, and manage performance.

9. Chief Revenue Officer Details and Accountabilities

  • Value Proposition Establishment: Establish and qualify Oakland Roots SC’s value proposition to sponsors and ensure consistency in messaging across all partner interaction.
  • New Business Acquisition: Identify, pursue, and close new business from qualified prospects for partnerships.
  • Sales Strategy Development: Establish and implement sales and new business development strategies, including the use of social media and other platforms, to develop leads and close sales with partners, ranging from the local level up to Fortune 500 companies.
  • Market Definition: Define the value proposition and market to “C-Level” executives.
  • Creative Pitching: Creatively conceptualize and pitch customized and unique activation programs to prospective partners to show value-added elements of sponsorship deals with the Oakland Roots SC, including connecting the Root's purpose to its partner relationships.
  • Data Analytics Interpretation: Interpret data analytics to best guide sales pitches and partner benefits.
  • Contract Negotiation Leadership: Lead and/or provide direction for contract negotiations.
  • Strategic Sales Leadership: Serve as a leader of the sales and new business development department to provide strategic vision for the Oakland Roots SC sales operation, ensuring revenue growth is aligned with company objectives and values.
  • Sales Team Management: Lead the recruiting, hiring, training, and day-to-day management of the new stadium sales team consisting of sales professionals.
  • Sales Event Design: Design the calendar, content, and strategy for recurring sales events - including ideas like friends and family, top businesses, local youth clubs, local tastemakers, and influencer events.

10. Chief Revenue Officer Roles

  • Sales Strategy Development: Develop the sales journey, purchase process, CRM tracking, and sales-to-service hand-off strategy for club, membership, and supporters section seating.
  • Sales Leadership: Lead the planning and implementation of all outbound sales efforts, including experience center appointments, product launches, sales events, seller incentives, and buyer incentives, for all membership-focused products.
  • Sales Reporting: Provide consistent reporting information by maintaining accurate daily, weekly, and overall updates of sales, outbound metrics, and event recaps.
  • Toolset Optimization: Establish the right mix of toolsets and apps to ensure success within the sales and sponsorship departments.
  • Performance Management: Set clear success metrics and hold others accountable for achieving their goals.
  • Market Awareness: Stay current on events at the local, state, and national levels.
  • Strategic Revenue Planning: Work with the CEO and Board to develop and implement a multi-year revenue strategy that includes the growth of major donors, foundation support, and membership programs.
  • Team Leadership: Take the lead in hiring the revenue team, which will grow from 2 to 7 members over the next two years, while providing strong leadership and effective management for the team.
  • Industry Advancement: Advance the field of nonprofit journalism and grow inewsource’s reach through collaboration with local organizations as well as state and national entities.
  • Stakeholder Management: Balance a multitude of, and sometimes conflicting, viewpoints while always keeping journalistic integrity and the best interests of the organization at the forefront.
  • Coaching and Development: Coach, mentor, and develop team members to their highest potential.
  • Sales Team Leadership: Lead the sales team in helping define success in ticketing and guest services.

Chief Revenue Officer (University of Miami)

Get AI-powered advice on this job and more exclusive features.

LEGENDS GLOBAL x UNIVERSITY OF MIAMI

The University of Miami and Legends Global began a formal marketing-partnership relationship in April 2021 and expanded that relationship into a comprehensive, first-of-its-kind arrangement covering nearly all Hurricane revenue streams in December 2023. The expanded deal places Legends in a central role driving revenue strategy and execution for UM athletics, creating a dedicated team led by the Chief Revenue Officer, Hurricanes Sales & Partnerships.

THE ROLE

The Chief Revenue Officer serves as the strategic and operational leader responsible for driving all revenue-generating activities for the University of Miami Athletics under the Legends Global partnership model. This individual will be a senior executive on the University’s leadership team, serving as a key advisor to the Director of Athletics, and will provide visionary leadership to maximize and diversify revenue streams, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders of the University. The Chief Revenue Officer will report to key leaders at Legends Global and the University.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute an integrated commercial strategy across all athletics revenue-producing business verticals with the objective of increasing annual revenue
  • Oversee the partnerships team assisting with sales identification, closing negotiations and activation efforts to grow high-level corporate relationships and sponsorship revenue
  • Oversee ticketing, premium seating and hospitality programs including pricing and yield optimization
  • Direct all merchandise efforts including product development, pricing strategies, management of inventory levels, and competitive positioning of merchandise
  • Work with Athletic Department and campus leadership to add to and enhance revenue generating opportunities for the Legends Global team.
  • Work with Canes Connection (the official NIL Collective of Miami Hurricane Athletics) to assist Hurricane athletes in cultivating and securing name, image and likeness opportunities
  • Serve as a key senior advisor to the Director of Athletics on revenue generation, marketing, digital and fan engagement tactics to enhance brand value and audience growth
  • Collaborate with University advancement to align fundraising and donor engagement initiatives
  • Implement analytics-driven decision making across all revenue verticals to demonstrate returns on investment across ticketing, partnerships and marketing functions
  • Moderate all budget management including profit-and-loss reporting and revenue forecasts to maintain EBITDA budget and provide clear, actionable financial insights to inform strategy and decision-making for the Athletics Department
  • Recruit, develop and mentor a high-performing cross-functional commercial team
  • Represent the University sports property, the University, and Legends Global in a professional manner
  • Ensure all revenue-generating activities and operations comply with local, state, and federal laws, as well as all NCAA and conference rules and regulations
  • Build strong understanding of all University and Legends Global business units and offerings in order to leverage new business areas, leads, and categories
  • Other job-related duties as assigned

Supervisory Responsibilities

Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with all Legends Global policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Sports Management, Marketing, Communications, or a related field required
  • 15+ years of senior-level experience in revenue generation, sponsorship sales, or marketing within collegiate athletics, professional sports, media, or a related industry
  • Proven success overseeing complex, multi-line P&L or annual revenue portfolios exceeding $25 million
  • Expertise in sponsorship negotiation, premium sales, ticketing, and partner activation, merchandise and venue management business
  • Experience collaborating within university or multi-stakeholder environments
  • Strong understanding of marketing, CRM, and data analytics tools used in sports business
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and grow high-performing teams
  • Experience collaborating with university administration, athletic departments, rights holders, and external agencies

Leadership Competencies

  • Strategic Integrator – aligns diverse business units under a cohesive growth strategy.
  • Relationship Builder – fosters trust across university, corporate, and community partners.
  • Innovator – drives new revenue models through creative partnerships and digital engagement.
  • Analytical Decision Maker – leverages data insights to guide pricing, packaging, and sales performance.
  • Mission-Aligned Leader – balances commercial objectives with institutional integrity and fan experience.
  • Executive Presence – represents Legends and the University of Miami confidently and collaboratively.

Success Metrics

  • Year-over-year growth in total athletics revenue.
  • Corporate partner satisfaction and renewal rates.
  • Ticket yield, attendance, and donor engagement improvement.
  • Brand health and fan engagement across digital and in-venue channels.
  • Effective integration of Legends’ analytics, CRM, and marketing technologies.

Compensation

OptiSigns is a fast-growing B2B SaaS company in digital signage and digital experiences. Our platform combines AI, IoT, and no-code tools to help organizations engage customers and employees through screen-based experiences that drive measurable business outcomes.

The opportunity is to connect them — using product and customer signals to identify high-potential accounts, convert them efficiently, and expand them over time.

We are also building an AI-first, AI-native organization. Our engineering team already works this way: AI handles research, drafting, testing, and repetitive execution while people own judgment and final verification. Revenue is next.

  • Build and lead the global revenue strategy across new business, expansion, retention, partnerships, and revenue operations.

  • Build an AI-first, AI-native revenue organization where AI agents handle research, prospecting support, drafting, analysis, and repetitive workflows while people focus on judgment, relationships, and closing.

  • Strong hands-on understanding of RevOps, pipeline management, forecasting, and attribution.
  • Experience building partnerships, channel, or reseller programs.
  • International experience across multiple markets.
  • AI-first and AI-native mindset — you actively use AI in your own work and know how to redesign revenue workflows around it.
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment and getting directly involved when needed.
  • Experience scaling a SaaS business through and beyond $100M ARR is highly preferred.

You will inherit a substantial global customer base, proven product-market fit, and meaningful inbound demand. The mandate is to turn those advantages into a more predictable, scalable revenue system.

OptiSigns is on a strong growth trajectory toward $100M ARR. This role is about building the scalable, predictable, AI-native revenue engine that takes us through $100M ARR and well beyond it.

The CRO must balance near-term revenue delivery with the continuous creation of future backlog. Operating Context Microvast operates in markets characterized by long qualification cycles, complex technical requirements, multi-year automotive programs, large capital commitments and significant warranty exposure. The CRO must prevent short-term sales activity from displacing early business development and must ensure that commercial commitments are executable by Engineering, Operations and Supply Chain.Key Responsibilities1. Revenue Strategy and Executive Leadership Develop and execute the global revenue strategy aligned with Microvast's corporate plan, product roadmap, manufacturing footprint, capacity and profitability objectives. Backlog Creation and Revenue Balance Maintain three separately managed revenue horizons: strategic BD pipeline, qualified sales pipeline and contracted backlog. Establish required pipeline and backlog coverage using Microvast's historical win rates, program delays and cancellation experience. Lead corrective action when future pipeline, bookings, backlog quality or backlog conversion falls below plan. 3. Global Business Development Direct the identification of new markets, applications, customers, partners and strategic programs 12 to 36 months or more ahead. Ensure BD builds senior customer access, develops opportunities before RFQ and produces a continuous flow of commercially qualified opportunities. Approve clear qualification and handoff standards between BD and Sales. A qualified pre-RFQ opportunity is the preferred handoff; an RFQ or formal pricing request is the mandatory handoff. Prevent BD resources from being routinely absorbed by active sales execution without CRO approval. 4. Global Sales and Commercial Closing Lead the conversion of qualified opportunities into profitable, bankable and executable contracts and purchase orders. Govern opportunity strategy, quotations, pricing, negotiations, contracting, capacity commitments, payment terms and sales forecasting. Require cross-functional validation of technical scope, quality requirements, delivery schedules, warranty exposure and manufacturing feasibility before binding commitments are made. Treat paid pilots, sample orders, prototype orders and trial orders requiring a formal quotation or purchase order as Sales-owned commercial opportunities, except where a named OEM opportunity owner is formally assigned. 5. Strategic OEM Management Designate named strategic automotive OEM accounts and establish a single accountable account owner for each. Oversee backlog conversion, customer releases, long-range forecasts, pricing changes, cost recovery, program profitability and executive relationships. Drive incremental bookings from new platforms, applications, geographic divisions, extensions and volume increases within existing OEM accounts. Escalate volume reductions, sourcing changes, launch delays, cancellations and other threats to backlog or profitability. 6. Global Services and Customer Satisfaction Own the global warranty-service and customer-satisfaction strategy, including response standards, escalation paths and service coverage. Ensure rapid containment, root-cause coordination and closure of field issues with Quality, Engineering, Operations and suppliers. Use field data and customer feedback to improve reliability, product design and manufacturing performance. Develop appropriate lifecycle-service revenue, including extended warranties, maintenance, training, monitoring and upgrades. 7. Product Marketing and Brand Direct product positioning, customer value propositions, market intelligence, competitive analysis and product-launch messaging. Ensure technical features are translated into credible customer benefits supported by validated evidence. Align product marketing, corporate branding, trade shows, sales enablement and thought leadership with revenue priorities. Create a structured feedback loop from customers and markets to Product Management, Engineering and R&D. 8. Commercial Governance and Risk Implement the operating rule of one Account Owner, one Opportunity Owner and one official forecast for every customer opportunity. Establish pricing authority, deal-review gates, contract-approval limits, CRM standards and handoff procedures. Prevent duplicate bookings, conflicting customer commitments and uncontrolled commercial, warranty, credit or capacity exposure. Partner with Finance and Legal on revenue quality, payment security, credit risk, receivables escalation, contract terms and revenue-recognition considerations. 9. Organization and Cross-Functional Execution Build, lead and develop a high-performing global revenue organization with clear roles, succession plans and performance standards. Coordinate with Product Management, Engineering, Program Management, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance and Legal. Resolve ownership conflicts between BD, Sales, OEM Management and Services promptly and document the decision in CRM. Promote a customer-focused culture grounded in integrity, execution discipline, fact-based forecasting and long-term value creation. Decision Rights and Commercial Ownership Revenue stage Primary owner CRO governance New-market access and early opportunity development VP Global Business Development Protect future-backlog creation and approve handoff criteria. Qualified opportunity, RFQ, formal quotation and closing VP Global Sales Approve material pricing, risk and capacity commitments. Named strategic OEM account and multi-year backlog VP OEM Management Confirm account ownership and resolve cross-functional conflicts. Warranty execution and paid lifecycle services VP Global Services Set customer-satisfaction and cost standards. Positioning, market intelligence and sales enablement Director Product Marketing Align messaging and investment with revenue priorities.Required QualificationsEducation Bachelor's degree in engineering, business, finance, marketing or a related discipline required; MBA or other relevant advanced degree preferred. Experience Fifteen or more years of progressive global commercial leadership experience, including substantial responsibility for revenue, business development, sales or strategic accounts. At least five years in a senior executive or enterprise commercial leadership role with responsibility across multiple regions or business lines. Demonstrated success creating pipeline, winning large multi-year programs and converting backlog into profitable revenue. Meaningful experience in batteries, automotive OEMs, energy storage, commercial vehicles, industrial technology or another technically complex manufacturing sector strongly preferred. Experience negotiating complex global contracts involving pricing, capacity, warranty, quality, localization, intellectual property, payment security and long-term supply commitments. Business and Technical Knowledge Strong understanding of long-cycle B2B and OEM selling, sourcing processes, RFQ management, product qualification and program launches. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

About Smartsheet

Smartsheet is a leading enterprise platform for dynamic work, empowering organizations to plan, execute, and report on work at scale. Backed by multiple private equity firms, Smartsheet operates with the rigor, discipline, and growth orientation of a world-class PE‑backed SaaS company. We are at a pivotal moment — accelerating our AI capabilities, evolving our operating model, and building the organizational infrastructure to scale intelligently.

The Opportunity

Smartsheet is in the midst of a significant transformation. The company’s AI roadmap is fundamentally changing what our platform can do — and the pace of that innovation is accelerating. The opportunity in front of us is clear. The challenge is execution: how do we ensure that our revenue organization can lead the transition?

As Sr. Director, Revenue Enablement, you will own that answer. This role is built around the need to deliver learning and enablement that keeps pace with our roadmap, and aligns every member of the GTM to key principles in value selling, customer value and AI solutions expertise. You will design and operate the systems, programs, and tools that make that happen.

This role reports directly to the CMO and sits at the intersection of sales productivity, AI adoption, and commercial execution. It requires someone who combines the rigor of a data‑driven operator with the creativity of a learning designer and the credibility to influence senior GTM leaders.

The right candidate thrives in a high‑velocity, PE‑backed environment where speed, measurability, and ROI are non‑negotiable. You are here to build an enablement machine.

What You Will Own

Enablement Velocity & AI-Driven Sales Motion

  • Design and operate a modern, AI‑augmented enablement system that dramatically compresses time‑to‑productivity for new hires and time‑to‑adoption for new product capabilities.

  • Establish a repeatable motion for enabling the field on AI product releases: from launch readiness to certified competency, with measurable adoption milestones.
  • Define and own the success metrics that connect enablement activity to revenue outcomes — ramp time, win rates, pipeline conversion, expansion rates, and forecast accuracy.

Field Readiness & Product Marketing Partnership

Coaching, Methodology & Execution Discipline

  • Define and continuously evolve the enterprise B2B selling competencies required to win in Smartsheet’s market — including AI fluency as a core selling skill.
  • Drive consistent execution of sales methodology, deal rigor, and pipeline hygiene through both programming and data‑driven inspection.

Content, Tools & Technology

  • Own the enablement content ecosystem: messaging frameworks, playbooks, competitive battlecards, training assets, and partner materials.

How You Will Drive Business Value

The Sr. Director, Revenue Enablement is accountable for delivering measurable impact on commercial performance — not just managing programs. The expectation is that this role produces outcomes that are visible to the CMO, CRO, and the board:

  • Faster time‑to‑productivity: Reduce ramp time for new AEs and CSMs through structured onboarding and role‑based learning programs that are AI‑assisted and continuously optimized
  • Accelerated AI feature adoption: Shrink the lag between AI product releases and field readiness — ensuring sellers can demo, position, and sell new capabilities within weeks of launch, not quarters
  • Higher win rates and deal quality: Drive consistent application of sales methodology and competitive positioning, translating enablement investment into measurable improvement in conversion and deal size
  • Enablement ROI visibility: Build the reporting infrastructure that connects program activity to commercial outcomes, providing the CMO and CRO with clear, data‑driven insight into what is working and what to invest in next

Job Description

Join the Microvast Team (NASDAQ: MVST), a technology innovator that designs, develops and manufactures lithium-ion battery solutions. By integrating the process from raw material to system assembly, Microvast has developed a family of products covering a broad breadth of market applications. More information can be found on the corporate website: www.microvast.com

Job Description

The Revenue Operations Coordinator enables the Chief Revenue Officer and the global revenue organization to operate with discipline, speed and accurate information. The position combines executive assistance, meeting and calendar administration, cross-functional business coordination, CRM data discipline, ERP transaction follow-up, reporting support and action tracking.

Responsibilities

CRO Office and Executive Support

  • Manage the CRO's calendar, priorities, meeting requests and scheduling across global time zones, balancing customer, executive, operating and travel commitments.
  • Prepare daily and weekly priority summaries, decision lists, briefing materials and follow-up reminders for the CRO.
  • Screen and route requests to the appropriate revenue leader or cross-functional owner; elevate urgent customer, backlog, service, cash or delivery risks promptly.
  • Coordinate business travel, itineraries, customer visits, internal events and related administrative logistics.
  • Handle confidential commercial, employee, customer and executive information with discretion and sound judgment.

Revenue Organization Coordination

  • Coordinate work among Global Business Development, Global Sales, OEM Management, Global Services and Product Marketing and with Product Management, Engineering, Program Management, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance and Legal.
  • Maintain the master revenue calendar for opportunity reviews, BD reviews, OEM/backlog reviews, service reviews, forecast cycles and strategic planning meetings.
  • Track cross-functional dependencies, decisions, owners, due dates and unresolved issues through closure.
  • Support the handover process between BD and Sales and later transfers to OEM/backlog governance and Services, confirming that required documents and acceptance records are complete.
  • Help prevent responsibilities from being forgotten when teams are busy by maintaining visible action lists, aging reports and escalation reminders.

CRM Administration and Data Discipline

  • Be a proficient daily user of the company CRM and support consistent entry of accounts, contacts, opportunities, activities, handovers, stages, forecast categories, next actions and controlled-document links.
  • Review CRM records for completeness, duplicate accounts or opportunities, missing owners, stale next actions, overdue handovers and inconsistent stages; route corrections to the accountable owner.
  • Prepare CRM-based meeting reports, dashboards and exception lists for the CRO and functional leaders.
  • Support user training, field definitions, controlled lists and adoption of the rule: one Account Owner, one Opportunity Owner and one official forecast.
  • Coordinate with Revenue Operations or system administrators on workflow, access, reporting and data-quality issues; do not independently change system controls or ownership rules.

ERP, Order and Backlog Coordination

  • Understand the ERP order-to-cash flow sufficiently to follow customer-master requests, quotations, approved purchase orders/contracts, sales orders, backlog, order changes, deliveries, invoices and payment status.
  • Confirm that ERP order-entry requests contain the originating CRM Opportunity ID, approved customer and product information, required commercial approvals and controlled source documents.
  • Support reconciliation of CRM closed-won opportunities with ERP orders and backlog; identify missing links, unmatched records and possible double counting for responsible teams to correct.
  • Maintain follow-up lists for pending customer master approvals, order entry, backlog changes, delivery risks, invoicing and other CRO-level exceptions.
  • Coordinate information and follow-up but do not approve customers, prices, contracts, credit, backlog eligibility, accounting treatment or ERP transactions unless separately authorized.

Meetings, Minutes and Action Management

  • Develop agendas with the CRO and meeting owner, gather pre-read materials, confirm required attendees and distribute materials in advance.
  • Attend assigned customer and internal meetings, take accurate minutes and document decisions, commitments, action owners, due dates, risks and items requiring escalation.
  • Issue concise minutes normally within one business day and maintain a searchable decision and action log.
  • Follow up with action owners before due dates, update status and escalate overdue or business-critical items according to the agreed process.
  • Maintain clear records of who made each decision; never convert discussion notes into an approval or customer commitment without confirmation from the authorized owner.

Reporting, Documents and Communications

  • Compile weekly and monthly revenue-office materials covering pipeline, RFQs, pilots, bookings, backlog, revenue, forecast, service issues, risks and required decisions using approved source data.
  • Prepare and format presentations, correspondence, reports, organizational materials, customer briefing books and other CRO communications.
  • Maintain controlled folders, naming conventions, current versions and links for meeting packs, handover documents, quotations, contracts and revenue reports.
  • Coordinate requested inputs from global teams, validate completeness and resolve obvious inconsistencies before materials reach the CRO.
  • Support special commercial and organizational projects assigned by the CRO, including research, implementation tracking and executive communications.

Required Qualifications

Education And Experience 

  • Bachelor's degree in business administration, operations, finance, marketing, communications or a related discipline preferred; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Five or more years of progressive experience in executive assistance, commercial coordination, sales operations, revenue operations, project coordination or a comparable role.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting a senior executive and coordinating work across multiple functions, locations and time zones.
  • Practical experience using CRM and ERP systems; experience with technically complex manufacturing, automotive OEMs, batteries, energy storage or industrial products is preferred.
  • Experience preparing management reports, meeting minutes, presentations, action trackers and confidential executive materials.

 Systems and Administrative Skills

  • Strong working proficiency with CRM platforms and the ability to understand accounts, contacts, opportunities, stages, forecasts, activities and handovers.
  • Working knowledge of ERP concepts including customer master, sales orders, backlog, order changes, delivery, billing and payment status.
  • Advanced skills in Microsoft Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Teams or comparable tools; comfortable learning dashboards and reporting applications.
  • Excellent scheduling, meeting planning, minute taking, document control, recordkeeping and travel coordination skills.
  • Ability to analyze data for completeness and inconsistency; capable of producing clear tables, trackers, summaries and executive-ready reports.

 Professional Competencies

  • Strong business judgment and enough commercial understanding to distinguish an early lead, qualified opportunity, RFQ, pilot order, binding award, backlog and revenue transaction.
  • Exceptional organization, attention to detail and follow-through while managing multiple priorities and urgent requests.
  • Concise written and verbal communication, professional English and confidence working with senior leaders and global teams; additional languages are beneficial.
  • Diplomatic persistence: able to request overdue information, challenge incomplete records and escalate appropriately without assuming another person's authority.
  • High integrity, discretion, reliability, cultural awareness and willingness to accommodate global meeting schedules and occasional business travel.

Annual salary + benefits
