Data is at the heart of everything we do: Xceptor has been designed around data manipulation in its broadest sense. We source data from wherever it flows. We curate, normalise, validate, repair, and enrich that data so it reaches its destination in a reliable and consistent format. Data coming out of Xceptor is data our clients can trust.

Our expertise

We are recognised as an expert in the Financial Services vertical, which strongly aligns with Business Users in Middle and Back-Office teams. We enable these users to solve their data challenges by themselves, rather than through a technology-led project.

Our mission

We empower business users within financial institutions to build automated processes that deliver trusted data.

Our values

  • Client Centric; we prioritise our Clients’ experience and needs.
  • One Team; we actively support one another to achieve our goals.
  • Impactful; we focus, we innovate, we make every minute matter.

Base Salary Range - $170,000 - $210,000 plus bonus

Your Role

We are seeking an experienced Director, Head of Product Operations & Enablement to act as a key strategic and operational partner to the Chief Product Officer (CPO). This role spans the full range from strategy to execution - helping shape where the Product organisation is going, while owning the operational machine that gets it there. You will drive the effectiveness, alignment, and performance of the Product organisation, using data, insight, and increasingly AI-enabled tooling to keep that machine running smoothly as we scale.

This is a dual strategy-and-operations role. You will help shape product strategy and portfolio direction alongside the CPO, while also owning the operational infrastructure that turns that strategy into results - managing the product portfolio, driving delivery, preparing board and executive materials, shaping the roadmap, allocating resource and budget, and contributing to pricing decisions. The role rests on three pillars: business and data insights, customer and market insights, and process and governance. If the Product Operating Model is the blueprint for how Xceptor creates and delivers product value, this role keeps the building systems running - ensuring product teams are aligned, prioritised effectively, and equipped to deliver high-quality outcomes at scale.

Who we're looking for

We’re looking for a senior product leader who combines strategic and operational strengths, with a track record of building effective operating models and managing complex portfolios.

Product & Delivery Leadership

  • 15 years’ experience in Product, Product Operations, or related roles, including prior product leadership experience (e.g. former Head of Product, VP Product, or Product Director).
  • A blend of management consulting and in-house product experience is strongly preferred - someone equally comfortable structuring strategic problems and rolling up their sleeves to run delivery.
  • Strong experience designing and scaling product operating models and governance.

Product & Operating Model Expertise

  • Deep understanding of product management practices.
  • Experience implementing planning, prioritisation, and governance frameworks.
  • Experience managing a product portfolio, including roadmap planning, resource allocation, and board-level reporting.
  • Experience building or scaling the core pillars of product operations - business and data insight, customer and market insight, and process and governance.

Data & Performance Orientation

  • Experience defining and tracking product KPIs.
  • Strong analytical capability and data-driven decision making.
  • Experience connecting commercial or financial metrics to product delivery data to inform prioritisation.
  • Exposure to pricing strategy or commercial decision-making is a plus.

Cross-functional Leadership

  • Ability to influence across product, engineering, and business and drive transformation in an organisation.
  • Strong stakeholder management in complex environments, including experience preparing materials for and presenting to boards or senior leadership.
  • Experience coordinating cross-functional launch or go-to-market readiness processes.

Execution Excellence

  • Strong organisational and operational discipline.
  • Ability to deliver initiatives from concept through execution and drive new ways of working.

Leadership & Team Development

  • Experience leading and developing a high-performing team.
  • Ability to build clarity, alignment, and accountability across teams in ambiguous, fast‑evolving environments.

What You’ll Be Doing

Product Strategy, Operating Model & Governance

  • Partner with the CPO to translate strategic priorities into an operating model, planning cadence, and governance structure that enables effective execution.
  • Lead the definition and evolution of the product operating model - including structure, decision rights, and ways of working - establishing scalable planning, prioritisation, and delivery frameworks.
  • Define governance structures and decision‑making processes, including cross‑functional rituals such as quarterly/PI planning, OKR‑setting, and business reviews, that drive alignment, accountability, and strategic outcomes across the organisation.
  • Ensure the operating model reflects the regulatory and risk environment in which Xceptor operates, embedding appropriate compliance and control considerations into product governance.

Portfolio Management, Roadmap & Resource Allocation

  • Own the day‑to‑day management of the product portfolio in partnership with the CPO, ensuring investment, roadmap, and resourcing decisions are aligned to business strategy and organisational objectives.
  • Lead roadmap planning and prioritisation processes across the product function, balancing strategic bets, run‑the‑business work, and customer commitments.
  • Drive resource allocation across product teams, ensuring capacity is aligned to priority and rebalanced as priorities shift.
  • Provide executive‑level transparency and visibility into priorities, trade‑offs, progress, and outcomes.

Business & Data Insights

  • Establish and oversee a product performance framework, defining KPIs and success measures that drive accountability and value creation.
  • Connect commercial and financial metrics - revenue, retention, cost‑to‑serve - to product delivery data, enabling prioritisation decisions to be grounded in business outcomes, not just output.
  • Deliver meaningful reporting and insights on progress, risks, performance, and impact to support strategic decision‑making and continuous improvement.
  • Act as steward of product data definitions and dashboards, ensuring metrics are consistent, trusted, and understood the same way across Product, Engineering, and the business.

Customer & Market Insights

  • Build the mechanisms that bring customer feedback, sales and support insights, win/loss data, and user research into a structured input for roadmap and portfolio decisions as part of the product management operating system.
  • Ensure product teams stay close to customers and the market as the organisation scales, preventing insight from being siloed in individual teams or lost in unread reports. Coordinate competitive and market intelligence gathering and testing with product marketing to inform strategic planning and positioning.

Delivery Oversight & ELT Reporting

  • Oversee delivery tracking and governance across the product portfolio, identifying risks and driving corrective action to keep roadmap commitments on track.
  • Own the preparation of board and executive materials on product strategy, portfolio performance, and delivery, acting as a trusted right hand to the CPO in board and leadership forums.
  • Ensure a consistent, high‑quality reporting cadence across the product organisation, from team level up to the board.

Launch & Go‑to‑Market Readiness

  • Own the cross‑functional launch readiness process, coordinating Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to ensure new products and features land successfully in the market.
  • Identify and close operational gaps between “built” and “launched”, ensuring go‑to‑market teams and product teams operate from the same priorities and timelines.

Pricing & Commercial Input

  • Partner with Product, Finance, and Commercial leadership on pricing strategy and frameworks, ensuring pricing decisions are informed by portfolio priorities and value delivered.
  • Support the CPO in connecting pricing, packaging, and commercial considerations into roadmap and portfolio planning.

Strategic Alignment and Execution Leadership

  • Drive alignment across Product, Engineering, and business functions to ensure successful delivery against strategic priorities.
  • Navigate complex dependencies, remove organisational barriers, and facilitate effective coordination across teams, domains, and leadership stakeholders.

Product Enablement, AI Tooling & Knowledge Management

  • Champion the development and adoption of product management tools, frameworks, playbooks, and best practices building with AI.
  • Maintain a single source of truth for product documentation, ways of working, and onboarding materials, so new and existing Product Managers can ramp quickly and consistently.
  • Drive initiatives that strengthen product capability, support organisational maturity, and establish consistent standards of excellence across the product function.
  • Explore and pilot AI‑enabled automation for reporting, insight synthesis, and other operational workflows to keep the product operations function efficient as it scales.

CPO Office, Strategy and Transformation

  • Be a trusted partner to the CPO, leading strategic initiatives and driving execution against key organisational priorities.
  • Support executive planning, communications, and stakeholder engagement, while delivering cross‑functional programmes that enhance the effectiveness and impact of the product organisation.

People Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop a high‑performing Product Operations team.
  • Create a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
  • Establish clear objectives, development plans, and career pathways for team members.
  • Drive workforce planning, succession planning, recruitment, and capability development across the function.

Diversity & Inclusion at Xceptor

We believe great ideas come from everywhere — and that the best teams are made up of people with different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. At Xceptor, we’re committed to building a workplace where everyone feels welcome, valued, and empowered to be themselves.

Hybrid at Xceptor

We love the buzz of the office and the flexibility of home—so at Xceptor, you get the best of both. Job Description

Job Description

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Product Manager to support Financial Systems, Business Intelligence, Order-to-Cash, and Revenue Operations initiatives within a complex enterprise environment.

 

This role sits at the intersection of Product, Finance, Legal, Revenue Operations, and technical teams. You will work proactively across these organizations to understand existing financial and commercial processes, identify data and workflow gaps, document requirements, and help translate business needs into clear functional specifications that technical teams can execute.

 

The ideal candidate combines strong Product Management fundamentals with practical knowledge of financial systems, contract and billing processes, operational reporting, and the data flows connecting CPQ/CLM and ERP platforms to downstream BI and analytics environments.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

* Own and support Product Management initiatives across Financial Systems, Order-to-Cash, Revenue Operations, and related BI capabilities.

* Partner proactively with Product Managers, Finance, Legal, Revenue Operations, and other stakeholders to map existing processes, identify gaps, and drive alignment.

* Understand and document end-to-end commercial and financial workflows spanning contracts, billing, entitlements, and downstream revenue recognition.

* Validate pricing, order, and contract data to troubleshoot operational issues and support accurate reporting.

* Define requirements for operational dashboards, reporting, and analytics that provide visibility into financial and commercial processes.

* Create process maps, workflow documentation, business requirements, and non-technical functional specifications that engineering and technical teams can translate into solutions.

* Partner with technical and data teams to ensure business requirements and financial-system logic are accurately represented in downstream systems and BI platforms.

* Understand how data moves between CPQ/CLM systems, ERP platforms, billing/revenue systems, and analytics environments.

* Identify opportunities to improve data quality, operational efficiency, process transparency, and reporting.

* Communicate clearly with senior stakeholders and proactively drive conversations needed to resolve ambiguity and move initiatives forward.

 

 

Qualifications

Must-Have Qualifications

 

* 5+ years of Product Management experience within Financial Systems, Financial Systems BI, Order-to-Cash, Revenue Operations, or related SaaS/technology environments.

* Solid understanding of core accounting terminology and the contract lifecycle, including billing, entitlements, and downstream revenue recognition impacts such as ASC 606.

* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence and initiative to proactively engage busy Product, Finance, and Legal leaders to gather information, map processes, and drive alignment.

* Proven experience validating pricing, order, and contract data for troubleshooting, operational reporting, and dashboard development.

* Strong analytical, process-mapping, and documentation skills.

* Experience translating business needs into clear, non-technical functional specifications for engineering, data, or other technical teams.

* General understanding of ERP platforms such as Workday, NetSuite, or SAP.

* General understanding of CPQ/CLM platforms such as Salesforce CPQ, Zuora, Conga, Icertis, DocuSign CLM, or Ironclad.

* Understanding of how CPQ/CLM, ERP, billing, and related commercial-system data flows into BI and analytics platforms.

 

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

 

* Conceptual understanding of modern data stacks and how data platforms support Financial Systems and BI use cases.

* Familiarity with business applications of Generative AI, large language models (LLMs), or predictive machine-learning models within corporate finance or financial operations.

* Experience in a high-volume marketplace or enterprise sales environment involving complex deal structures.

* Experience with contract analytics, contractual obligation tracking, or related compliance/reporting capabilities.

* Experience applying Lean, Six Sigma, or similar process-improvement methodologies to Financial Systems, Revenue Operations, or related processes.



Additional Information

Ideal Candidate Profile

 

The strongest candidate is a Product Manager who can bridge Finance, Product, Legal, Revenue Operations, data, and engineering teams. You should be comfortable going beyond backlog management: proactively investigating how processes work today, validating the underlying data, identifying operational gaps, defining what the business needs, and helping technical teams translate those needs into scalable reporting, workflow, and BI solutions.

 

Deep engineering expertise is not required. The emphasis is on Product Management, financial and commercial process understanding, analytical thinking, stakeholder engagement, functional requirements, and the ability to connect business processes with the systems and data that support them.

Handed a pipeline export, your instinct should be to find the problem, and to find what is working well enough to scale.

This role reports to the CFO. You will lead and develop the RevOps team, including the Deal Desk Manager and Salesforce Administrator, and work in dotted-line partnership with the Sales Operations Manager, GTM Engineering, and Marketing Operations. This is not a role for someone who manages through layers or operates exclusively at the strategic level — you should be comfortable getting into the data, inspecting the funnel, building the analyses and models yourself, and sitting down with functional leaders to solve problems.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the weekly inspection of pipeline creation, lead flow, funnel conversion, and rep-level productivity, and turn each week's findings into a short, specific list of actions for Sales and Marketing leadership.
  • Diagnose where the funnel is breaking and where it is outperforming, and make sure both get acted on.
  • Assess opportunity and pipeline quality directly, rather than taking stage and amount at face value.
  • Use AI to inspect pipeline at scale — opportunity quality, deal risk, and forecast credibility — rather than sampling manually.
  • Build AI-driven workflows for account prioritization, buying-signal detection, and weekly GTM inspection, replacing recurring manual analysis with automated reporting that leadership can trust.
  • Partner with GTM Engineering and functional leaders to identify and implement high-value AI use cases.
  • Deliver end-to-end visibility from lead generation through new business, onboarding, retention, expansion, and churn, including the analytical view of GRR, NRR, churn, and expansion tied back to acquisition source, segment, and deal characteristics.
  • Analyze conversion, velocity, pipeline health, cohort and segment performance, and revenue leakage; identify what our best customers and closed-won deals have in common and sharpen ICP, targeting, and segmentation around it.
  • Own the analytical framework for GTM capacity planning — headcount, productivity, quota capacity, pipeline requirements, and segment opportunity — and model the expected return from incremental GTM headcount, programs, and channels in partnership with Finance on annual planning.
  • Pressure-test forecast assumptions and surface leading indicators before they show up in reported results, partnering with the Sales Operations Manager, who owns the weekly forecast process, deal-level scrutiny, and sales operating cadence.
  • Own the GTM performance narrative for executive leadership and the Board, anticipating the questions before they are asked.
  • Set priorities and requirements for core GTM systems, data architecture, and reporting, and govern GTM definitions, metrics, and data quality so that Salesforce and other systems produce reliable, decision-useful data.

EXPERIENCE

  • 6–10+ years across Sales Strategy, Sales Operations, GTM Strategy, Revenue Analytics, Revenue Intelligence, Revenue Operations, or FP&A
  • A career built through Sales Strategy, Sales Ops, Marketing Ops, or GTM Strategy, rather than one centered primarily on Salesforce administration and systems ownership
  • Experience at high-growth SaaS companies in the ~$30M–$150M ARR range, where you personally pulled the data, built the model, and worked directly in the CRM
  • Proven ability to diagnose performance problems independently — and equally, to spot what is working and build the case for scaling it
  • Bachelor's Degree with equivalent experience a plus

KNOWLEDGE

  • Deep, practical AI experience — hands-on building, not familiarity with AI tools for drafting and content generation
  • Hands-on with the modern GTM stack: Salesforce, Gong, Clay, enrichment and intent data, SQL, dbt, or BI tools
  • Strong full-funnel analytics: pipeline, conversion, segmentation, retention, expansion, cohort analysis, and capacity modeling
  • Strong Excel/Google Sheets modeling skills; SQL, BI, or data warehouse experience is a plus
  • Exposure to Salesforce Revenue Cloud / CPQ or similar quote-to-cash systems is preferred; this is not a Salesforce implementation role, and you will not be the day-to-day administrator
  • Root-cause diagnosis across Marketing, BDR, Sales, and Customer Success — demand, qualification, process, capacity, productivity, or execution
  • Ability to communicate complex analytical findings clearly to executives and functional leaders
  • Builder mentality: inquisitive, high-energy, low-ego, and comfortable working in a small team and directly in the details

DESIRED BEHAVIORS

  • Receptive to change – is flexible. Seeks and adopts improved approaches and processes.
  • Initiates action – is results oriented, takes responsibility for actions and outcomes. Meets commitments and strives for high performance.
  • Manages the workload - makes timely decisions, prioritizes effectively, solves problems, monitors results and takes remedial action where necessary.
  • Technically proficient – knows the role and has a solid familiarity with tasks and responsibilities.
  • Takes responsibility for own learning - knows personal strengths and recognizes development needs. Is open to feedback and always seeks to learn.
  • Communicates ideas – strong facilitation and written communication, proposes a way forward. Listens to views of colleagues and takes in diverse perspectives.
  • Works collaboratively – shares information, fosters teamwork and contributes to a positive work environment where people want to come to work.
  • Display ethical character and competence - acts with integrity and intent, is accountable for own actions, behaves according to the company values.
  • Act as a good citizen of UpKeep.

COMPENSATION

Job Description

Job Description

Fractional Chief Marketing Officer

Hometown Builders Unlimited
Slinger, Wisconsin

CURRENT REALITY

You know how to market a home-service business.

You understand lead generation, paid traffic, content, websites, follow-up, and the numbers behind all of it.

But you’re tired of being held responsible for results while being kept at arm’s length.

No access to leadership.
No clear direction.
No authority to make decisions.
Not enough support to execute the plan.

You don’t need another client who wants “more leads” but won’t give you the access or influence required to produce them.

You need a company that’s ready to treat marketing like a real business function.

A BETTER FUTURE

At Hometown Builders Unlimited, you’ll work directly with leadership.

You’ll have a seat at the table, clear business goals, and real influence over the marketing direction of the company.

We’re looking for someone who can bring strategy, leadership, accountability, and fresh ideas into one clear marketing plan.

You won’t be hired to simply post on social media or manage random tasks.

You’ll help build a marketing system that produces qualified opportunities, tracks performance, and supports the long-term direction of the business.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We’re hiring a Fractional Chief Marketing Officer to lead our marketing strategy and help us build a steady, measurable flow of qualified leads.

This position requires one day per week in our Slinger, Wisconsin office. The remaining work may be completed remotely.

You’ll own five key areas:

1. Marketing Strategy and Leadership

  • Build quarterly and annual marketing plans
  • Connect marketing priorities to company goals
  • Manage the marketing budget
  • Review performance and recommend changes
  • Report monthly on lead generation and key marketing numbers

2. Paid Advertising

  • Manage Google Ads
  • Oversee Meta advertising
  • Build audience-targeting strategies
  • Improve campaign conversion rates
  • Coordinate retargeting campaigns and lead funnels

3. Website, SEO, and Conversion

  • Oversee website updates
  • Improve search rankings
  • Keep website content accurate and current
  • Improve landing-page conversion
  • Strengthen user experience and site performance

4. Social Media, Content, and Creative Direction

  • Build the company’s social media strategy
  • Create content calendars
  • Direct photo and video content
  • Plan reels, testimonials, project showcases, and educational videos
  • Develop seasonal campaigns and promotional ideas
  • Keep the brand consistent across every platform

5. Analytics and Performance

  • Track website traffic, conversions, and lead sources
  • Measure advertising performance
  • Monitor engagement and audience growth
  • Turn the numbers into clear decisions and next steps

This role is for someone who can think strategically, lead confidently, and stay close enough to execution to make sure the plan gets done.

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED

Your two primary scorecard numbers will be:

  1. Qualified leads generated per month
  2. Cost per qualified lead

We care about real business results.

Traffic, impressions, likes, and engagement may support the strategy, but they aren’t the finish line.

YOU’D BE A GREAT FIT IF...

  • You’ve produced measurable marketing results for home-service companies
  • You know how to connect marketing activity to qualified leads
  • You take responsibility for results and don’t hide behind reports
  • You communicate clearly and follow through
  • You protect the brand and care about the quality of the work
  • You can lead vendors, agencies, and internal team members
  • You bring ideas, but you also know how to test, measure, and improve them
  • You work well with direct access to ownership and leadership
  • You can work from our Slinger office one day per week
  • You’re always looking for ways to raise the standard

THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF...

  • Your experience is mostly outside the home-service world
  • You focus on vanity metrics instead of qualified opportunities
  • You need someone else to organize every priority for you
  • You make excuses when campaigns miss the mark
  • You struggle to explain marketing performance in plain language
  • You prefer random tactics over a documented strategy
  • You aren’t available to work from our office one day per week
  • You want the title but not the responsibility
  • You say yes to everything instead of giving leadership a clear recommendation

NEXT STEPS

Send us a 3–5 minute video introducing yourself.

Use the video to sell us on three things:

  1. Your experience marketing home-service businesses
  2. The results you’ve created for other companies
  3. How you believe you could help Hometown Builders Unlimited generate more qualified leads at a better cost

Be specific.

Tell us what you worked on, what changed, and what numbers improved.

Send your video to:

Tyler@hometownbuildersunlimited.com

We’re not looking for a polished sales pitch.

We’re looking for someone who understands the home-service market, can think like a marketing leader, and knows how to produce measurable results.

Company Overview

ID.me is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with ID.me once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 152 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with ID.me at 20 federal agencies, 45 state government agencies, and 70+ healthcare organizations. More than 600+ consumer brands use ID.me to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. ID.me’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. ID.me is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/ .

ID.me is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At ID.me, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found here .

About the Role

ID.me is looking for a Senior Manager, Revenue Accounting & Billing Operations to own our revenue and billing function end-to-end as we scale toward IPO readiness. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Accounting & Financial Operations, you'll own the full order-to-cash cycle — from how a deal is structured and booked in Salesforce, through usage capture and invoicing, to revenue recognition, deferred revenue, AR, and the monthly close.

This is a builder role for someone who wants to fix the system, not just operate it.

This is a builder's role. We've grown quickly across multiple verticals, and there's real opportunity now to design the billing and revenue infrastructure that carries us through our next stage of scale. You'll lead that build: automating billing vertical by vertical, partnering with Revenue Operations and the Salesforce team to get data right at the source, and working with the Data team to own the integrity and efficiency of the billing data pipeline. You'll also work directly with the leadership team to get full value from the finance systems we already own, and to design the data structure that makes reporting, analysis, and operating metrics automatic rather than assembled by hand. If you like leaving a process meaningfully better than you found it — and having the autonomy and support to do it — this is that role.

You’ll lead a team of three and be expected to bring ideas and then execute them. We want someone who is proactive, comfortable getting into the weeds of a usage file or a Salesforce field definition, and equally comfortable presenting a recognition position or an automation roadmap to leadership. Deep experience with revenue recognition in a usage-based or consumption-based billing model is essential; this is the core complexity of our business.

This position works from one of our officesMountain View, CA, McLean, VA, New York. NY office five days per week.

Key Responsibilities

Own the end-to-end revenue and billing cycle

  • Own the full order-to-cash cycle — deal booking and contract intake, usage and consumption data capture, invoicing, collections support, revenue recognition, deferred revenue, and AR — across all verticals and product lines.
  • Own revenue recognition for usage-based arrangements, including variable consideration, minimum commitments and overages, tiered and volume pricing, true-ups, and breakage, and author the ASC 606 memos that document and support those positions.
  • Own the monthly and quarterly revenue close, including journal entries, reconciliations, the ASC 606 revenue sub-ledger (subscription, usage, professional services, billing), revenue-by-customer/vertical schedules, and month-over-month fluctuation analysis.
  • Own billing accuracy and timeliness across verticals, including invoice preparation and review, customer billing inquiries, dispute resolution, and collections partnership.
  • Support external audits as the primary revenue and billing point of contact, and lead revenue-related SOX and IPO readiness — control design, documentation, and testing support.

Automate it — vertical by vertical

  • Lead the accounting automation roadmap for revenue and billing: identify the highest-effort manual processes, build the business case, and deliver the automation — hands‑on, not just as a project sponsor.
  • Automate billing end-to-end for every vertical, eliminating spreadsheet‑based and manual invoicing in favor of systematic, auditable, scalable processes.
  • Partner with the Senior Director to optimize the finance tool stack we already own (NetSuite, NetSuite ARM, Salesforce, Snowflake, Sigma, and Closing tool)— getting full value from existing investments before adding new systems, and leading evaluation when a gap is real.

Description

Part Time Account Executive - Minneapolis, MN

At Delta Defense, we stand for something bigger than a product. We believe the inalienable right to self-defense is fundamental to freedom. We believe in personal responsibility, training, and protecting the people we love. And we exist for the millions of responsible American gun owners — and those who may one day legally defend themselves — who take that responsibility seriously.

Delta Defense is the private company behind the marketing, operations, and customer service of the U.S. Concealed Carry Association (USCCA) — an organization dedicated to safeguarding the life, freedom, and finances of responsibly armed Americans. As an Outside Sales Account Executive, you carry that mission into every parking lot, range, retailer, and training room you step into. Learn more about the USCCA at https://www.usconcealedcarry.com/

As a Part-Time Account Executive on our Outside Sales team, you will drive sales and build strong relationships within an assigned territory. Ideal candidates are passionate about the Second Amendment, highly self motivated, and able to independently engage with local ranges, retailers, and instructors.

The reality of this role:

This part-time position offers flexibility to suit your schedule but does not include company benefits. In this role you have the chance to make a significant impact while still enjoying the flexibility of a part-time schedule.

Most days, you’ll be earning attention before you earn the sale.

You'll stand up at the end of a concealed carry class. In front of a room of strangers who just spent several hours learning to carry a firearm responsibly — and who are tired, skeptical, and not sure why they should listen to you. You'll show up cold at a range on a Saturday morning. You'll walk into a retailer whose owner has seen plenty of reps before you and isn't easily impressed.

And your job is to earn the right to be heard.

That's what makes this role different. It's face-to-face, relationship-driven, and credibility-first — especially in front of firearms instructors, range owners, and everyday Americans who care deeply about self-defense and personal freedom. If you're a responsible gun owner who enjoys being at the range, talking gear and training, and helping others protect themselves, you'll have instant rapport and authenticity. If you're new to the space but eager to learn the community, be honest about that too — people here respect humility far more than a memorized pitch.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Represent the USCCA in rural markets through education, outreach, and relationship-building.
  • Maintain and expand relationships with partner ranges, firearm instructors, and retailers.
  • Deliver compelling group presentations and drive awareness of USCCA Membership benefits.
  • Support CCW classes and onboarding events with accurate, compliant, and mission-aligned messaging.
  • Present and sell USCCA membership benefits to individuals and groups through pitches, classes, and events.
  • Collaborate with marketing and other support teams to organize, schedule, and execute sales events for maximum results.
  • Travel within assigned territory to attend partner events, training, and community engagements.
  • Work hours will vary based on event schedules and territory needs.

Experience/Educational Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent/GED.
  • Proven ability to close sales and achieve performance goals.
  • Strong interpersonal and presentation skills, with the ability to connect both 1:1 and in group settings.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain State Property & Casualty Insurance license (company training provided).
  • Reliable transportation and the ability to travel within assigned territory.
  • Strong organizational skills, self-motivation, and a results-driven mindset.
  • Proficient in or ability to learn Microsoft Suite Products, Google Suite & Salesforce.
  • Demonstrates the Core Values of Delta Defense LLC.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of sales, instruction, or community engagement experience.
  • Firearms industry familiarity and/or instructor certification.
  • Experience building relationships in rural markets.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with strong leadership and interpersonal skills to effectively build and maintain relationships.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, coupled with business acumen to drive sales and strategic initiatives.
  • Exceptional communication, presentation, and negotiation skills to confidently engage with diverse audiences.

Territory:

Minneapolis, MN

Compensation and Perks:

  • Salary - $25.00/hour plus 12% commission
  • 401K retirement plan eligible
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • USCCA Membership
  • Employee discount on USCCA store merchandise
  • Company-provided computer equipment and branded apparel allowance
  • Paid training
  • Please note that part time role does not include the company's full benefits package, such as health insurance coverage, available to full time employees

Our commitment to you:

If you’re selected for this role, you’ll receive the tools, coaching, and support you need to succeed. To set you up for a strong start, you’ll complete a required, paid training program that runs for the first 5 weeks. Training includes on-site orientation at company headquarters, self-paced learning, and a blend of virtual and in-person instructor-led classroom training. Because the training builds week to week, you’ll need to be fully available throughout the program.

Submit your application at: Delta Defense Careers

AI is walking, driving and flying into the physical world: humanoids, robotaxis, drones and a new class of autonomous machines. Each machine is built from thousands of parts. Sourcing just one still means trade shows, cold calls and endless scrolling on distributor sites. Supplier quotes land in a dozen formats, get re-keyed by hand into spreadsheets, and 100+ email threads follow just to confirm whether a part lands on time. It's 2026, and the most important machines of the next decade are still being sourced the way they were before the internet.

Syntro is building the first agentic procurement platform purpose-built for modern hardware manufacturing. We give manufacturers the ability to discover, select, and manage suppliers across the entire hardware lifecycle, from first prototype to production, at the speed and intelligence of AI.

We're an all-Stanford team that's experienced this problem firsthand at Apple, Dell, and Peloton. We're backed by Pear VC and Accel, alongside angels including Diane Greene (Founder, VMware) and Jeff Epstein (former CFO, Oracle).

The Role

We're hiring a Chief of Staff who operates as a force multiplier for the founders and can own initiatives across GTM, operations, and strategy. You'll frequently be the one who picks up a problem nobody else has, and you won't let go until it's solved or ready to scale.

You'll work directly with the CEO on the highest-leverage problems in the company, shifting between strategic and deeply tactical work within the same day.

What You'll Own

  • Build and close pipeline: Stand up repeatable top-of-funnel across conferences, outbound, referrals, and partnerships. Run discovery, demos and close revenue.
  • Turn field signal into product decisions: Take what you hear in the field and turn it into decisions: what ships next, what gets killed, what it takes to win the next cohort
  • Founder Leverage: Run point on whatever's highest-priority and least covered: prepping for critical partner and investor conversations and owning internal machinery (tax, legal, admin) with clear owners

Who You Are

  • You have worked in high-growth tech as a Chief of Staff, founder, early startup operator, GTM/BizOps leader, or management consultant with an operating track record
  • You're fluent in AI, not just as a user but as someone who understands how the models work and how AI products get built and sold.
  • You've proven yourself at 0-1 GTM: You've personally taken something new to market and closed customers
  • You're an exceptional written and verbal communicator who turns ambiguity into clear decisions quickly.
  • You're built for pace: this is an intense, all-in role at a company moving fast, and you do your best work when the tempo is high.
  • You have a relentless bias toward action: You move first, figure it out as you go, and don't wait to be told.

Every day, Remitly Business gains new signups who never complete their first transaction. Description
Amazon Health Services (AHS) is on a mission to make it dramatically easier for customers to find, choose, afford, and engage with the services, products, and professionals they need to get and stay healthy. We use design, service, and technology to redefine the healthcare experience. Our team centralizes marketing for all of AHS, alongside the data engines that power our optimization and valuation services. We are looking for an entrepreneurial leader to help customers embrace a new healthcare paradigm and drive lasting impact. The AHS Brand, Discovery, and Engagement Team is seeking a Sr. Product Marketing Manager (PMM) to serve as the single-threaded owner for the One Medical Senior Health Program’s marketing strategy. In this role, you will lead the strategic vision to acquire and engage customers aged 65+. You will translate national brand objectives into high-impact, locally relevant marketing programs, working backward from customer data to build a scalable marketing playbook across performance channels (including Onsite/SEO, Outbound, and Direct Mail). The successful candidate will be a data-obsessed, customer-centric leader who thinks strategically and executes with operational rigor. You must thrive in an entrepreneurial environment where ambiguity and competing priorities are the norm. You will anticipate and remove bottlenecks, make high-judgment tradeoffs, and balance business needs against constraints. You will sit at the center of the regional patient experience and own the full-funnel metrics—from initial awareness to in-office visits and long-term engagement. This requires exceptional analytical skills, a bias for action, and the ability to earn trust and influence a wide array of stakeholders, from channel managers to senior business leaders. This position will sit onsite in Seattle, WA.

Key job responsibilities

  • Own End-to-End Strategy: Define, develop, and execute the comprehensive growth strategy for One Medical Senior Health, working backward from customer insights to hit ambitious patient acquisition and retention targets.
  • Orchestrate Cross-Functional Channels: Act as the central strategic partner for regional marketing, aligning channel managers (Performance Marketing, SEO, Social, Content, PR) to deliver a seamless, full-funnel customer experience.
  • Scale Local Playbooks: Create, simplify, and scale a regional marketing playbook that enables hyper-local execution across digital channels (local SEO, geofencing) and physical touchpoints (in-office activations, community partnerships, local events).
  • Dive Deep into Analytics: Own full-funnel metrics—from impressions and clicks to sign-ups, office visits, and retention. Diagnose performance gaps and build experimental frameworks that drive continuous optimization.
  • Lead Innovation & Experimentation: Design and execute new, scalable marketing programs with measurable business impact. Own the measurement and reporting of these initiatives directly to senior leadership.
  • Manage Prioritization & Tradeoffs: Balance business needs against technical and operational constraints. Anticipate bottlenecks, make high-judgment tradeoffs, and establish streamlined processes that protect both financial and customer goals.

A day in the life

You will develop strategies to drive customer acquisition and engagement for One Medical’s Senior health program through behavioral analysis, customer research, retention program management, personalized content development, marketing channel management, and creative development. You will dive deep into marketing performance, analyzing key funnel metrics to identify trends and optimization opportunities. If a dashboard does not exist, you will work with Business Intelligence or Data Engineering teams to build one from scratch. Throughout the day, you will meet with performance marketing channel managers to review location-based ad campaigns and make data-driven decisions on budget allocation. You will also lead strategic planning sessions with Senior Health stakeholders to outline marketing plans, working backward from patient acquisition goals. Part of your day will focus on refining the marketing playbook—simplifying processes for seasonal marketing event programs. You will wrap up by preparing a data-rich document for weekly business reviews, clearly communicating the impact of your team’s initiatives to senior leadership.

About The Team

The AHS Brand, Discovery, and Engagement Team drives new customer acquisition across all Amazon Health businesses, including One Medical, Virtual Health Services, Amazon Pharmacy, and Health Business Connectors. We are heavily data-driven, customer-obsessed, and focused on automating channel optimization at scale. We hold an exceptionally high bar for our work and strategy, but we do not take ourselves too seriously. We actively collaborate with data engineering leaders to unlock customer behavioral signals that help us serve our patients better.

Shape the future of cinematic storytelling: for creators, by creators. We're seeking a founding Product Marketing Manager to own how the industry understands our GenAI-enabled creative platform — built at Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios to help professional creators bring animation, live action, and VFX content to screen. AI Studios is a fast-growing team operating as a startup within Amazon, with direct ownership of studio-level goals.

You will build the product marketing function for AI Studios' content creation platform from the ground up and own its strategy end to end. You are accountable for how our platform is positioned, differentiated, and understood at scale — the narrative, competitive positioning, and market brand that drive awareness and demand across Amazon MGM Studios, AWS, and the broader creative industry. You will operate with independence in a space where the long-term strategy is not yet defined, set the marketing strategy, and bring the data-driven judgment to make the hard positioning trade-offs. The single most important thing you bring is credibility in the AI content-creation industry: you know the tools, you have made content with them, and you can hold your own in any room — with the best creators and filmmakers, and with the most skeptical executives.

Key job responsibilities

  • Own the platform's core positioning and value proposition — the messaging and go-to-market narrative that define what it is, who it's for, and why it matters — so customers and partners understand it clearly and consistently.
  • Own competitive differentiation: track a fast-moving landscape, articulate where we lead and where we are heading, and evolve the story as the market and our capabilities change.
  • Aggregate and synthesize signals — competitive intelligence, customer and creator needs, industry and model trends — into a coherent marketing strategy and point of view that others build on.
  • Build the definitive narrative and asset portfolio, versioned for distinct audiences (executive, artist and creative, technical and model-focused) and kept current with our latest capabilities, so the organization is always ready to represent the platform at its best.
  • Drive awareness and demand across internal Amazon (Prime Video, Amazon MGM Studios, AWS, AGI, etc.), converting broad interest into a durable pipeline of engagement rather than one-off scrambles.
  • Represent the platform credibly in high-stakes rooms — and equip senior leaders with the framing, competitive answers, and visual aids they need to carry the story themselves.
  • Partner with Business Development and go-to-market teams to shape how the platform is positioned for the customer segments it serves over time.
  • Create the mechanisms that let product marketing scale as the function grows, force-multiplying your impact through creative partners and the broader team rather than producing everything yourself.
  • Collaborate closely with your cross-functional counterparts, including Product Management, UX Design, Engineering, Applied Science, and Creative teams to understand and inform the direction of our product suite.

A day in the life

Your morning starts with a request from leadership for a tailored pitch ahead of an executive meeting — and because you own a current, coherent narrative, you turn it around without pulling anyone off their day job. You sync with a creative lead to capture a fresh demo and usage anecdotes, then sharpen the competitive framing on where the platform leads and where it is heading. After lunch, you prep a model-focused cut of the story with Science for a technical audience and a VP-level cut for an upcoming review, and align with Business Development on how the positioning maps to their go-to-market. You field inbound interest from another team and fold it into the demand plan. You close the day evolving the differentiation story against the latest competitor release. Throughout, you're the person who owns how the industry sees what we're building.

About the team

AI Studios is a small, high-ownership "startup within Amazon," formed by Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios to build multimodal AI tools and models for content creation with human's in the driver's seat. We work directly with professional filmmakers, animators, and VFX artists on active productions. We operate from first principles, learn directly from working creators on real productions, and hold a high bar for craft, safety, and storytelling magic. If you're motivated by invention and inspired by storytellers, this is your seat at the table.

  • Experience using data and metrics to drive improvements
  • Experience with Excel or Tableau (data manipulation, macros, charts and pivot tables)
  • Experience communicating results to senior leadership
  • Experience building, executing and scaling cross-functional marketing programs
  • Experience leading go-to-market for consumer software or hardware product launches
  • Experience prior success in driving execution of large-scale project plans with multiple teams in support of business goals

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with customer segmentation, profiling, and targeting
  • Hands-on fluency creating content with generative-AI tools
  • Experience and credibility in the AI content-creation or media-production industry

https://www.whatjobs.com/pub_api__cpl__3.snippet:
Overview

Intuit’s Enterprise Suite (IES) is transforming how mid-market and growing enterprise businesses manage their finances, projects, and operations — all in one connected platform. As we expand IES across industries like Construction, Manufacturing, Financial Services/Real Estate/Family Office, Tech, Non-profit, and Healthcare, we’re seeking a Principal Product Marketing Manager to define our upmarket strategy and growth plan for the Healthcare vertical.

This is a senior, highly strategic, full-stack PMM role — combining market insight, product influence, packaging strategy, and storytelling leadership. You’ll partner closely with Product, Sales, Marketing, and Industry GMs to define how IES competes, differentiates, and wins in each vertical — shaping the next chapter of Intuit’s mid-market expansion.

Responsibilities

Define the Healthcare Vertical Strategy

  • Lead the end-to-end product marketing strategy for industry expansion — from market sizing and segmentation to positioning, pricing, and launch planning.
  • Identify high-growth verticals and subsegments with the strongest product-market fit, leveraging market, customer, and usage insights.
  • Develop frameworks that guide how Intuit builds, packages, and monetizes vertical workflows across QuickBooks Advanced and IES.
  • Partner with Finance, Analytics, and Product to model TAM, revenue potential, and attach opportunities across SKUs.

Shape Product and Packaging Decisions

  • Influence the product roadmap by connecting customer needs to monetization and adoption opportunities within each industry.
  • Define vertical editions, feature tiering, and pricing strategies that align with customer value and competitive dynamics.
  • Collaborate with Product to ensure new capabilities are positioned for maximum adoption, revenue, and retention.
  • Partner with PMMs across core departments to ensure a consistent and differentiated “vertical ERP” story.

Lead Go-to-Market Strategy and Execution

  • Own the narrative for how IES delivers end-to-end industry workflows — ensuring clarity and resonance from the website to sales decks.
  • Build the GTM blueprint for vertical launches, including naming, messaging, content strategy, enablement, and demand activation.
  • Partner with Channel and Sales Enablement to equip sales teams with vertical-specific playbooks, proof points, and competitive positioning.
  • Lead engagements and pitches with firms, selling partners and analysts
  • Lead cross-functional readiness reviews to ensure alignment across product, sales, and marketing teams for each launch.

Act as a Strategic Thought Partner

  • Serve as the senior voice of the market — regularly briefing leadership on trends, competitive movements, and opportunities for expansion.
  • Advise cross-functional leaders on how to prioritize investments that accelerate vertical adoption and market share.
  • Represent Intuit at industry events, customer councils, and analyst briefings as a credible thought leader for mid-market ERP innovation.

Qualifications

What You Bring

  • 12+ years of experience in product marketing, product strategy, or go-to-market leadership
  • Direct experience building product or GTM for Healthcare software
  • Deep understanding of how to translate customer insight into product and packaging decisions.
  • Track record of driving multi-vertical go-to-market initiatives that deliver measurable growth.
  • Exceptional storytelling and executive communication skills — able to inspire action across all levels of the organization.
  • Analytical rigor with comfort in modeling market opportunities, pricing, and financial impact.
  • Experience leading without authority — influencing roadmaps, org priorities, and cross-functional outcomes.

Pay and Benefits

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

The Expected Base Pay Range For This Position Is

Mountain View $205,000 - $277,500

The Director of Product Marketing is responsible for translating Microvast's technology and product capabilities into clear market value, differentiated positioning and effective commercial programs. The role owns global product positioning, messaging, market intelligence, launch marketing, sales enablement and brand execution, helping Business Development and Sales create and convert demand while ensuring every external claim is accurate, consistent and approved.

Responsibilities

Global Product Marketing Strategy

  • Develop and execute the global product marketing plan aligned with Microvast's revenue priorities, product road map, capacity, target applications and strategic markets.
  • Translate CRO and business priorities into product, segment, geography, channel, launch and content objectives with measurable outcomes.
  • Prioritize marketing investment based on addressable demand, product readiness, strategic value, competitive differentiation and commercial timing.
  • Maintain an integrated annual calendar for launches, campaigns, trade shows, customer programs, content and sales-enablement releases.

Segmentation and Go-to-Market Planning

  • Define priority markets, applications, customer profiles, buying groups, use cases and value drivers for each product family.
  • Develop go-to-market plans covering target audience, positioning, route to market, proof requirements, launch sequence, content and field enablement.

Positioning, Messaging and Value Proposition

  • Create differentiated positioning and value propositions based on verified customer outcomes, product capabilities, competitive alternatives and total economics.
  • Develop consistent message architecture by company, product family, application, audience and stage of the customer journey.

  • Maintain an approved claims library with supporting evidence, owners, usage guidance and review dates for performance, safety, cost, sustainability and reliability claims.

Product Launch and Lifecycle Marketing

  • Lead the market-readiness workstream for product introductions, major updates, certifications, application expansions and commercial phase changes.
  • Establish launch gates covering audience, positioning, proof, pricing input, sales training, content, channel readiness, customer references and communications approvals.
  • Coordinate launch plans with Product Management, Engineering, Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, Services, Legal and regional stakeholders.
  • Manage lifecycle messaging and content as products mature, improve, reposition or approach replacement, ensuring obsolete claims and materials are retired.

Sales, Business Development and OEM Enablement

  • Provide the revenue organization with current pitch decks, product briefs, application guides, case studies, comparison tools, objection handling and proof points.
  • Train Business Development, Sales, OEM Management, channel partners and relevant service personnel on value propositions, differentiation, use cases and approved claims.
  • Support priority customer workshops, RFQs, proposals and executive meetings with reusable content and account-specific message adaptation.
  • Create feedback mechanisms to identify missing tools, repeated objections, competitive gaps and content that materially improves opportunity progression.

Market, Customer and Competitive Intelligence

  • Build a structured intelligence program covering market size, growth, customers, competitors, products, pricing signals, regulations, incentives and technology trends.
  • Conduct customer, partner, analyst and field interviews to understand needs, decision criteria, buying processes, adoption barriers and unmet requirements.
  • Lead win-loss and no-decision analysis with Sales and Business Development and translate findings into positioning, product and commercial actions.
  • Deliver concise market and competitor updates to the CRO, Product Management, Engineering and revenue leaders with implications and recommended actions.

Brand, Content and Creative Governance

  • Maintain consistent product naming, visual identity, tone, terminology, templates and brand application across regions, business lines and channels.
  • Develop and govern high-quality website content, brochures, presentations, videos, technical-marketing materials, customer stories and campaign assets.
  • Ensure materials are technically accurate, current, audience-appropriate, translated where necessary and controlled through a documented review process.
  • Protect Microvast's credibility by preventing unsupported, outdated, inconsistent or unauthorized claims from reaching customers or the public.

Campaigns, Digital, Events and Demand Support

  • Plan integrated campaigns and market-development programs that support priority applications, launches, geographies and strategic-account objectives.
  • Manage product-marketing participation in trade shows, conferences, webinars, demonstrations, customer events and thought-leadership opportunities.
  • Establish lead-capture, qualification and routing rules so responses are assigned promptly to Business Development, Sales or OEM Management.
  • Measure content engagement, event performance, lead quality and commercial influence without claiming ownership of bookings or revenue closed by Sales.

Pricing, Packaging and Commercial Insight

  • Provide customer value, competitor, application and willingness-to-pay insight to support pricing strategy and product or service packaging.
  • Develop value calculators, total-cost-of-ownership tools and business cases using assumptions validated by Finance, Product Management and technical functions.
  • Recommend packaging, option structure, service bundles and commercial messages that improve product clarity and value realization.
  • Do not issue quotations, approve discounts or make customer commitments; route commercial decisions through Sales, the Account Owner and the approval matrix.

Team, Budget and Process Leadership

  • Build and lead a high-performing product marketing team with clear product or market coverage, skills, objectives and succession plans.
  • Manage agencies, contractors, translation partners, creative vendors, event suppliers and the approved marketing budget.
  • Establish repeatable processes for briefs, reviews, approvals, asset management, localization, version control, launch readiness and performance reporting.
  • Promote customer curiosity, technical accuracy, commercial focus, brand discipline, global collaboration and measurable impact.

Required QualificationsEducation And Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in marketing, business, engineering, communications or a related discipline required; MBA or relevant advanced degree preferred.
  • Ten or more years of progressive B2B product marketing, strategic marketing, technical marketing or commercialization experience.
  • At least three years leading teams, agencies or major cross-functional product launches in a global or multi-region environment.
  • Demonstrated success developing positioning, go-to-market plans, launch programs, sales enablement and market or competitive intelligence for complex products.
  • Experience in batteries, electric vehicles, automotive, commercial vehicles, energy storage, industrial technology or advanced manufacturing strongly preferred.
  • Experience marketing to technical, purchasing, executive and operating stakeholders across the United States, Europe and Asia is preferred.

Business, Marketing and Technical Knowledge

  • Strong command of segmentation, positioning, messaging, buyer research, product launches, content strategy, demand programs and sales enablement.
  • Ability to understand battery cells, modules, packs, BMS, thermal management, performance, safety and manufacturing sufficiently to create credible technical marketing.
  • Strong analytical capability in market sizing, competitive analysis, pricing research, win-loss analysis, campaign measurement and marketing-attribution limits.
  • Proficiency with CRM, content-management, digital-analytics, presentation, creative-workflow and asset-management tools.

Nash is the autonomic logistics platform. Self-optimizing, self-healing AI Agents unify decisioning and execution across fleets, carriers, and fulfillment networks. Set the objective, and the system runs until you hit it. We’re 1,000+ customers across 20+ countries, backed by a16z and Y Combinator.

About this role

Nash is hiring its first global field and event marketing lead. You will own how Nash shows up in person: the event strategy for the company, and the field execution behind it in every region. You will build the event calendar with our regional GTM leads, and lead a team of regional field managers across APAC, EMEA and North America. You report to the VP of Growth and work directly with Sales leaders in each region.

What you own

  • The event calendar. You decide which shows and sponsorships earn a place, and how big Nash goes at each one.
  • The account list for each event, shared with Sales, so events and outreach point the same way.
  • What each event returned, and what that says about where Nash shows up next.
  • The field budget across regions, invested against pipeline and deal acceleration.
  • Every in-person moment Nash creates: booths, dinners, hosted events, gifting, merch and swag.
  • ABM events for our top accounts, built with the account teams. Executive dinners, onsites, and gifts made for one account at a time.
  • The relationships with show organizers, partners and vendors that earn speaking slots, better booth placement, and co-hosted events.
  • Vendors and production partners in every region. You choose them, set the terms, and hold them to the standard, across booth build, print, swag, freight and storage.
  • The content each event produces. You shoot your own, direct photographers and videographers, and get attendees and the team posting.
  • Internal events, including all-hands and company offsites, held to the same standard as the ones customers see.
  • The regional team. You hire the field managers, set the standard, and keep running the events that matter most yourself.

What you bring

  • 7+ years in B2B field or event marketing, across more than one region.
  • Shows you owned outright. You picked them, ran them, and answered for what came back.
  • You have run an event people wanted to come to and talked about afterward. One you were proud of, and that became a flagship part of the company.
  • A team you built and led across time zones, employees or contractors, including the hiring.
  • Super self-starter. You find the person who can unblock you, and you can put something good together on budget and with days' notice, then build the system that makes the next one easier to run.
  • Taste and polish. You know the difference between a booth people stop at and one they walk past, and the details guests notice are right, from the invite through the run of show.
  • Pipeline and the big picture. You can walk through the pipeline your events produced and how it moved, and you plan a year of events as one program rather than a series of one-offs.
  • AI already in your workflow, and something you built or improved that you can show us.
  • Command of budget and logistics at scale, and steadiness in the week of a show.
  • Willingness to travel 30 to 40% of the year.

More about Nash

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics.

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.

What You’ll Love About Us

  • Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career!
  • Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates
  • Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
  • Flexible paid time off
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

Job Description

Job Description


*****A minimum of 3 years of  Manager experience in a fine dining restaurant is required to be considered.*****

 

REPORTS TO: General Manager


Job Summary:

The Events and Operations Manager assists the General Manager and Assistant General Manager in the day-to-day operations of RCSH restaurant. This role is directly accountable for the supervision and management of front-of-house bar operations, hosts, and servers. The manager maintains the highest quality of beverage and service standards, cleanliness, sanitation, and safety. In the absence of the General Manager, the manager oversees and coordinates activities concerning all front-of-the-house operations. Success is real growth in sales, profit, and market share, and is the result of living The Sizzle for our employees and guests.

In this role, you will also assist with generating new and repeat banquet and catering sales, actively network and promote the brand within the community, and greet the hosts of private dining events, which are primarily held in the evenings and on weekends. The role involves supporting event coordination, driving customer satisfaction, and maintaining high operational standards.


Key Responsibilities:


Operational Support:

  • Assist the General Manager in overseeing daily restaurant operations to ensure efficiency and high standards of service.
  • Help implement and enforce company policies, procedures, and standards as directed by the General Manager.
  • Supervise day-to-day operations to ensure all standards of RCSH quality and service are achieved during each shift.
  • Provide ongoing coaching and appropriate progressive discipline to all Team Members, managing appropriate documentation and ensuring each Team Member has clarity around their current level of performance.
  • Increase sales in the restaurant by providing the highest levels of uncompromising quality of food, beverage, reception, greeting, seating, and service.
  • Conduct first interviews and recommend hires to the General Manager and Chef.
  • Provide orientation and training according to all RCSH training systems, standards, and manuals for new hires.
  • Construct the weekly work schedule to meet the demands of the business.
  • Supervise operations and Team Members to ensure that all cleaning, maintenance, housekeeping, and side work duties are accomplished in line with operations standards.
  • Proactively communicate with the General Manager and other members of the management team to share and convey information regarding the restaurant.
  • Maintain familiarity with all national, state, and local safety, health, and sanitation standards and ensure all Team Members are following guidelines appropriately.
  • Maintain a strong presence on the restaurant floor, engaging with guests to ensure satisfaction.
  • Address and resolve customer complaints and concerns in a professional manner.
  • Implement strategies to improve guest experience and increase guest loyalty.
  • Correctly perform all duties necessary to close the restaurant.
  • Additional duties as assigned.


Event Coordination:

  • Support the General Manager in planning, coordinating, and executing events within the restaurant, including private parties, corporate gatherings, and special promotions.
  • Collaborate with clients to understand their event needs and ensure their expectations are met.
  • Work closely with the kitchen and service staff to deliver seamless event experiences.
  • Assist in managing event budgets, timelines, and logistics.
  • Utilize the Tripleseat discussion templates and event contract to interact with Private Dining guests via phone and/or email to confirm event details and answer any questions.
  • Follow up with guests post-event to ensure satisfaction.
  • Communicate all event details to the local Restaurant Management, ensuring 100% clarity of details and expectations.
  • Keep records of guest contact information, interactions, and transactions in the reservation system and Tripleseat.
  • Generate reports within the event booking management software as requested.
  • Assist in the coordination of private dining menu requests.
  • Backup for Regional Sales Manager in restaurant location.
  • Manage Private Dining events on the books successfully and work pipeline of inquiries, prospects, tentative, and definite bookings.
  • Work closely with the Regional Sales Manager to generate new business and maintain contact with present accounts.
  • Assist the Regional Sales Manager with Private Dining events from organization to execution, including delegation of responsibilities to the Restaurant Team.
  • Administrative duties assigned as needed.
  • Additional duties as assigned.


Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Hospitality Management, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in restaurant management and event coordination.
  • Proven ability to manage operations and lead a team effectively.
  • Strong organizational, multitasking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Proficiency in restaurant management software and Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.
  • Familiarity with event booking management software, particularly Tripleseat, is a plus.


Benefits:

  • Competitive salary, commission, and performance-based bonuses.
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.
  • RRSP with company match.
  • Paid time off and holidays.
  • Opportunities for professional development and career advancement.
  • Employee discounts on dining and events.
