Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

The Food & Beverage Events Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for large and small scale events, banquet operations, and dining environments to ensure exceptional guest experiences and strong financial performance. This role drives service excellence, team alignment, and revenue optimization while supporting a high-performing, hospitality-focused culture.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
  • Oversees and manages all areas of the Conference and food services and makes decisions on matters of importance. Ensures sanitary practices for food handling, general cleanliness, and maintenance of kitchen and dining areas as well as compliance with operational standards, Company policies, federal/state/local laws and ordinances.
  • Responsible for ensuring consistent high quality of food preparation and service.
  • Responsible for communication with event planners, clients, and guests with regards to their event, including meeting room, event area set-up, audio/visual and other meeting needs as well as assists in all food choices for the event.
  • Accurately estimates food and beverage costs, maintains portion control to minimize waste.
  • Accurately estimates food needs, places orders with distributors for delivery.
  • Prepares food or supervises food preparation for events and guests.
  • Ensures positive guest/client service in all areas. Responds to complaints, taking all appropriate actions to turn dissatisfied guests/clients into return guests.
  • Maintains a professional appearance in accordance with Company standards; wears the appropriate uniform or attire.
  • Maintains open and effective communication with team members and management.
  • Attends and participates in team meetings.
  • Completes all required Company training/compliance courses as assigned, adheres to Company standards and compliant with all policies and procedures.
  • Performs other related duties and responsibilities as assigned.
EXPERIENCE
  • A minimum two (2) years of supervisory experience in related field required.
SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Oversees and coordinates the department's activities. While a portion of the time may involve performing tasks similar to those of direct reports, the primary responsibilities are related to management and coordination. Analyzes and resolves issues, establishes work methods, ensures regulatory compliance, and maintains productivity.

Specific supervisory duties include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Establishes objectives and goals for the team. Assigns, monitors, and reviews work; evaluates direct report's performance.
  • Recruits and interviews, Orientates and trains. Issues corrective action and makes recommendations for termination.
  • Investigates and resolves concerns and complaints.
  • Creates department work schedules. Approves time records and time off requests.
  • Oversees the department's budget.
  • Ensures accurate and efficient management of inventory.
LICENSES & CERTIFICATIONS
  • Food and Beverage Food Handlers Manager Permit - must be state/county-specific.
  • Alcohol Awareness Training Certification - must be state/county-specific.
SKILLS & ABILITIES

This position requires the capability to understand and follow both oral and written directions, as well as the ability to communicate effectively in English and interact successfully with internal and external customers.

  • Proficient in time management; the ability to effectively organize and manage multiple priorities.
  • Build strong working relationships with team members at all levels. Skilled in building and motivating a team.
  • Performs well with frequent interruptions and/or distractions.
  • Business acumen, including but not limited to financial management, budgeting, cost control, and revenue optimization.
  • Ability to effectively listen, understand, and resolve challenges and concerns from management, team members, and/or customers (internal/external).
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills to include coaching, counseling, and mentoring.
  • Able to identify and seize revenue-generating opportunities while effectively managing costs and resources.
  • Proven ability to drive revenue growth, optimize costs, and achieve financial targets.
  • Able to engage diplomatically and effectively with third party operators, empathizing, and reacting appropriately to partner feedback and helping resolve issues where necessary.
  • Basic math skills.
  • Basic knowledge of Google Docs/Microsoft Word, Google Sheets/Excel
  • Able to maintain a positive and professional working environment.
  • Able to work effectively in a culturally diverse environment and support diversity and inclusion within the organization.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS
  • Stooping: Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist. Specifically, if it is to a considerable degree and requires full motion of the lower extremities and back muscles.
  • Kneeling/Crouching: Bending legs at knee to come to a rest on knee or knees.
  • Standing: Particularly for sustained periods of time.
  • Walking: Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks.
  • Pushing: Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward, or outward.
  • Pulling: Using upper extremities to exert force in order to draw, haul, or tug objects in a sustained motion.
  • Lifting: Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position-to-position. Specifically, if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires substantial use of upper extremities and back muscles.
  • Repetitive Motion: Substantial movements (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers.
  • Close and Distance Vision: Clear vision at 20 inches or less and 20 feet or more. Required to perform an activity such as preparing and analyzing data, transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, extensive reading or visual inspections.

This role will report jointly to the Vice President of Sales and Marketing and the Director of Physicians Preference Vitamins.

Strong understanding of ecommerce revenue growth, conversion, customer acquisition, and product adoption.

Excellent writing, messaging, organization, and analytical skills.

Role Details

Contract position 20 hours per week Flexible days and times, provided work is high quality, timely, and results-driven Time in the Katy office is preferred Remote work is acceptable for a candidate with proven experience Compensation range: $40 - $50/hour, based on experience, performance, and measurable results.

Physicians Preference Vitamins offers high-quality, physician-grade vitamins and supplements designed to support wellness with clean, premium formulations. This role will help build awareness, adoption, and ecommerce revenue for specific supplement products, one product at a time.

Leads the product marketing function for Paychex with accountability for the commercial strategy of every product set: the ideal customer profile, the positioning and value narrative, the pricing and packaging architecture, the go-to-market strategy, and the market intelligence that helps inform the product roadmap. Partners with Product to influence roadmap direction, owns the pricing and bundling recommendation brought to governance, and supplies the points of view and messaging strategy that Content, Design, Demand Generation, and Enablement execute against. Responsibilities

  • Market intelligence and roadmap partnership. Own continuous sensing of the HCM market — industry and technology trends, regulatory and compliance change, competitive movement, win/loss findings, analyst and channel influencer input, and market sizing. Bring a written, evidence-based point of view to every product roadmap review to influence prioritization and investment decisions, while Product Management retains the prioritization decision.
  • Ideal customer profile and buyer insight. Own the definition, maintenance, publication, and organizational adoption of the ICP, buyer and user personas, buying committee dynamics, and journey maps for every product set. Establish the voice-of-customer research program — primary interviews, advisory boards, and survey research — and hold the organization accountable to targeting, building for, and serving the profiles defined.
  • Pricing, packaging, and bundling strategy. Own the monetization strategy, analysis, and recommendation for each product set: pricing model and metric, tiering, packaging fences, bundle architecture, willingness-to-pay research, competitive price positioning, price change programs, and discount guardrails. Partner with Finance, Product, and Sales for input and modeling, and secure approval through the pricing governance forum.
  • Positioning, messaging, and value narrative. Own portfolio-level and product-level positioning and the messaging architecture that cascades across every channel. Translate product capability into customer benefits and quantified business outcomes, deliver points of view and messaging briefs to Content, Design, Demand Generation, Brand, and Enablement, and govern message consistency across the enterprise.
  • Launch and go-to-market orchestration. Own the launch tiering model, go-to-market plans, and cross-functional launch readiness across Product, Sales, Enablement, Service, Compliance, and the partner channel. Hold go/no-go authority on go-to-market readiness, accountability for 30/60/90-day post-launch performance, and ownership of end-of-life and migration go-to-market.
  • Lifecycle, adoption, and expansion. Own the post-sale commercial narrative: activation and time-to-value messaging, feature adoption strategy, cross-sell and attach strategy by ICP, the retention and renewal narrative, and the customer proof and reference agenda.

Define the job architecture and competency model, assess and develop existing talent, recruit scarce capabilities in pricing and monetization, competitive intelligence, and primary research, and coach the team to author and defend points of view.

  • Master's Degree in MBA or related advanced degree - Preferred

  • 3 years of experience in Influencing product roadmap decisions through market, buyer, and competitive evidence in a matrixed organization, without direct authority over the roadmap.
  • 3 years of experience in HCM, payroll, HR technology, benefits, insurance, or financial services experience serving small and mid-sized business customers.

  • Pragmatic Institute Product Marketing Certification, Product Marketing Alliance certification; Professional Pricing Society Certified Pricing Professional (CPP) - Preferred

Think about your last hotel stay. Did you skip the front desk line with mobile check-in? Message the staff for extra pillows? Order a late-night snack with a tap on your phone? Then you’ve likely run into Canary in the wild.

Canary Technologies is the leading agentic AI platform for hotel and guest management, powering the digital infrastructure for more than 20,000 hotels in 125+ countries. The world's most renowned hospitality brands, including Marriott International, Four Seasons and Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, partner with us to increase revenue, improve operations and elevate the guest experience.

We’re scaling our team to bring innovation to life faster than ever.

We're growing quickly, and we're looking for people who are passionate about their work, want to grow with us and are ready to take on more responsibility along the way. We value rigor and velocity in equal measure: high standards, fast pace, real ownership. If that's the environment you're looking for, this is the place for you.

Come join us! Let’s shape the future of hospitality together.

About the Role

We're looking for a seasoned Associate Product Marketing Director to run and scale the impact of product marketing across Canary. You'll manage an existing team of top PMMs and act as the connective tissue between product, sales, and marketing. You will define Canary’s unique place in the hospitality market as the leader in agentic AI solutions for guest and staff management.

This is not a coordinator role. It’s also not a pure strategy role. You'll set the positioning and messaging framework for the entire platform, own pricing and packaging strategy, and make Canary’s value clear and compelling for individual hotels as well as world-class brands. You'll work directly with the Head of Brand Marketing and the rest of the leadership team to influence strategy and prioritize roadmap.

  • Team leadership. Manage, coach, and develop a team of PMMs (currently 3). Build the function's operating model and hold a high bar on quality and speed of execution. Foster a culture of continuous investment in individuals and the function as a whole rooted in ongoing feedback and improvements that makes the team better every quarter.
  • Positioning and messaging. Define and maintain Canary's platform and product-level positioning. Translate complex AI capabilities into clear, differentiated value props for hotel operators — from global enterprise brands to independent properties.
  • Storytelling and narrative. Build the overarching platform narrative and ensure it holds across every touchpoint — the website, sales decks, event keynotes, analyst briefings, and customer conversations. Differentiate Canary’s narrative from the competitive landscape.
  • Product launches. Own the GTM process end to end — launch strategy, tiering, internal collaboration, and external amplification.
  • Product suite performance. Continuous analytics and monitoring on product performance and opportunities for improvement from pipeline through churn reduction.
  • Market intelligence. Maintain a deep, current read on the hospitality tech competitive landscape, buyer dynamics, and how the AI wave is reshaping the category.
  • 8+ years in product marketing, with at least 2–3 years managing and developing a PMM team.
  • Experience scaling the impact of a PMM function — not just inheriting one.
  • Deep expertise in pricing and packaging strategy, ideally in a SaaS context with a multi-product portfolio.
  • Strong positioning and messaging chops — you've taken complex products to market and made them simple and compelling.
  • Experience with product launches from concept through post-launch measurement; you've run launches across multiple tiers and know how to calibrate the machine.
  • A storyteller at heart — you write and communicate with precision and can shift register from a hotel GM to a C‑suite executive to an analyst.
  • Analytically rigorous — you use data to make decisions, build business cases, and keep customer value and ROI as central to the product story.
  • Background in B2B SaaS AI or hospitality technology strongly preferred; candidates who've worked in vertically focused SaaS (especially in industries with complex, multi-segment buyer dynamics) will stand out.
  • Based in New York City; comfortable in a hybrid environment (3 days / week in office)

Target cash compensation ranges from $190,000 – $230,000, including a fixed annual salary and a performance-based bonus paid monthly.

This role also includes a stock option grant, subject to board approval.

Actual compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's skill level, experience, and specific work location.

We work hard to make Canary a fun, rewarding, and high-energy place to work. Here’s how we take care of our flock:

Time Off

  • Unlimited PTO: Take the time you need to truly rest and recharge.
  • Holidays + Canary Days: Standard holidays plus monthly company-wide days off for a guaranteed long weekend.

  • Office Exchange: A travel stipend to visit the team in person at our SF, NY, or Dallas hubs.

Growth & Community

  • Self Improvement Club: A monthly budget to help you smash your personal goals.

  • Referral Program: Help us grow the flock and score a cash bonus for successful hires.

About this position

About Mobia Medical

The world's leading companies rely on Dataiku to operationalize AI and run it as a true business performance engine delivering measurable value. For more, visit the Dataiku blog , LinkedIn , X , and YouTube .

About the role

Dataiku is the platform for AI Success, helping organizations put AI to work across their business. The Growth team drives pipeline generation globally through paid media, content syndication, ABM, and marketing operations, and we're looking for a Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing to build and own the lifecycle function end to end.

You'll work closely with the VP of Digital & Growth and cross-functional partners across Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success, supporting a global organization across regions. We don't have a lifecycle function today. Email and nurture are secondary responsibilities inside other teams' jobs, so nobody owns what a prospect or customer hears from us, in what order, or how often. There are existing nurture workflows without a current owner and no single view of what runs where, so establishing that visibility is the first priority. You'll build the function from there: the strategy, the systems, the programs, and the team.

What you'll own

The lifecycle operating system

  • One authoritative email and lifecycle calendar across prospect, new-user and customer programs: what goes out, to whom, from which team, and when.
  • Frequency governance, suppression logic and deliverability standards, including being able to say how much of an audience a given send reaches.
  • Segmentation and audience standards, set with the web and marketing ops teams who manage list creation today.
  • A standard for what a lifecycle program needs before it launches: entry criteria, success metric, exit.

Prospect and new-user nurture

  • New-user onboarding and activation nurture: the sequences that move a first touch to an engaged, sales-ready account.
  • Account progression communication: the programs that move accounts from first engagement toward qualified opportunity.
  • Nurture designed around named-account cohorts, built alongside the integrated campaign work so the two don't duplicate each other.
  • Visibility for BDRs into what a lead has already received before they reach out.

Customer lifecycle, retention and expansion

You'll partner closely with Customer Success and Product on this.

  • Programmatic customer nurture: adoption, education, and the sequences that keep users active after initial deployment.
  • Retention and expansion programs, built on account signals rather than calendar cadence.

Automation, data and measurement

  • The lifecycle layer of the marketing automation stack end to end: HubSpot workflows, Salesforce integration, and account and intent data from 6sense.
  • Consolidating the existing nurture workflows into something documented and maintained.
  • Reporting lifecycle contribution in terms the business already uses: engagement progression, influenced pipeline, retention and expansion. You'll build your own reporting rather than wait for a dashboard.
  • The data quality this function depends on, with marketing ops: deliverability, consent, record hygiene.

AI and agentic workflows

  • Lifecycle work inside agentic workflows, rather than AI as a separate experiment. Lifecycle is one of the clearest applications: audience assembly, copy variation, program QA, performance summaries.
  • A standard for what a well-built lifecycle agent looks like, and where human in the loop is required.

Building the function

  • This is the lead role for a function that doesn't exist yet. You'll build the team as the function develops.
  • Getting the rest of the organization aligned on what you're building. Lifecycle touches Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success.

What you bring

  • 6+ years in lifecycle, nurture, email or growth marketing in B2B, ideally enterprise software with long, multi-threaded buying cycles.
  • Hands-on marketing automation depth. You've built and owned complex nurture programs yourself. HubSpot or Marketo depth, Salesforce fluency, and real comfort with the data model under both.
  • Command of deliverability, frequency capping, suppression, consent and list hygiene. This role exists partly because nobody has owned these.
  • Experience on both sides of the lifecycle, prospect and customer. If your background covers one, tell us how you'd approach the other.
  • Fluency with intent and account data (6sense, Demandbase or similar), and a view on where it should drive program entry rather than only reporting.
  • Comfort building with AI, expected rather than optional. No engineering background needed. You should already be using LLMs in your own work, with a view on where they belong in lifecycle programs and where human in the loop is required.
  • Analytical strength. You can define a metric, instrument it, and defend it, including when the honest answer is that the current number isn't reliable.
  • Comfort with a build role: ambiguity, direct conversations about tradeoffs, and establishing a function through influence before you have a team.
  • Experience working across regions in a global organization.
  • Excellent written English. Other languages welcome, not required.

Why this role

Lifecycle is unowned at Dataiku today. This role defines it, reporting to the VP who owns the function, with a mandate to build the team behind it.

The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

About New York Times Games

The New York Times is looking for a Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager to join the New York Times Games team, reporting to the Executive Director of Marketing, Games.

In 2025, players completed more than 11 billion games across our portfolio, led by hits like Wordle and Connections, alongside the iconic New York Times Crossword, which has existed in print since 1942.

Games is one of the largest and fastest-growing businesses among our portfolio of products, including Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic and News.

About The Role

We need a senior lifecycle marketer to lead how we keep Games players engaged over time across email, push (app and desktop), display and other channels. You will focus on deepening engagement with our existing players (non sub + sub) and reducing churn.

You will lead the end-to-end marketing lifecycle strategy for Games players, from onboarding and activation through ongoing engagement, win-back and reactivation. You will design and run cross-channel programs that create timely, relevant, and personalized experiences for our players, grounded in data and insight. You will work closely with product, growth marketing, product marketing, data and creative partners to bring these programs to life.

This is a temporary hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters, reporting to the Executive Director, Marketing, Games. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities

Lifecycle Strategy and Planning

  • Define the lifecycle marketing strategy for Games, including goals for activation, engagement, retention and reactivation.
  • Map player journeys and identify key moments where lifecycle programs can deepen engagement and reduce churn.
  • Partner with product and product marketing to ensure lifecycle programs align with feature launches, game updates and the broader Games roadmap.

Channel Execution and Optimization

  • Lead the planning and execution of lifecycle campaigns and automations across email, push, display and other channels, from brief through launch, in partnership with channel owners.
  • Work with channel owners to build, test and optimize always-on programs (onboarding flows, engagement nudges, winback journeys) that drive meaningful changes in player behavior.

Data, Measurement and Insights

  • Own key lifecycle metrics for Games, including retention, reactivation, engagement and churn, and build reporting that gives the team a clear view of performance.
  • Partner with analytics and data science teams to use segmentation, cohort analysis and predictive signals to inform targeting and personalization of lifecycle programs.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Build strong relationships with product, product marketing, growth marketing, media team and channel owners, audience insights, data analytics, engineering and creative to align on shared goals, design and launch lifecycle programs.

Player Experience And Brand Stewardship

  • Champion the perspective of our players, bringing research and behavior insights into planning and creative development.
  • Balance performance goals with a thoughtful, respectful approach to frequency, personalization and offers.

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in lifecycle marketing, CRM, retention marketing or related fields, with a track record of driving measurable improvements in engagement and retention.
  • Experience owning cross-channel lifecycle programs (email, push, and at least one additional channel such as display or in-app messaging) for consumer products or subscription services.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with data to build hypotheses, design tests and interpret results.
  • Operate in cross-functional environments and collaborating with product, analytics, media partners and creative teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with cohort and funnel analysis.
  • Interest in The New York Times and New York Times Games; prior experience with digital subscription, content, or mobile app products.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate both autonomously and collaboratively, with curiosity about identifying and forging new opportunities.

This role partners closely with IT to deliver strategic marketing initiatives that align to business objectives and drive measurable impact. The Manager ensures data accuracy, system integrity, and scalable platforms across all channels supporting donor retention, lifecycle planning, and digital engagement. They manage the scope, requirements, and implementation of new marketing technology solutions while maintaining and evolving the existing MarTech stack. As a hybrid leader, the Manager oversees a small technical team, owns the CDP and marketing automation roadmap, and serves as a strategic technical liaison across Marketing, IT, Analytics, and Growth. The role drives data informed decision-making, enables advanced segmentation, and builds operational maturity that contributes to increased Donor Lifetime Value.

Strategy, Roadmap & Future-Proofing

  • Lead the evolution and optimization of the donor lifecycle strategy using insights from Salesforce, SFMC, CDP and Data Lake integration.
  • Assist in next-generation architecture development for CRM, CDP, and automation systems with an emphasis on Salesforce ecosystem advancement.
  • Identify emerging MarTech and Salesforce capabilities that improve engagement, personalization, and automation scalability.
  • Architect a robust, future-proof marketing automation framework integrated tightly with Salesforce and Fabric data assets.

Team Leadership & Development

  • Manage and mentor Marketing Automation Specialists who work hands-on within Salesforce Marketing Cloud.
  • Encourage technical mastery in SFMC, and data management best practices.
  • Conduct capacity planning to balance workload, timelines, and operational needs.
  • Provide feedback and coaching that strengthens accountability, autonomy, and execution quality.

Technical Operations & Execution

  • Serve as the senior technical authority for Salesforce, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CDP, and related MarTech platforms.
  • Oversee data governance, ingestion, normalization, and segmentation workflows across SFMC, CDP, DAM, Salesforce CRM, and the Data Lake.
  • Partner with IT and data teams to optimize data pipelines, improve data integrity, and ensure clean, actionable datasets for lifecycle marketing.
  • Build and enhance automations, journeys, and system integrations leveraging SFMC and CDP data structures.
  • Lead QA processes, documentation, testing, and compliance for related marketing technology operations.

Reporting & Analytics

  • Develop reporting frameworks using Salesforce, CDP, Data Lake integration, and marketing automation performance data.
  • Produce insights that optimize segmentation, journey design, audience strategy, and lifecycle performance.
  • Works with IT and I&A to validate data accuracy across Salesforce, SFMC, DAM, Data Lake, and the CDP, identifying and resolving discrepancies.
  • Identify trends that drive improved automation efficiency, data enrichment, and donor retention strategies.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Partnership

  • Act as the primary connector between Marketing, IT, Analytics, and Growth regarding Salesforce, SFMC, and CDP data capabilities.
  • Translate technical constraints into clear business implications without slowing momentum.

This job description is intended to present the general content and requirements for the performance of this job. The description is not to be construed as an exhaustive statement of duties, responsibilities, or requirements. Managers and supervisors may assign other duties as needed.

EDUCATION

  • Required: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Marketing Cloud Email Specialist or a related field.
  • Preferred: Advanced degrees or certifications in relevant areas, professional experience in the pharmaceutical industry, and experience in engaging and managing third-party providers. Certification in Salesforce, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CDP systems

Experience

  • Minimum of 7-10 years of experience in CRM-related roles. 2-3 years of experience in Management
  • Experience overseeing Martech Technology Platforms, Salesforce, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Consumer Data Management Platform and other integrated systems is essential (working with third-party solutions and across digital channels)
  • Preferred: Experience with data management, reporting tools (e.g., Tableau, SAP), DAM, CDP and CRM optimization.

  • Results Delivery: Consistently high performer, results-oriented, agile decision-making, and proposing improvement actions.

  • Leadership: Direct and tolerant with others, listens, and seeks to understand the interests of all divisions and areas before acting.
  • Teamwork: Collaborates with others, forms part of a group and works across areas prioritizing collective interests over personal ones.

This is a high-ownership role for someone who's equally comfortable building a channel investment plan, tuning a paid social campaign, and making sure our brand shows up when people (and increasingly, AI assistants) search for answers about credit and lending.

You'll report to the Head of Product and own the strategy, budget, and performance of Braviant's digital marketing channels — not just executing tactically, but setting the roadmap, building the creative, tracking ROI, and reporting results to leadership. There is no in-house design or creative team, so you'll produce your own ad and landing page creative, and partner closely with Growth/Strategy, Data/Analytics, and Legal/Compliance (for regulatory review) to keep our digital presence sharp, fast, and effective at driving qualified traffic and conversions.   • Turn data into recommendations — what to scale, what to fix, and what to test next

About VetPowered

VetPowered LLC was founded in 2009 to support Workshops for Warriors (wfw.org), an accredited 501(c)(3) not for profit school that trains, certifies, and places veterans and transitioning service members into dignified lifelong careers in advanced manufacturing to Rebuild America’s Manufacturing Force…One Veteran at a Time.

Workshops for Warriors has trained and certified 1,776 veterans and transitioning service members, awarded nearly 23,000 industry credentials, and placed graduates at 522 companies across 49 states. The average starting wage for a WFW graduate is $63,500.

Our goal is to train veterans into dignified lifelong careers and make America the world’s manufacturing superpower again.

That is the story almost nobody has heard. This role exists to change that, and to turn the telling of it into purchase orders, partnerships, and product revenue. This will allow us to create scholarships, provide housing, and brighter futures for all the men and women who honorably served our nation.

The Role

You are the first dedicated marketing hire at VetPowered. You write the plan, then you pick up the camera and shoot it. You own two revenue motions that most companies split across two teams: a direct-to-consumer product business, and a defense manufacturing business that sells through RFQs and teaming agreements. You build the attribution model that proves which one your work moved.

Year one proves the model. Headcount follows the numbers you put on the board.

What You Will Own

Brand and Marketing Strategy

  • Own the twelve-month marketing plan and budget for VetPowered, plus a supporting awareness plan for Workshops for Warriors, reviewed with the CEO each quarter
  • Define positioning and messaging for both brands and for the relationship between them, and build messaging frameworks that hold up across the site, email, paid media, PR, and the shop floor
  • Establish the content standards and approval path that keep an ITAR-registered defense supplier’s public presence clean

Product Marketing and Go-to-Market

  • Own go-to-market for the Mark 10, Mark 15, apparel, and what ships next: audience definition, positioning, launch narrative, pricing tests with the CFO, and success criteria set before launch rather than after
  • Translate product capability into customer-first value propositions for two distinct buyers, the individual end user and the institutional account
  • Build the launch calendar and sequence paid investment against content readiness, so spend never lands against an unfinished product page
  • Partner with the CEO and business development on capability statements, partner packets, and the collateral that supports defense procurement conversations

E-Commerce and Digital

  • Own vetpowered.com and the direct-to-consumer store: site merchandising, product detail pages, cart, and checkout, with conversion rate and average order value as measured outcomes you are accountable for
  • Run a testing roadmap across landing pages, product pages, and checkout, and report what it taught you rather than only what you shipped
  • Own the promotional calendar and its execution across launches, seasonal moments, and tentpole events
  • Build the lifecycle program from zero: welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase, and reactivation flows, plus the nurture sequences that follow an inbound RFQ within 48 hours
  • Manage paid social, paid search, and SEO, in house or through an agency, against ROAS and cost per acquired customer

Marketing Operations and Attribution

  • Build the attribution model in Salesforce with our administrator: lead source discipline, campaign structure, referral codes, UTM standards, and dashboards across two instances
  • Own the source field on the RFQ form and the reporting line from first touch through quote issued to purchase order
  • Deliver a monthly dashboard and a quarterly review, both in revenue terms

Content Production

  • Produce short-form and long-form video, photography, and writing from the shop floor, the school, and the field. You operate the kit.
  • Ghost-write and schedule the CEO’s LinkedIn presence to an agreed cadence
  • Hold every clip to the on-camera safety standard and to a written export-control screen before it posts

Ambassador Program and Partners

  • Recruit, brief, and manage a contracted brand ambassador and content creator. Own the scorecard and the 45-day and 90-day reviews.
  • Coordinate our outside PR firm on placements, award announcements, and response, with the CEO approving all public statements

How You Will Be Measured

Thirteen fixed measures. Year one targets are set with the CEO inside your first 30 days, after you pull the baselines. Six of the thirteen:

  • Attributed RFQs that reach quote issued, and attributed RFQs that convert to purchase orders
  • Net revenue from branded products
  • Executed partnership and teaming agreements sourced through marketing
  • Marketing Contribution Ratio at or above 1.0 by day 180
  • Content cycle time of three business days or fewer from shoot to approved post
  • Export-control screening on shop-floor content at 100 percent, with no exceptions

You will see the full scorecard at the final interview, and it comes attached to the offer.

What This Role Does Not Own

We would rather tell you now than let you find out in month two.

  • Recruiting quotas, lead qualification, and enrollment decisions at the school
  • Grant writing and funder relationships
  • Donor CRM data entry and gift processing
  • Business development and program management on manufacturing contracts

Required Qualifications

  • Seven or more years of progressive marketing experience, including three or more years owning a marketing plan and budget with revenue accountability
  • Hands-on short-form video production and editing, with a portfolio of published work you produced yourself
  • Built marketing attribution from scratch in Salesforce or a comparable CRM: lead source discipline, campaign structure, dashboards
  • Owned a direct-to-consumer e-commerce site and its commercial results, including conversion rate, AOV, and the promotional calendar
  • Managed creators, influencers, or brand ambassadors under written agreements
  • Able to work onsite in San Diego five days per week, including shop-floor and field shoots
  • U.S. person status under ITAR (see Export control and eligibility)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Marketing across both a for-profit and a nonprofit audience, or inside an organization that runs both
  • Manufacturing, defense industrial base, aerospace, or skilled trades exposure
  • Military service or a military-connected background. Veterans are encouraged to apply.
  • Shopify and Klaviyo, or comparable commerce and lifecycle platforms
  • Product marketing for a physical product, including packaging and pricing
  • Ghost-writing for an executive

How We Work

VetPowered’s voice is irreverent, confident, blue-collar, and funny. The joke is on the work, the grind, the machine, the 0500 alarm. It is never on a customer, a service branch, or anyone’s identity.

Workshops for Warriors content is earnest, proud, and outcome-focused, written so a donor in Topeka and a command sergeant major at Camp Pendleton can both share it.

You will work inside real constraints. Shop-floor content passes a written export-control screen before it posts. Safety on camera is not negotiable. School outcome figures come from an approved metric sheet and nowhere else. Compensation for this role will never vary with student enrollments at the school, because federal law governing VA-approved institutions does not permit it.

If those constraints read as obstacles, this is the wrong job. If they read as the reason the work matters, keep reading.

Location, Schedule, and Travel

Onsite five days per week. Primary duty station is 2717 Boston Avenue, San Diego, with regular presence at the Workshops for Warriors campus at 2970 and 3030 Main Street. Remote and hybrid candidates will not be considered.

Travel is roughly 10 percent, mostly executive events, industry conferences, and field shoots, occasionally on short notice.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

You will work on an active manufacturing floor. Required personal protective equipment includes eye protection and hearing protection where posted. You should expect to lift and carry production equipment weighing up to 25 pounds, stand and walk for extended periods, kneel, and work at height from a ladder or lift to get a shot. The floor has machine noise, coolant mist, and metal chips. Reasonable accommodations are available for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Compensation and Benefits

$120,000 to $140,000 base salary, depending on experience. This is the full range we expect to pay for this position. No incentive compensation at hire. Any future bonus plan is tied to the measures above.

This is a full-time salaried (exempt) position (40+ hours/week).

Benefits and Perks: VetPowered makes comprehensive benefits available on the first of the month following the date of hire. Options include Medical (50% employer contribution), dental and vision coverage (100% employer contribution), a 401k program with employer match, 8 paid holidays, Flexible work hours (position dependent), and paid time off.

1. Strategic Leadership & Planning

  • Set the digital marketing and marketing operations strategy and annual/quarterly roadmap in partnership with the Director of Marketing, translating Malco’s growth goals into channel, systems, and resourcing priorities for this scope.
  • Own budget planning and investment recommendations for digital marketing and marketing operations — tooling, agencies, paid, and future headcount — and make the case for tradeoffs and new investment rather than simply executing a pre-set budget.
  • Act as the senior decision-maker for day-to-day digital and marketing-ops priorities and tradeoffs
  • Own vendor and agency selection and management within this scope (web development, SEO, paid social, martech platforms), including negotiating scope and holding partners accountable to results.

2. Website & Digital Experience

  • Own strategy, roadmap, and performance for all Malco web properties (DTC site(s), brand pages) — UX, conversion, and technical health.
  • Partner with agencies/developers on site builds, updates, and maintenance; act as the internal owner who sets priorities and evaluates output.
  • Ensure site content (product, technical, regulatory, label) stays synced with the PIM/knowledge base so what’s live on-site is always accurate.

3. SEO, AEO & Organic Discovery

  • Own Malco’s organic search and AI-search (AEO) strategy across brand and product content — the goal is that when detailers search or ask AI tools about detailing chemicals, Malco brands surface.
  • Conduct keyword, topic, and prompt research and translate it into a content and technical roadmap that Content Studio and this role execute against.
  • Own on-page and technical SEO (site structure, metadata, schema markup, page speed) and monitor how Malco content performs in AI answer engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) as that channel grows.
  • Own the architecture, configuration, and integrations of Malco’s marketing technology stack: website/CMS, digital asset management, content management, marketing automation (HubSpot, Klaviyo, or equivalent), project management (Asana), analytics, SEO tooling, and AI tooling.
  • Work alongside IT to support our product information management (PIM) infrastructure as the single source of truth for product copy, specifications, application data, regulatory/label content, and creative assets across Amazon, Shopify, distributor portals, sell sheets, and international markets.
  • Build and maintain integrations between systems — product data flowing from ERP to CMS to Amazon; assets flowing from DAM to email, social, and web; campaign data flowing from execution platforms to dashboards — and govern access, permissions, and data hygiene across all marketing platforms.
  • Own the architecture and configuration of marketing automation platforms — data model, segmentation logic, lifecycle flows, deliverability, and integrations.
  • Evaluate, recommend, and onboard new marketing technology as the team’s needs evolve.

5. AI Workflows & Knowledge Management

  • Build the prompt library, AI workflows, and automation systems that allow the marketing team to produce a high volume of on-brand content across four brands without proportional headcount growth.
  • Build and maintain Malco’s proprietary marketing knowledge base — brand voice, technical product knowledge, application expertise, competitive positioning, and regulatory language — as a structured, version-controlled system that AI workflows draw from.
  • Design the create-once, scale-everywhere workflow that turns a single video shoot, photo set, or product launch into ten or more channel-ready assets across web, social, email, distributor kits, and sales enablement.
  • Continuously test, refine, and document AI workflows; train the team to use them effectively without ceding editorial judgment.
  • Build the listening infrastructure that captures continuous signal from the professional detailing community — industry forums, social media, product reviews, search/AI-search trends, and competitor content.
  • Design systems for synthesizing field and distributor feedback into structured intelligence the marketing team acts on, and build competitive intelligence capabilities that track content, channel programs, product launches, and community building.
  • Build and maintain the technical infrastructure that gets marketing assets, product data, sales tools, and campaign content into distributor portals, syndication feeds, and partner systems.
  • Architect content and product data syndication so that new launches, updated specifications, and marketing campaigns flow to distributor channels without manual rekeying.
  • Partner with Sales Operations and IT on distributor-facing systems and CRM ownership where accountabilities overlap.

8. Performance Dashboards & Marketing Reporting

  • Build the marketing performance dashboard, including website and SEO/AEO performance alongside automation and distributor metrics.
  • Define and govern marketing key performance indicators and the data sources that feed them; instrument campaigns and channels so attribution is possible.
  • Surface insights rather than just numbers — the dashboard should tell a story without requiring extensive interpretation.
  • Assess team workload and make the case for a Marketing Operations/Digital Implementer or Junior Associate hire when volume justifies it; scope, interview, and onboard that hire once approved.
  • Build a team structure and workflow that stays lean without becoming a bottleneck as Malco scales

10. Internal Enablement & Documentation

  • Train the marketing team on the systems and workflows you build, and keep them clearly documented so the team can rely on them with confidence over time.
  • Be the internal expert the team turns to when a system, website, SEO, or social question blocks them.
  • Continuously identify opportunities to remove manual work and increase output through automation and AI.

Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Marketing, Operations, Business Systems, or related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Experience / Requirements:

  • 5+ years in a role spanning digital marketing and marketing operations/technology — website management, SEO, marketing automation, or a comparable systems-and-channel hybrid — ideally at a multi-brand or multi-channel consumer goods, B2B manufacturing, or DTC business.
  • Proven track record of setting and owning strategy for a function — not just executing against someone else's plan — including budget and investment recommendations, roadmap-setting, and prioritization tradeoffs.
  • Prior experience managing at least one direct report and/or agency/vendor relationships as the senior accountable owner.
  • Hands‑on experience owning a website/CMS (Shopify, WordPress, or equivalent), including content, UX, and conversion optimization.

  • Demonstrated experience building and deploying AI workflows for marketing content or operations at scale.
  • Hands‑on experience configuring and integrating marketing automation platforms (HubSpot, Klaviyo, Marketo, or equivalent).

About the Role

Our owned channels—push notifications, email, and reactivation campaigns—are our fastest levers for driving revenue, but they’re flying blind: we can’t track click-through on individual sends, attribute engagement across games, or even avoid spamming the same player three times for one campaign. You’ll be the one who builds the instrumentation to turn our messaging strategy from guesswork into a measured, optimized growth engine.

Responsibilities

  • Own email, push notification and in-app messaging as a single lifecycle function for Skillz Platform — strategy, calendar, execution and measurement.

  • Manage the Email Marketing Manager and build the lifecycle bench.

  • Report weekly: what was sent, what it earned, what is being retired, and what needs unblocking.

Key Competencies

  • Incrementality-first thinking — instinctively asks what the control group did; treats sends, opens and pMAU as inputs rather than results.
  • Lifecycle craft — journey design, triggers, frequency capping, suppression logic and deliverability, across push, email and in-app together rather than channel by channel.
  • Offer economics — understands that a reactivated user arriving on bonus cash can be NGR-negative, and can defend a step-down against a stakeholder whose reactivation number it depresses.
  • Hands-on tooling — configures journeys and segments themselves; can pull their own data in SQL or a BI tool.
  • Player respect — treats notification volume as a finite asset and argues for fewer, better sends.
  • Builds from zero — the function, the DL, the runbook and the measurement all need creating; comfortable with that rather than expecting an established machine.

Experience

  1. 6–10 years in lifecycle / CRM / retention marketing for a consumer mobile product, including direct ownership of a reactivation or win-back program.
  2. Deep hands-on experience with a lifecycle platform — CleverTap strongly preferred; Braze, MoEngage, Iterable or WebEngage acceptable — including journey building, segmentation and frequency management.
  3. Ran holdout-based incrementality measurement on messaging campaigns and can evidence a campaign they killed on the number.
  4. Real-money gaming, online gambling, fantasy sports, fintech or e-commerce with a wallet/deposit economy strongly preferred.
  5. Owned push notification deliverability and opt-in economics, including double-dialogue opt-in patterns and the constraints of iOS re-enablement.
  6. Comfortable partnering with Product on instrumentation gaps and with Analytics on independent scoring; experience taking over tooling ownership from another function is a plus.

Azurity Pharmaceuticals is a privately held, specialty pharmaceutical company that focuses on innovative products that meet the needs of underserved patients. As an industry leader in providing unique, accessible, and high-quality medications, Azurity leverages its integrated capabilities and vast partner network to continually expand its broad commercial product portfolio and robust late-stage pipeline. The company’s patient-centric products span the cardiovascular, neurology, endocrinology, gastro-intestinal, institutional, and orphan markets, and have benefited millions of patients. For more information, visit www.azurity.com.

Azurity Pharmaceuticals is proud to be an inclusive workplace and an Equal Opportunity Employer. Azurity's success is attributable to our incredibly talented, dedicated team that focuses on benefiting the lives of patients by bringing the best science and commitment to quality into everything that we do. We seek highly motivated individuals with the dedication, integrity, and creative spirit needed to thrive in our organization.

About the Role

Azurity Pharmaceuticals is a privately held specialty pharmaceutical company focused on innovative products that meet the needs of underserved patients. Within the Surgical Business Unit— our hospital-focused, targeted-delivery specialty business — we are preparing to launch D-PLEX100, a locally administered, extended-release surgical anti-infective for the prevention of surgical site infection.

We are seeking a Senior Manager, Brand Marketing to execute the account-facing and institutional marketing program for D-PLEX100 in the US. Reporting to the Head of Marketing-D-PLEX100 within the Surgical Business Unit, this individual develops the formulary and value-story tools, congress and KOL logistics, and account-facing materials that help move D-PLEX100 from institutional approval to protocol adoption. D-PLEX100 is an inpatient, DRG-reimbursed product whose adoption is governed at the account level by institutional Pharmacy & Therapeutics (P&T) committees, so institutional marketing works in close coordination with HCP demand generation and with Market Access/HEOR.

The ideal candidate brings a minimum of 5 years of US-based marketing experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry, with hospital, surgical, anti-infective, or other institutional/inpatient product experience preferred. This is a US-focused, execution-oriented role in a fast-paced, launch-stage environment that rewards a hands-on, collaborative contributor.

Key Responsibilities

Institutional Marketing & Execution

  • Develop and execute account-facing and institutional marketing materials for D-PLEX100 — formulary value tools, P&T submission support materials, and value-analysis-committee content — aligned to the brand strategy set by the Senior Director.
  • Manage day-to-day production of institutional campaigns and materials, ensuring timely development, medical/legal/regulatory review, and deployment.
  • Support monitoring of P&T and formulary access, protocol adoption, and account-level uptake, and surface insights to inform tactics.
  • Support primary and secondary market research with pharmacy, infection-prevention, and institutional decision-maker audiences to inform the value story.

Launch Planning & Readiness

  • Support cross-functional US launch readiness for D-PLEX100 and subsequent indications, contributing institutional-marketing deliverables to the integrated launch plan and readiness gates.
  • Help develop US launch materials, field and account-team tools, and training content, sequenced to regulatory approval and the reimbursement and coding milestones that gate the commercial model.
  • Coordinate institutional-access deliverables (formulary tools, P&T submission support, coding materials) with HCP demand generation so promotion and access readiness move together.
  • Partner with Medical Affairs, Market Access/HEOR, Regulatory, and external agencies to deliver high-quality, compliant promotional and educational content.

Product & Lifecycle Support

  • Prioritize and allocate institutional-marketing tactics and budget within the brand plan to maximize impact and return.
  • Support indication-expansion planning by developing institutional positioning and account-facing tools for new surgical settings as they advance.
  • Track the competitive and standard-of-care landscape — including infection-prevention bundles and protocol inertia — and surface implications for institutional tactics.
  • Work with sales training, commercial partners, and medical and legal teams to develop and implement commercial training for the franchise.

Stakeholder & Field Collaboration

  • Support alignment between marketing and the hospital field and account teams on institutional strategy and messaging.
  • Engage pharmacy, infection-prevention, and antimicrobial-stewardship stakeholders and KOLs to gather insight and inform the value story.
  • Manage congress and KOL logistics, and collaborate with external partners, agencies, and vendors to develop omnichannel campaigns tailored to institutional audiences.

Measures of Success

  • Execution: institutional materials and account tools are delivered on time, clear medical/legal/regulatory review, and are field- and account-ready at launch.
  • Access support: formulary and P&T submission tools are in place and used to support target-account access.
  • Coordination: institutional-access deliverables stay aligned with HCP demand generation so promotion and access readiness move together.
  • Quality: institutional messaging remains compliant and consistent across channels and materials.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Life Sciences, Business, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of US-based marketing / launch experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple brands, indications, or workstreams simultaneously in a fast-paced, evolving organization, with a hands-on, collaborative approach.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop marketing materials and manage them through medical/legal/regulatory review.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills.
  • Experience partnering with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Sales, and Regulatory on compliant promotional and educational content.
  • Willingness to travel ~20–30% (including conferences, sales meetings, and field rides).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hospital, surgical, anti-infective, or other institutional / inpatient product experience preferred.
  • Exposure to institutional access, formulary, or P&T marketing for a hospital-administered product.
  • Familiarity with inpatient DRG-reimbursed products and pharmacy / infection-prevention / antimicrobial-stewardship stakeholders.
  • Launch experience with an in-licensed or newly acquired asset.
  • Congress and KOL logistics experience.

  • Unlock Your Earning Potential: Join our team and be rewarded with a competitive compensation package, including an annual bonus based on company performance, that recognizes your exceptional talent.
    • Sales - In lieu of annual bonuses, we offer an Incentive compensation program that allows you to earn more - even over plan.
    • Fuel Your Success: *Sales Only* - We understand the value of your hard work and provide a car reimbursement program and gas card for both business and personal use as part of our commitment to supporting you.

  • Time Off That Counts: Take advantage of our generous time off policy, which offers up to 15 vacation days annually + rollover (up to 40 hours) as well as five sick/wellness days. For new employees, vacation accrual will be prorated based on your start date.
  • Meaningful Time with Your Loved Ones: We close between Christmas and New Year’s to give you an extra week off to spend quality time with your family and recharge.
  • Enjoy the Holidays: Over the course of the year, Azurity recognizes 13 holidays.
  • Invest in Your Education: We support your professional growth with tuition reimbursement for undergraduate and graduate level courses or certifications.
  • Recognize and Be Recognized: Our Azurity High Five peer recognition platform allows you to celebrate your colleagues’ accomplishments and receive recognition for your own outstanding work.

Unbound Now is ending human trafficking by identifying victims, supporting survivors, seeking justice, and leading system change. We are motivated by our faith in Jesus and work each day as individuals driven by hope, oriented towards service, and committed to excellence. Job Title: Digital Content & Marketing Manager


Job Status: Full-time, Exempt


Job Location: HQ - Ft. Worth, TX


Job Summary: The Digital Content & Marketing Manager supports the Communications team by executing Unbound Now's digital marketing and communications strategy. This role is responsible for creating and executing engaging content across social media, email marketing, graphic design, and website communications to increase brand awareness, strengthen community engagement, support fundraising efforts, and advance the organization's mission.

The ideal candidate is a creative storyteller, organized project manager, and collaborative communicator who enjoys bringing campaigns to life with compelling visuals, engaging copy, and strategic digital content while maintaining a consistent, recognizable brand.


Compensation: Annual salary


Benefits:  Unbound Now is proud to offer a premier benefits package that prioritizes the health and financial security of our team members and their families:

  • 100% Employer-Paid Health Insurance: We cover 100% of medical premiums for both the employee and their family. 
  • Employer-Paid Life Insurance: Fully covered for the employee at no cost.
  • Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with a 3% salary match (eligible after 90 days; 1-year vesting).
  • Dental & Vision: Comprehensive plans available at the employee’s expense.


Schedule/Availability: 8:30 a.m.-5:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, with a one-hour lunch break. Occasional weekends and evenings are required as needed.


Working conditions: Work is performed in a normal office environment or other professional environment. Work duties may, on rare occasions, be performed in an environment requiring exposure to weather extremes, fumes, odors, and noise. 


Travel: This position requires occasional travel in or out of state for training and/or office visits.


Responsibilities:

  • Execute the organization's digital marketing and communications strategy in collaboration with the Communications team. 
  • Implement annual, quarterly, and monthly communications calendars.
  • Coordinate and align messaging across social media, email marketing, website content, fundraising campaigns, and events.
  • Identify opportunities to increase audience engagement and strengthen the organization's digital presence.
  • Stay current on social media trends, emerging technologies, and nonprofit marketing best practices.
  • Manage the organization's social media platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, YouTube, and emerging platforms.
  • Create, schedule, publish, and optimize content across all digital channels.
  • Write engaging captions and calls to action that reflect the organization's voice.
  • Monitor comments and messages while fostering positive community engagement.
  • Support campaign execution through coordinated social media efforts.
  • Design digital and print marketing materials, including:
    • Social media graphics
    • Flyers and brochures
    • Event collateral
    • One-pagers
    • Infographics
    • Presentation materials
    • Fundraising and donor communications
    • Digital advertisements
  • Maintain brand standards and ensure visual consistency across all communications.
  • Develop and manage branded templates within Canva and Adobe Creative Suite.
  • Manage email marketing campaign execution that supports fundraising, donor stewardship, volunteer recruitment, advocacy, and organizational updates.
  • Build, schedule, and test email communications.
  • Monitor campaign performance, including open rates, click-through rates, and engagement metrics.
  • Write engaging copy for social media, email campaigns, website content, blogs, and marketing materials.
  • Capture and share stories that highlight the organization's impact, programs, donors, and community partners across digital channels. 
  • Ensure messaging aligns with established brand voice and organizational priorities.
  • Assist in updating website content, landing pages, and campaign materials as needed.
  • Coordinate website updates to support organizational initiatives and fundraising campaigns.
  • Ensure digital content is accurate, visually engaging, and aligned with brand standards.
  • Apply basic SEO best practices to improve discoverability.
  • Monitor digital performance across social media, email marketing, website traffic, and online campaigns.
  • Track key performance indicators, including audience growth, engagement, email performance, and campaign effectiveness.
  • Prepare monthly reports with insights and recommendations to improve future communications.
  • Work closely with the Director of Communications to execute strategic marketing initiatives.
  • Collaborate with Development, Regional Directors, Programs, and Leadership teams to support fundraising campaigns, events, volunteer recruitment, and organizational communications.
  • Assist with communications planning and project management for organizational initiatives.


Desired Outcomes:

  • Increased Engagement: Growth in donor, partner, and community engagement through compelling, consistent messaging across all channels.
  • Brand Consistency: All communications, print and digital, reflect Unbound Now’s brand voice, visual identity, and standards of clarity and excellence.
  • Survivor-Centered Messaging: Survivor input is consistently incorporated into communications, ensuring messaging is strengths-based, trauma-informed, and hope-filled.
  • Expanded Reach: Significant increase in social media presence, website traffic, and media coverage that elevates Unbound Now’s mission and impact.
  • Effective Campaigns: Successful execution of targeted campaigns that drive fundraising, advocacy, and program awareness goals.
  • Internal Alignment: Leadership and staff across offices have the tools and guidance needed to communicate effectively with stakeholders.
  • Positive Public Perception: Strengthened trust and credibility with stakeholders, resulting in increased support from donors, foundations, and partners.


Working Relationships:

Reports to: Director of Communications

Works with: HQ team,  Development team, and Regional Directors

Supervises:  Communication Interns


Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Graphic Design, Journalism, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Three or more years of experience in digital marketing, communications, or content creation.
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating graphic design, photography, videography, and content creation.
  • Excellent writing, editing, and storytelling skills.
  • Experience managing social media platforms and email marketing campaigns.
  • Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, Premiere Pro, CapCut, Lightroom, or similar creative software.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Ability to work collaboratively while managing day-to-day communications independently.

Preferred

  • Experience working in a nonprofit organization.
  • Experience supporting fundraising and donor engagement campaigns.
  • Familiarity with website content management systems (WordPress or similar).
  • Experience with email marketing platforms such as Virtuous, Constant Contact, HubSpot, or similar.
  • Working knowledge of Google Analytics, SEO, and digital marketing best practices.
  • Experience using AI-powered creative tools to enhance content development while maintaining brand standards.
  • Support larger video productions led by the Director of Communications or external creative partners.

Skills & Competencies

  • Skilled in building collaborative relationships across departments and with external partners.

Job Description

Vego Garden is making gardening as accessible and sustainable as possible, while encouraging gardening to be an avenue for personal and community development! 

Since its successful launch in 2020, Vego Garden has quickly become the leading brand in raised garden beds and one of the fastest-growing consumer brands in the country. In just five years, our rapid growth has led to the establishment of a 200,000-square-foot headquarters and distribution center, along with a beautiful 5-acre farm.

Today, Vego Garden proudly employs over 100 dedicated team members across the U.S. and internationally. Our high-quality raised garden beds are recognized for their durability, eco-friendly materials, and safety for both children and pets. We are proud to be partnering with Costco, ACE Hardware, Home Depot, Menards, Lowe’s, Wayfair, and Amazon.

We owe our success to our loyal customers and passionate team. Through our Vego Garden Kids and Giving Back Program, we have donated more than 3,500 garden beds to schools, underserved communities, and other philanthropic initiatives - helping to grow gardens and give back across the nation by making gardening easier anytime, anywhere! We're proud to be a certified Great Place to Work company!

Vego Garden Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, or marital status.

Job Purpose:

Vego Garden is looking for a Senior Retention Marketing Manager to lead existing customer growth and increase customer lifetime value.

You will own the retention strategy across the customer lifecycle—from turning first-time buyers into repeat customers to growing engagement, expanding category adoption, and reactivating lapsed customers. You will combine customer insights, lifecycle marketing, and rigorous experimentation to build lasting customer relationships and drive measurable, profitable growth.

This role requires both strategic thinking and hands-on execution, with accountability for repeat purchase behavior, existing customer revenue, and long-term customer value.

Essential Responsibilities:

Retention Strategy & Existing Customer Growth

  • Build and execute a retention roadmap that increases repeat purchase rate, purchase frequency, cross-category adoption, and customer lifetime value.
  • Identify the highest-impact opportunities across onboarding, second-purchase conversion, cross-sell, loyalty, and win-back.
  • Develop customer journeys that reflect gardening seasonality, product ownership, and customers’ evolving needs.
  • Partner with the Growth Director to set retention goals, prioritize investments, and forecast existing customer revenue.

Lifecycle Marketing & Customer Experience

  • Own the strategy and execution of email, SMS, and other relevant lifecycle channels, including automated journeys and promotional campaigns.
  • Build segmented, personalized experiences based on purchase history, engagement, customer value, and lifecycle stage.
  • Strengthen post-purchase journeys through product education, timely recommendations, and content that helps customers succeed in their gardens.
  • Manage the retention calendar, balancing education, product discovery, seasonal demand, and promotional activity.
  • Establish strong standards for deliverability, audience health, consent, and communication frequency.

Customer Insights, Measurement & Experimentation

  • Analyze customer cohorts to understand repeat purchase patterns, time to second purchase, category progression, and lapse risk.
  • Build reporting that connects retention activity to customer behavior, revenue, and profitability.
  • Run structured experiments across messaging, offers, timing, segmentation, and customer journeys.
  • Use holdouts and incrementality testing where appropriate to distinguish additional revenue from purchases that would have happened anyway.
  • Turn customer feedback and performance insights into clear recommendations for marketing, merchandising, and customer experience.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner with acquisition teams to improve customer quality and connect first-purchase campaigns with long-term value.
  • Work with Creative, Content, Merchandising, E-commerce, and Customer Experience to deliver cohesive customer journeys.
  • Shape loyalty and referral initiatives based on customer needs and business economics.
  • Manage relevant agency, platform, and contractor relationships to support execution.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in retention, lifecycle, CRM, or customer marketing, including ownership of retention programs for a DTC or e-commerce business.
  • A demonstrated track record of improving repeat purchase behavior, existing customer revenue, or customer lifetime value.
  • Hands-on expertise with email and SMS platforms such as Klaviyo or comparable tools, including automation, segmentation, testing, and reporting.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience using cohort analysis and customer data to prioritize growth opportunities.
  • A clear understanding of contribution margin, promotional economics, and the trade-offs between short-term revenue and long-term customer value.
  • The ability to translate customer insights into compelling messaging, relevant offers, and thoughtful lifecycle experiences.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and project management skills.
  • Comfort moving between strategy, execution, and performance analysis in a fast-paced environment.

Nice to Have
  • Experience in gardening, home, outdoor living, or other categories with seasonal demand and longer purchase cycles.
  • Experience with Shopify, loyalty platforms, customer data tools, or subscription programs.
  • Experience designing incrementality tests or working with BI tools and SQL.
  • A personal interest in gardening and helping customers build confidence as they grow.

Physical Demands:

This position primarily involves working at a desk and operating a computer for prolonged periods with moderate walking and standing.

Job Location and Work Schedule:

  • This is a full-time position based out of Tomball, TX.
  • Work Arrangement: Hybrid schedule with one remote workday and four days onsite per week.
  • 13808 Boudreaux Road, Bldg. #2, Tomball, TX 77377.
  • Monday through Friday.
  • 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. Lunch break 12:00 pm to 12:30 pm.

Benefits

  • The salary range is $80,000 - $110,000.
  • Flexible Paid Time Off.
  • 12 PTO days per year, accrued bi-weekly, with incremental increases annually.
  • 7 paid Holidays.
  • 401k contribution match of 4%.
  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life insurance plans. The Company pays 100% of premiums for its employees for Dental, Vision, Life, and select Medical plans.
  • Toll Roads Allowance of $100 per month for hybrid employees.
  • Phone Allowance of $50 per month.
  • Professional Development reimbursement.
  • Company-sponsored breakfasts and lunches.
  • We offer great culture, supportive leadership, engaging activities, employee appreciation, and other perks that make every day at work more rewarding!
