About New Western

 

New Western has been named a Glassdoor Best Place to Work three years in a row (2023, 2024, 2025). We are a leading real estate investment marketplace specializing in sourcing distressed residential properties for investors. Operating in nearly 50 markets across 20 states, our innovative approach revitalizes neighborhoods, creates affordable housing options, and addresses the housing supply crisis. Join us to make a meaningful impact on the real estate market while contributing to a collaborative, mission-driven team.

Role Description

We’re looking for a hands-on Demand Generation Marketing Manager who thrives at the intersection of strategy, analytics, execution, and people leadership.

This is a marketing operations and demand generation role — not a creative or brand marketing position. The ideal candidate is a business-minded marketer who understands how marketing activity translates into pipeline, revenue, and business results. They are equally comfortable digging into performance data, evaluating how marketing dollars are invested, communicating insights to executive leadership, and rolling up their sleeves to get work done.

Think of this person as a business athlete and player-coach: highly organized, analytical, collaborative, adaptable, and driven to deliver results. They can zoom out to develop strategy and zoom in to troubleshoot campaign performance, improve processes, manage projects, or coach a team member through execution.

Success in this role requires strong judgment, curiosity, accountability, and the ability to connect marketing performance to broader business priorities across multiple markets. The right person will bring structure to complexity, turn data into decisions, and continuously improve how demand generation programs are planned, measured, and optimized.

If you enjoy analyzing what’s working, understanding where marketing dollars are going, building better systems, developing people, and solving problems alongside your team, this role is built for you.

ON-SITE POSITION MON-FRI, IRVING, TX

Core Responsibilities
  • Lead, coach, and develop a small team of approximately 3–5 marketing professionals, balancing people leadership with hands-on involvement in execution.
  • Own demand generation performance across campaigns and initiatives, monitoring KPIs and identifying opportunities to improve lead generation, conversion, efficiency, and overall marketing contribution.
  • Dig into marketing performance data to understand what is working, what isn’t, and why — translating findings into clear actions and recommendations.
  • Evaluate and manage marketing investments, ensuring marketing dollars are allocated thoughtfully based on performance, business priorities, and market-specific needs.
  • Communicate marketing performance and insights to executive leadership, providing clear, concise recommendations that support business and investment decisions.
  • Partner cross-functionally with senior leadership and teams across the organization to align demand generation priorities with business objectives.
  • Translate strategic priorities into clear plans, projects, timelines, owners, and measurable outcomes.
  • Manage external marketing partners, agencies, technology providers, and vendors, holding partners accountable for performance and deliverables.
  • Establish and improve marketing processes, systems, reporting, and workflows that increase efficiency, visibility, and accountability.
  • Ensure campaigns and projects are executed accurately, on time, and against defined performance objectives.
  • Remove obstacles and solve problems quickly, while remaining actively involved in the day-to-day work of the team.
  • Balance competing priorities and adapt quickly as business needs, market conditions, and performance data change.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and results.
  • Use data and business context — not assumptions — to make decisions and recommend where marketing resources should be focused.
  •  
Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • 3–5+ years of progressive marketing experience, ideally with significant exposure to demand generation, marketing operations, performance marketing, or revenue-focused marketing.
  • Demonstrated experience leading, coaching, and developing a small team while remaining hands-on.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to interpret marketing performance data, identify trends, and translate insights into practical business recommendations.
  • Experience managing marketing budgets, investments, campaigns, or programs and understanding the relationship between spend, performance, and business outcomes.
  • Exceptional project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, timelines, and deliverables simultaneously.
  • Strong business acumen and the ability to connect marketing activity to broader organizational goals.
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present performance, insights, and recommendations to executive leadership.
  • Proven ability to collaborate effectively across functions and influence stakeholders without relying solely on direct authority.
  • Comfortable balancing strategic thinking with detailed, hands-on execution.
  • Strong judgment, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to bring structure to complex or evolving environments.
  • A results-oriented, accountable mindset with a bias toward action and continuous improvement.
  • Comfortable receiving direct feedback, being coached, and operating in a high-performance, high-accountability environment.
  • Adaptable, resilient, curious, and energized by changing priorities.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a high-growth, multi-market, or performance-driven organization.
  • Experience in real estate or a real estate-adjacent business.
  • Experience with marketing automation, CRM, analytics, attribution, reporting, or other marketing technology.
  • Experience partnering closely with sales, operations, finance, or other revenue-focused functions.
  • Graduate-level degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or another related field.
What Success Looks Like

In this role, success means:

  • Marketing performance is visible, measurable, and understood.
  • Marketing dollars are invested based on data, business priorities, and expected return — not simply historical spending.
  • Executive leadership has clear visibility into what marketing is delivering and where opportunities exist.
  • Demand generation programs continuously improve based on performance insights.
  • Projects move forward with clear ownership, accountability, and timelines.
  • The marketing team is well coached, organized, and equipped to deliver.
  • Processes and systems make the team more efficient without adding unnecessary complexity.
  • The organization views marketing as a strategic business function and measurable growth driver.

Professional, customer‑focused, and partner‑centric approach with a demonstrated ability to establish trust, drive engagement, and support mutually beneficial business relationships. Company Description

Sea to Summit is an award-winning Australian brand in the outdoor industry. We design, manufacture, and distribute innovative, meticulously engineered outdoor equipment for adventures at every altitude.

We are a motivated group of experienced, creative, and forward-thinking professionals connected by a shared passion for creating frictionless gear so people can enjoy limitless adventures.

Job Description

TheSenior Retail Marketing Manager is the strategic lead for Sea to Summit's North American retail go-to-market (GTM) programme. This role owns the retail GTM calendar and process end-to-end from seasonal strategy alignment through to in-season execution and is responsible for translating brand and commercial priorities into retail marketing plans that drive sell-in and sell-through across independent and key account channels.

This is a commercially minded role that requires the ability to think strategically, plan ahead of the business, and direct available resources including field sales representatives, tech reps, and sales agents to deliver results at scale. The Retail Marketing Manager works closely with Sales and Marketing leadership, the global brand team based in Perth, Australia, and cross-functional partners across E-Commerce, Operations, and Finance.

  • Own the North American retail GTM calendar, including all planning milestones, approval gates, and cross-functional dependencies from seasonal strategy alignment through to in-season support.
  • Lead seasonal retail marketing strategy aligned with commercial priorities, account segmentation, and global brand direction identifying key moments, tools, and resource requirements well in advance of execution.
  • Partner with Sales leadership on account segmentation and translate account tiers into differentiated marketing support plans.
  • Contribute North American perspective to the global planning cadence, including asset handoffs, seasonal share-backs, and planning cycle inputs.

Key Account Marketing

  • Develop bespoke marketing plans for priority key accounts, working alongside account reps and sales leadership to align marketing investment with account opportunity.
  • Build retail marketing pitch decks and sell-in support tools tailored to key and focus accounts.
  • Integrate into key account planning meetings and ensure marketing timelines are aligned to commercial calendars.
  • Evaluate and evolve key account programmes including fixture programmes, window contests, and digital co-op based on performance data and rep feedback.

Foundational Merchandising & Retail Activation

  • Own the Authorised Dealer Kit programme and foundational merchandising approach for all Sea to Summit retail doors, with particular focus on new account activation.
  • Manage POP/POS planning, production, and distribution briefing regional production timelines and coordinating with global on asset development.
  • Direct tech reps, sales agents, and field resources to execute in-store merchandising, clinic programmes, and retail activations.
  • Support retail staff training and readiness to sell, including clinic kit coordination and ExpertVoice programme management.
  • Own North American tradeshow planning and activation, applying a prioritisation framework to determine appropriate investment level for each show.
  • Develop show-specific messaging strategy and brief creative on booth assets, activations, and collateral needs with appropriate lead times.

Qualifications

  • 5–7 years of progressive experience in retail marketing, trade marketing, or brand marketing with demonstrated ownership of strategy and execution.
  • Proven track record owning a retail or trade marketing calendar and managing cross-functional projects from planning through delivery.
  • Experience working with wholesale or independent retail channels; outdoor, sporting goods, or adjacent consumer goods industry experience preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to direct and activate field resources, agency partners, or sales teams to execute rather than defaulting to doing it themselves.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritise across competing demands and operate with a sense of urgency.
  • Ability to perform quantitative analysis on campaign and programme performance and translate data into actionable recommendations.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to present effectively to retail partners, sales leadership, and senior stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite; Adobe Creative Cloud experience (Photoshop, InDesign, Illustrator) a plus.
  • Familiarity with ClickUp, Klaviyo, and B2B platforms such as Elastic advantageous.
  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Marketing, or a related field; equivalent experience considered

Additional Information

Why Join Sea to Summit?

USD $125k - $135k annually

This is a full-time, office-based position located in Broomfield, Colorado. This position comes with a comprehensive benefits package including health insurance (medical, dental, vision), retirement match, employee assistance programmes, paid time off, community service leave, paid holidays, wellness stipend, gear allowance, and some other great perks. Occasional travel is required for tradeshows, retailer visits, and consumer events.

If you’re passionate about people and thrive in a dynamic environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Dataiku is the Platform for AI Success, the enterprise orchestration layer for building, deploying, and governing AI. In a single environment, teams design and operate analytics, machine learning, and AI agents with the transparency, collaboration, and control enterprises require. Sitting above data platforms, cloud infrastructure, and AI services, Dataiku connects the full enterprise AI stack - empowering organizations to run AI across multi-vendor environments with centralized governance.

The world's leading companies rely on Dataiku to operationalize AI and run it as a true business performance engine delivering measurable value. For more, visit the Dataiku blog , LinkedIn , X , and YouTube .

About the role

Dataiku is the platform for AI Success, helping organizations put AI to work across their business. The Growth team drives pipeline generation globally through paid media, content syndication, ABM, and marketing operations, and we're looking for a Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing to build and own the lifecycle function end to end.

You'll work closely with the VP of Digital & Growth and cross-functional partners across Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success, supporting a global organization across regions. We don't have a lifecycle function today. Email and nurture are secondary responsibilities inside other teams' jobs, so nobody owns what a prospect or customer hears from us, in what order, or how often. There are existing nurture workflows without a current owner and no single view of what runs where, so establishing that visibility is the first priority. You'll build the function from there: the strategy, the systems, the programs, and the team.

What you'll own

The lifecycle operating system

  • One authoritative email and lifecycle calendar across prospect, new-user and customer programs: what goes out, to whom, from which team, and when.
  • Frequency governance, suppression logic and deliverability standards, including being able to say how much of an audience a given send reaches.
  • Segmentation and audience standards, set with the web and marketing ops teams who manage list creation today.
  • A standard for what a lifecycle program needs before it launches: entry criteria, success metric, exit.

Prospect and new-user nurture

  • New-user onboarding and activation nurture: the sequences that move a first touch to an engaged, sales-ready account.
  • Account progression communication: the programs that move accounts from first engagement toward qualified opportunity.
  • Nurture designed around named-account cohorts, built alongside the integrated campaign work so the two don't duplicate each other.
  • Visibility for BDRs into what a lead has already received before they reach out.

Customer lifecycle, retention and expansion

You'll partner closely with Customer Success and Product on this.

  • Programmatic customer nurture: adoption, education, and the sequences that keep users active after initial deployment.
  • Retention and expansion programs, built on account signals rather than calendar cadence.

Automation, data and measurement

  • The lifecycle layer of the marketing automation stack end to end: HubSpot workflows, Salesforce integration, and account and intent data from 6sense.
  • Consolidating the existing nurture workflows into something documented and maintained.
  • Reporting lifecycle contribution in terms the business already uses: engagement progression, influenced pipeline, retention and expansion. You'll build your own reporting rather than wait for a dashboard.
  • The data quality this function depends on, with marketing ops: deliverability, consent, record hygiene.

AI and agentic workflows

  • Lifecycle work inside agentic workflows, rather than AI as a separate experiment. Lifecycle is one of the clearest applications: audience assembly, copy variation, program QA, performance summaries.
  • A standard for what a well-built lifecycle agent looks like, and where human in the loop is required.

Building the function

  • This is the lead role for a function that doesn't exist yet. You'll build the team as the function develops.
  • Getting the rest of the organization aligned on what you're building. Lifecycle touches Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success.

What you bring

  • 6+ years in lifecycle, nurture, email or growth marketing in B2B, ideally enterprise software with long, multi-threaded buying cycles.
  • Hands-on marketing automation depth. You've built and owned complex nurture programs yourself. HubSpot or Marketo depth, Salesforce fluency, and real comfort with the data model under both.
  • Command of deliverability, frequency capping, suppression, consent and list hygiene. This role exists partly because nobody has owned these.
  • Experience on both sides of the lifecycle, prospect and customer. If your background covers one, tell us how you'd approach the other.
  • Fluency with intent and account data (6sense, Demandbase or similar), and a view on where it should drive program entry rather than only reporting.
  • Comfort building with AI, expected rather than optional. No engineering background needed. You should already be using LLMs in your own work, with a view on where they belong in lifecycle programs and where human in the loop is required.
  • Analytical strength. You can define a metric, instrument it, and defend it, including when the honest answer is that the current number isn't reliable.
  • Comfort with a build role: ambiguity, direct conversations about tradeoffs, and establishing a function through influence before you have a team.
  • Experience working across regions in a global organization.
  • Excellent written English. Other languages welcome, not required.

Why this role

Lifecycle is unowned at Dataiku today. This role defines it, reporting to the VP who owns the function, with a mandate to build the team behind it.

About the role

Dataiku is the platform for AI Success, helping organizations put AI to work across their business. The Growth team drives pipeline generation globally through paid media, content syndication, ABM, and marketing operations, and we're looking for a Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing to build and own the lifecycle function end to end.

You'll work closely with the VP of Digital & Growth and cross-functional partners across Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success, supporting a global organization across regions. We don't have a lifecycle function today. Email and nurture are secondary responsibilities inside other teams' jobs, so nobody owns what a prospect or customer hears from us, in what order, or how often. There are existing nurture workflows without a current owner and no single view of what runs where, so establishing that visibility is the first priority. You'll build the function from there: the strategy, the systems, the programs, and the team.

What you'll own

The lifecycle operating system

  • One authoritative email and lifecycle calendar across prospect, new-user and customer programs: what goes out, to whom, from which team, and when.
  • Frequency governance, suppression logic and deliverability standards, including being able to say how much of an audience a given send reaches.
  • Segmentation and audience standards, set with the web and marketing ops teams who manage list creation today.
  • A standard for what a lifecycle program needs before it launches: entry criteria, success metric, exit.

Prospect and new-user nurture

  • New-user onboarding and activation nurture: the sequences that move a first touch to an engaged, sales-ready account.
  • Account progression communication: the programs that move accounts from first engagement toward qualified opportunity.
  • Nurture designed around named-account cohorts, built alongside the integrated campaign work so the two don't duplicate each other.
  • Visibility for BDRs into what a lead has already received before they reach out.

Customer lifecycle, retention and expansion

You'll partner closely with Customer Success and Product on this.

  • Programmatic customer nurture: adoption, education, and the sequences that keep users active after initial deployment.
  • Retention and expansion programs, built on account signals rather than calendar cadence.

Automation, data and measurement

  • The lifecycle layer of the marketing automation stack end to end: HubSpot workflows, Salesforce integration, and account and intent data from 6sense.
  • Consolidating the existing nurture workflows into something documented and maintained.
  • Reporting lifecycle contribution in terms the business already uses: engagement progression, influenced pipeline, retention and expansion. You'll build your own reporting rather than wait for a dashboard.
  • The data quality this function depends on, with marketing ops: deliverability, consent, record hygiene.

AI and agentic workflows

  • Lifecycle work inside agentic workflows, rather than AI as a separate experiment. Lifecycle is one of the clearest applications: audience assembly, copy variation, program QA, performance summaries.
  • A standard for what a well-built lifecycle agent looks like, and where human in the loop is required.

Building the function

  • This is the lead role for a function that doesn't exist yet. You'll build the team as the function develops.
  • Getting the rest of the organization aligned on what you're building. Lifecycle touches Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success.

What you bring

  • 6+ years in lifecycle, nurture, email or growth marketing in B2B, ideally enterprise software with long, multi-threaded buying cycles.
  • Hands-on marketing automation depth. You've built and owned complex nurture programs yourself. HubSpot or Marketo depth, Salesforce fluency, and real comfort with the data model under both.
  • Command of deliverability, frequency capping, suppression, consent and list hygiene. This role exists partly because nobody has owned these.
  • Experience on both sides of the lifecycle, prospect and customer. If your background covers one, tell us how you'd approach the other.
  • Fluency with intent and account data (6sense, Demandbase or similar), and a view on where it should drive program entry rather than only reporting.
  • Comfort building with AI, expected rather than optional. No engineering background needed. You should already be using LLMs in your own work, with a view on where they belong in lifecycle programs and where human in the loop is required.
  • Analytical strength. You can define a metric, instrument it, and defend it, including when the honest answer is that the current number isn't reliable.
  • Comfort with a build role: ambiguity, direct conversations about tradeoffs, and establishing a function through influence before you have a team.
  • Experience working across regions in a global organization.
  • Excellent written English. Other languages welcome, not required.

Why this role

Lifecycle is unowned at Dataiku today. This role defines it, reporting to the VP who owns the function, with a mandate to build the team behind it.

About Clipboard

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.


Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

NOTE: This is an active job posting for US candidates. There is a separate posting for non-US candidates on the Clipboard Careers page.

Role overview:

The Collections Account Manager (CAM) role is a critical role on the Billing team here at Clipboard, and this team ensures the successful management of billing processes for our biggest and most valuable workplace customers, who tend to also be more complex and risky. You will be a vital resource for workplaces, resolving billing issues, maintaining accurate invoicing, and managing financial relationships. Your responsibilities include:

  • Managing a portfolio of accounts, addressing billing concerns and ensuring timely invoice payments.

  • Conducting high volumes of outbound calls to connect with customers about past-due account balances and resolve them.

  • Navigating negotiations and evaluate tradeoffs between risk mitigation and growth potential when making decisions.

  • Resolving customer invoice disputes and other billing-related issues.

  • Managing customer payments and remittances.

  • Building trust with providers and healthcare executives through strong financial acumen.

  • Clearly articulating the billing processes and educate stakeholders on invoicing procedures.

  • Gathering and relaying feedback to improve billing systems and processes.

  • Collaborating with internal teams to execute billing-related initiatives and trials.

Quick background on Billing:

There’s much to explain to paint the full picture of the Billing machine, but ultimately the core goal is to optimize the speed with which our customers pay us while maintaining their overall experience with us as a vendor. We want to collect money as fast as possible and minimize losses, while preserving the customer experience, in service of reliably converting revenue into cash (the lifeline of a capital-intensive business like ours). This in a way is “ensuring high-quality growth” for the company.

Although Clipboard provides a service where workplaces can find qualified professionals to fill shifts, we are in many ways a lending company at our core since we pay professionals immediately after they work a shift. For illustrative purposes: a nurse works a shift → we pay the nurse $100 immediately with our cash → the workplace pays us $120 a month later. We extend debt to workplaces using cash we borrow, with interest, from an Asset-Backed Line (ABL) of credit – workplaces use that debt to pay their staffing costs, and we expect to be paid back by the workplaces at a later date based on agreed-upon net terms.

The point is: Billing is doing the critical work of actually converting our revenue into cash that we put in the bank. Otherwise, money we cannot collect is money we’ve burned. We consistently fight a multi-faceted battle: a battle wherein we must maximize the speed at which we recognize revenue, maximize the margin associated with each shift, and maximize the customer experience, all without letting one unduly impact the other. Optimizing collections is critical to make sure Clipboard is generating sustainable, high-quality growth and turning top-line revenue into cash that we use to service or grow other parts of the business.

Though the CAM role lives in the realm of finance and numbers, you don’t need to be skilled in finance or accounting – while it’d be a plus, we expect you to learn the basics along the way.

Success factors for this role:

  • Extreme ownership: Take full responsibility for managing billing issues and solutions.

  • Curiosity: Investigate and understand the root cause of billing problems so that you can identify the best solution.

  • Scrappiness: Find innovative solutions to overcome obstacles and maintain progress.

  • Adaptability: Thrive in a fast-paced, evolving market.

Benefits:

  • Competitive pay

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Fully remote

  • Opportunity to make a significant impact with healthcare customers

Hiring plan:

  1. Application

  2. Case Study

  3. Interview 1

  4. Interview 2

  5. Offer!

System requirements:

To succeed in this role, you must have:

  • A reliable laptop/desktop (no Chromebooks or Linux OS).

  • Minimum 20 Mbps wired internet connection.

  • Wired headset for clear communication.

  • A quiet, distraction-free workspace.

  • Stable power and internet connectivity.

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here.

Description

At Macmillan Learning, we're committed to driving innovation that transforms education. We seek team members who thrive on pushing boundaries, envisioning future possibilities, and building solutions that make a lasting impact. Whether you're a Pioneer shaping bold new ideas, a Builder turning possibilities into reality, or a Stabilizer optimizing for success, you'll play a vital role in advancing our mission. If you're excited by the prospect of testing new technologies, implementing transformative strategies, and thriving in a fast-paced, innovative environment, we'd love to hear from you!

Every renewal season, instructors and institutions decide whether to keep using Macmillan Learning's materials and that decision usually comes down to a relationship, not a reminder email.

As an Account Manager, you'll own that relationship for a portfolio of accounts. You'll get to know what each customer is actually trying to accomplish, keep ahead of renewal risk instead of reacting to it, and find real opportunities to grow how they use our products, not just close a transaction. You'll work closely with Sales, Customer Success, and Customer Support so that from the customer's side, it feels like one coordinated team, not a series of handoffs.

This role suits someone who's comfortable managing a broad book of business, likes being the person who actually knows their accounts, and can move between relationship-building and day-to-day account management without losing track of either.

We know some talented people hesitate to apply when they don't check every box on a list. If this role has you excited and you believe you could do the work well, we want to hear from you, even if your path here doesn't match every requirement exactly. We're looking for people who care about our mission and bring their own perspective to the table. Different backgrounds, skills, and ways of working make us better at what we do. If this opportunity speaks to you, tell us how your experience and abilities could add value here. We want Macmillan Learning to be a place where everyone can do their best work and where different viewpoints are genuinely welcome, so if you're a qualified candidate, we hope you'll apply. We're looking forward to learning what you'd bring to the team.

This is a remote, work-from-home position. You will cover the Kansas City metro area (Kansas/Missouri), as well as Missouri, Chicago, Madison, Milwaukee, Minnesota, and Iowa. We prefer candidates who reside within the territory; however, residence within these locations is not required.

What You'll Do

Own the relationship. Build trust with faculty, decision-makers, and other stakeholders across your accounts, going beyond a single point of contact to understand curriculum, buying processes, and priorities at an organizational level.

Protect and grow the business. Track account health, spot renewal risk early, and act on it before it becomes a problem. Identify where current customers could benefit from more of what Macmillan Learning offers, including additional courses, departments, or products, and partner with Sales on larger opportunities.

Bring the customer's voice inside. Share what you're hearing, including feedback, competitive intelligence, and shifts in the market or in higher ed, with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success, and use it to sharpen your own account strategy.

Help customers get value, not just access. Partner with Customer Success and Support to make sure customers are actually using and benefiting from what they've adopted.

Coordinate across teams. Work with Sales, Customer Success, Support, Marketing, and Product so priorities, risks, and commitments don't get lost between departments, and lead internal reviews for your more complex or strategically important accounts.

Keep the operational side accurate. Maintain account plans, CRM data, and forecasts that are current enough to actually be useful for prioritizing your time.

  • Bachelor's degree
  • 3+ years of experience in account management, customer success, sales, relationship management, or another customer-facing role
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with multiple stakeholders at once
  • Strong communication, presentation, organization, and time-management skills
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously
  • Sound business judgment and problem-solving skills
  • Comfort using data and customer insight to guide decisions and priorities
  • Experience working collaboratively across multiple teams

Nice to Have

  • You live within the geographic boundaries of this sales region
  • Experience in educational technology, higher education, publishing, or a related industry
  • Experience managing a book of business with retention and/or revenue responsibility
  • Experience selling or supporting SaaS, digital learning products, or other technology-enabled solutions
  • Familiarity with account planning, forecasting, CRM systems, and business reviews
  • Experience working with faculty, academic leaders, administrators, or institutional decision-makers

About the Role

ID.me is looking for a Senior Manager, Revenue Accounting & Billing Operations to own our revenue and billing function end-to-end as we scale toward IPO readiness. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Accounting & Financial Operations, you'll own the full order-to-cash cycle — from how a deal is structured and booked in Salesforce, through usage capture and invoicing, to revenue recognition, deferred revenue, AR, and the monthly close.

This is a builder role for someone who wants to fix the system, not just operate it.

This is a builder's role. We've grown quickly across multiple verticals, and there's real opportunity now to design the billing and revenue infrastructure that carries us through our next stage of scale. You'll lead that build: automating billing vertical by vertical, partnering with Revenue Operations and the Salesforce team to get data right at the source, and working with the Data team to own the integrity and efficiency of the billing data pipeline. You'll also work directly with the leadership team to get full value from the finance systems we already own, and to design the data structure that makes reporting, analysis, and operating metrics automatic rather than assembled by hand. If you like leaving a process meaningfully better than you found it — and having the autonomy and support to do it — this is that role.

You’ll lead a team of three and be expected to bring ideas and then execute them. We want someone who is proactive, comfortable getting into the weeds of a usage file or a Salesforce field definition, and equally comfortable presenting a recognition position or an automation roadmap to leadership. Deep experience with revenue recognition in a usage-based or consumption-based billing model is essential; this is the core complexity of our business.

This position works from one of our officesMountain View, CA, McLean, VA, New York. NY office five days per week.

Key Responsibilities

Own the end-to-end revenue and billing cycle

  • Own the full order-to-cash cycle — deal booking and contract intake, usage and consumption data capture, invoicing, collections support, revenue recognition, deferred revenue, and AR — across all verticals and product lines.
  • Own revenue recognition for usage-based arrangements, including variable consideration, minimum commitments and overages, tiered and volume pricing, true-ups, and breakage, and author the ASC 606 memos that document and support those positions.
  • Own the monthly and quarterly revenue close, including journal entries, reconciliations, the ASC 606 revenue sub-ledger (subscription, usage, professional services, billing), revenue-by-customer/vertical schedules, and month-over-month fluctuation analysis.
  • Own billing accuracy and timeliness across verticals, including invoice preparation and review, customer billing inquiries, dispute resolution, and collections partnership.
  • Support external audits as the primary revenue and billing point of contact, and lead revenue-related SOX and IPO readiness — control design, documentation, and testing support.

Automate it — vertical by vertical

  • Lead the accounting automation roadmap for revenue and billing: identify the highest-effort manual processes, build the business case, and deliver the automation — hands‑on, not just as a project sponsor.
  • Automate billing end-to-end for every vertical, eliminating spreadsheet‑based and manual invoicing in favor of systematic, auditable, scalable processes.
  • Partner with the Senior Director to optimize the finance tool stack we already own (NetSuite, NetSuite ARM, Salesforce, Snowflake, Sigma, and Closing tool)— getting full value from existing investments before adding new systems, and leading evaluation when a gap is real.
  • Apply AI tools (Claude) to revenue, billing, and close workflows, and serve as a subject matter expert for AI adoption across the accounting team.

Fix the data, upstream

  • Partner with Revenue Operations and the Salesforce team to enforce data hygiene at the source — define the required fields, validation rules, and booking standards needed for clean recognition and billing, and push back on deal and booking practices that create downstream cleanup.
  • Partner with the Data team to own billing data integrity and efficiency, including usage data completeness and accuracy, reconciliation between source systems and the billing engine, and the controls that prove it.
  • Build the data structure the organization needs — consistent customer, product, vertical, and contract dimensions — so revenue reporting, analysis, and operating metrics can be generated automatically rather than assembled by hand.
  • Review deal structures with Sales, Revenue Operations, and Legal before close, so recognition and billing treatment is settled upfront rather than discovered during close.

Lead the team

  • Manage and develop the revenue team, setting priorities, raising the technical bar, and building a function that scales with transaction volume and deal complexity.
  • Be a thought leader for the broader team: bring ideas about how the close, the controls, and the reporting should work, and then own the execution.
  • Be a team player — support the growth of peers across accounting and financial operations, and step in where the team needs help, including outside your direct scope.
  • Own revenue accounting and billing policy, keeping it current with new accounting standards, new pricing models, and new verticals or product lines.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance
  • 8+ years of progressive revenue accounting experience, including at least 2 years directly managing accounting staff
  • Deep expertise in ASC 606 and SaaS revenue recognition, with direct, hands‑on experience recognizing revenue in a usage-based or consumption‑based billing model (variable consideration, minimums and overages, tiered pricing, true‑ups)
  • Demonstrated ownership of an end‑to‑end billing or order‑to‑cash process, not just the accounting entries
  • Track record of delivering accounting automation — specific processes you identified, designed, and shipped, with measurable reduction in manual effort or close time
  • Experience working directly with Revenue Operations, Salesforce administrators, or Data/Engineering teams on data quality, system configuration, or data pipelines
  • Advanced proficiency with financial systems (NetSuite, NetSuite ARM, Salesforce) and advanced Excel skills, including comfort working with large data sets
  • Demonstrated proficiency with AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) to drive accounting process improvement
  • Proactive operator — brings problems forward with a proposed solution, and is willing to get into the detail to prove it works
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical accounting and systems issues for non‑accounting stakeholders and leadership

Preferred Qualifications

  • CPA
  • Big 4 or comparable public accounting experience
  • Experience in a high‑growth, pre‑IPO or newly public SaaS or technology company
  • Experience implementing or materially re‑architecting a billing system or revenue sub‑ledger
  • Working knowledge of SQL, or experience building reporting data models and partnering on a data warehouse/BI implementation (e.g., BigQuery, Snowflake, Looker, Tableau)
  • Exposure to SOX readiness, audit remediation, or public‑company control environments
  • Familiarity with Workiva or similar SOX/controls documentation tooling

What You'll Do

Sales Process & Systems

  • Implement and translate sales processes strategy into day-to-day execution across account, opportunity, pipeline, forecast, and close.
  • Partner with the Salesforce/System Admin to translate commercial needs into system requirements and automation.
  • Identify friction across the sales process at scale and lead cross-functional initiatives that improve seller productivity, cycle time, and conversion

Deal Desk and Commercial Standards

Planning and Coverage

  • Experience owning or significantly improving CRM, BI, planning, compensation, or revenue technology systems.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex data into clear insights and practical recommendations.
  • Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills and experience with BI or reporting tools such as Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or similar.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce or comparable CRM platforms; experience partnering with Business Systems or Data Engineering teams is highly valuable.
  • Experience designing scalable processes, data governance frameworks, reporting systems, and operational workflows.
  • Ability to manage complex, cross-functional programs with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
  • Strong commercial judgment and the ability to connect operational improvements to revenue outcomes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations to senior leaders.
  • Comfortable working hands-on in the details while maintaining a strategic view of the broader business.
  • AI fluency and curiosity about applying AI, automation, and emerging tools to improve sales productivity and operational efficiency.
  • High ownership, sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and a bias toward action.
  • Comfortable and energized operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment where priorities evolve quickly.
  • Proof of eligibility to work in the United States is required.

The base salary range for candidates within the San Francisco Bay Area is $145,800-$174,150. Actual base pay will depend on a variety of factors such as education, skills, experience, location, etc. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love.

Policies

Fin has a hybrid working policy. We believe that working in person helps us stay connected, collaborate easier and create a great culture while still providing flexibility to work from home. We expect employees to be in the office at least three days per week. We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. As an organization, our policy is to not advocate on behalf of the company or our employees on any social or political topics out of our internal or external communications. Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .

About the Team

The People Operations team owns the systems, processes, and programs that make the employee lifecycle run — from day one through every transition in between. We believe that clean data, simple workflows, and well-designed technology are what let the rest of the People & Talent function do its best work.

About the Role

We're looking for a People Operations Manager who can look at a messy, ambiguous problem and turn it into a clear plan — then execute it. Day-to-day, you'll own our HR technology stack, lead process transformation across the employee lifecycle, and serve as the go-to partner for Payroll, IT, Legal, and the broader People & Talent team when something needs to be built, fixed, or rethought. You'll work directly with vendors, HRBPs, and leadership to make sure our operations are scalable, compliant, and actually simple to use. In the first year, success means moving us from where we are to where we should be: better-configured systems, documented processes, and a team that trusts what's in our tools.

Responsibilities

  • Lead HR operations programs end-to-end — define scope, owners, milestones, risks, and success measures, often starting from an undefined brief.
  • Serve as the primary functional owner for core People technology platforms (e.g., HRIS, ATS, LMS, performance tools), including configuration, upgrades, and feature evaluation.
  • Lead technology deployments, platform conversions, and module rollouts, coordinating across IT, HRIS, and vendor teams.
  • Research and benchmark HR technology trends to build and maintain a People tech roadmap that supports scale.
  • Apply AI and emerging tools to improve how the broader People Operations function works — not just your own workflow.
  • Establish and enforce data governance standards across HR systems to ensure accuracy, consistency, and audit readiness.
  • Design and implement a tiered HR support model with clear ownership, escalation paths, and defined service levels.
  • Map current-state and future-state workflows across People, Payroll, Finance, and IT to reduce manual work and maximize automation.
  • Author and maintain the SOP and documentation library at a function level — consistent, audit-ready, and accessible across the team.
  • Own end-to-end compliance for higher-risk programs including I-9/E-Verify, records retention, and system access auditing.
  • Monitor employment law and data privacy developments and translate changes into compliant system configurations and workflows.
  • Manage relationships with external partners, including EOR providers and software vendors, and lead escalations and accountability conversations directly.
  • Facilitate alignment among diverse stakeholders — from managers to HR leadership — adapting communication style and detail level to the audience.

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

  • Owned People Operations programs in a high-growth technology environment, including navigating ambiguity and building structure where little existed before.
  • Served as a functional owner or administrator for HR platforms such as an HRIS, ATS, or LMS — including configuration, rollouts, and cross-functional coordination with IT and vendors.
  • Built or contributed to a People technology roadmap, including evaluating tools, benchmarking options, and making a case to leadership for investment decisions.
  • Documented and redesigned people processes across the full employee lifecycle, with a track record of reducing manual steps and improving the experience for employees and operators.
  • Influenced cross-functional partners — in Payroll, Finance, IT, or Legal — to adopt new workflows or ways of working, without direct authority over those teams.
  • Applied structured project management practices to multi-stakeholder initiatives: clear plans, tracked dependencies, proactive risk communication, and executive-ready status updates.
  • Established or enforced data governance standards in HR systems, including data quality audits, mass change approvals, and corrective action with multiple teams.
  • Managed compliance programs (such as I-9/E-Verify, records retention, or data privacy requirements) with a proactive approach — building audits and controls before issues surface.
  • Communicated clearly and directly across levels — from frontline employees to leadership — and adapted the message without losing the substance.

Bonus Points For

  • Experience with Paylocity, Lattice, or ChartHop specifically, or a documented history of migrating between major HR platforms.
  • Familiarity with employer-of-record (EOR) models and the operational complexity of a distributed, global workforce.
  • Experience building or refining a tiered HR service model (self-service through HRIS escalation).
  • Applied use of AI tools to redesign team workflows, not just individual productivity.

Compensation

The amount listed below is the total target cash compensation (TTCC) and includes base compensation and variable compensation in the form of either a company bonus or commissions. Variable compensation type is determined by your role and level. In addition to the cash compensation provided, this position is also eligible for equity consideration and other benefits including medical, vision, and dental insurance coverage. You can view our benefits offerings here.

Within the range, individual pay is determined by experience, job-related skills, qualifications, and other factors. If you have questions about the specific range, your recruiter can share this information.

Benefits and Perks

  • Generous Vacation Policy & Additional Company Holidays
  • Enhanced Parental Leave
  • Additional US Benefits: Pre-Tax Benefits including 401(K), Wellness Benefit, Holiday Break

*please note that benefits and perks for contract positions will vary*

Culture Values

  • Make Bold Bets: We choose courageous action over comfortable progress.
  • Innovate with Insight: We tackle decisions with rigor and judgment - combining data, experience and collective wisdom to drivepowerful outcomes.
  • One Team: We collaborate across boundaries to achieve far greater impact than any of us could accomplish alone.
  • Candor with Connection: We build meaningful relationships that enable honest feedback and direct conversations.
  • Champion the Customer: We seek to deeply understand our customers’ needs, ensuring their success is our north star.
  • Powerful Simplicity: We find elegant solutions to complex problems, making sophisticated things accessible.

Why choose Mixpanel?

We’re a leader in analytics with over 29,000 customers and $277M invested from prominent investors: like Andreessen-Horowitz, Sequoia, YC, and, most recently, Bain Capital. Mixpanel’s pioneering event-based data analytics platform offers a powerful yet simple solution for companies to understand user behaviors and easily track overarching company success metrics. Our accomplished teams continuously facilitate our expansion by tackling the ever-evolving challenges tied to scaling, reliability, design, and service. Choosing to work at Mixpanel means you’ll be helping the world’s most innovative companies learn from their data so they can make better decisions.

Mixpanel is an equal opportunity employer supporting workforce diversity. At Mixpanel, we are focused on things that really matter—our people, our customers, our partners—out of a recognition that those relationships are the most valuable assets we have. We actively encourage women, people with disabilities, veterans, underrepresented minorities, and LGBTQ+ people to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance or other similar laws that may be applicable, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. The Senior Sales Operations Manager is at the center of House-Hasson Hardware's sales organization, turning strategy into scalable process, data into decisions, and cross-functional coordination into results. This high-visibility role partners with Sales Leadership, Marketing, Operations, Purchasing, and Customer Service to improve customer experience and sales productivity — regularly leading initiatives across teams that don't report to this position. You'll bring structure to complex sales processes, turn data into actionable insight, build the tools and reporting that help the field sell more effectively, and drive initiatives from planning through execution. With exposure to sales process improvement, CRM strategy, analytics and reporting, forecasting, territory planning, and cross-functional project leadership, this is an opportunity to shape how House-Hasson's sales organization operates as it grows into new markets and a new industrial business division.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Own the big picture. Partner with executive leadership to develop and implement scalable sales processes that support company growth, maintaining a clear view of what's working across the sales cycle.
  • Fix what's broken. Evaluate the end-to-end sales cycle to identify inefficiencies, diagnose root causes, redesign processes, drive adoption, and measure the results.
  • Keep the field informed. Ensure the field sales team receives timely, accurate, and actionable information, and develop tools, templates, and resources that help them sell more effectively.
  • Be the connection point. Lead cross-functional initiatives with Marketing, Operations, Purchasing, and Customer Service — setting milestones, assigning owners, holding deadlines, and escalating appropriately to keep teams outside your direct authority accountable.
  • Turn information into insight. Build and maintain dashboards and reports measuring key sales KPIs — revenue, margin, growth, customer penetration, forecast accuracy, pipeline, retention, and productivity — and prepare executive-level reporting on pipeline health and performance.
  • Make the CRM work for the team. Drive CRM adoption, data quality, and reporting discipline, using it as a sales-management and productivity tool rather than just a system of record.
  • Coordinate what’s next. Lead seasonal promotions, dealer programs, virtual markets, vendor campaigns, and other sales initiatives from planning through execution, including forecasting, readiness, field communication, and post-initiative analysis.
  • Help the business run smarter. Identify opportunities to automate manual processes, and support annual sales planning, budgeting, forecasting, and territory optimization.
  • Build understanding of the business. Develop a comprehensive understanding of House-Hasson's customer base, store formats, market segments, and growth opportunities to support strategic account development and customer acquisition.
  • Start with listening. In your first 90 days, prioritize listening, data and process mapping, and establishing performance baselines before proposing major changes.
  • Grow the sales organization's capability. Support onboarding and ongoing training for sales representatives on systems, processes, and best practices, and participate in strategic projects tied to new business initiatives and organizational growth.

Qualifications: Required Skills & Abilities

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and financial modeling capabilities.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, complex formulas, forecasting/modeling with large datasets), with the ability to organize, analyze, and present information effectively.

  • Naturally takes ownership. You see what needs to happen, take initiative, and drive projects and processes through to completion.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority and build strong cross-functional relationships across departments.
  • Excellent project management and organizational skills, including managing initiatives from planning through execution.
  • Strong communicator and collaborator, able to translate complex data into meaningful business recommendations for leadership and the field.

  • Lead post-incident reviews and implement corrective and preventive actions following major operational issues.
  • Support peak-season planning and ensure operational readiness for sudden increases in shipment volumes and customer requirements.

Location

This is a hybrid in-office role.

Medidata follows a hybrid office policy in which employees who are hired for an in-person position are expected to work on site a certain number of days per week following Company policy.

About our Company

Medidata is powering smarter treatments and healthier people through digital solutions to support clinical trials. Celebrating over 25 years of ground-breaking technological innovation across more than 38,000 trials and 12 million patients, Medidata offers industry-leading expertise, analytics-powered insights, and one of the largest clinical trial data sets in the industry.

More than 1 million registered users across approximately 2,300 customers trust Medidata's seamless, end-to-end platform to improve patient experiences, accelerate clinical breakthroughs, and bring therapies to market faster.

A Dassault Systèmes brand (Euronext Paris: FR0014003TT8, DSY.PA), Medidata is headquartered in New York City and has been recognized as a Leader by Everest Group and IDC.

Discover more at www.medidata.com.

Listen to our latest podcast, from Dreamers to Disruptors, and follow us at @Medidata.

About the Team

The Director of Marketing Operations - Project Management & Planning is responsible for defining and leading the strategic vision, operating model, and execution framework for how marketing work gets done across the organization. This role goes beyond managing project delivery - it establishes project management as a core business capability that drives alignment, prioritization, and measurable impact across the marketing function. You will oversee a team of project management experts, while partnering with senior marketing and cross-functional executives to ensure that marketing investments are executed with rigor, transparency, and speed. As a leader within Marketing Operations, you will report to the VP of Marketing Operations and play a critical role in shaping how marketing translates strategy into execution at scale.

Responsibilities

  • Strategic Leadership & Operating Model Ownership: Define and evolve the marketing project management operating model - including workflows, prioritization frameworks, standards, and the supporting technology roadmap. Continuously improve processes to increase speed, quality, and cross-team collaboration, and lead the change management needed to embed new ways of working and drive adoption across teams.
  • Organizational Alignment & Executive Partnership: Act as a strategic partner to the marketing leadership team to align on priorities, trade-offs, and execution plans. Define and track the service levels and success metrics for execution (e.g., on-time delivery, cycle time, delivery volume, resource utilization), elevating reporting from project-level tracking to cross-initiative insights that inform executive decision-making.
  • Cross-Team Coordination: Maintain a clear view of active marketing initiatives - campaigns, launches, and programs - and lead the process that prioritizes, sequences, and resources them against business impact.
  • Cross-Functional Program Leadership: Directly lead select high-priority initiatives that span multiple marketing teams - owning planning, execution, and delivery for programs that cross team boundaries and require centralized coordination.
  • Annual Marketing Planning & Budget Ownership: Facilitate the annual marketing planning process, partnering with individual marketing teams to plan activities, headcount, and program budget for future years. Help drive capacity planning and scenario modeling when needed to align resources to strategic priorities, facilitate trade-off decisions, and ensure plans ladder up to overall marketing and business objectives.
  • Team Leadership & Capability Building: Lead and develop a team of project management experts. Build a high-performing organization with clear career paths, role clarity, and scalable ways of working. Champion the application of AI across marketing project management - automating status reporting, surfacing risks and capacity conflicts earlier, and streamlining intake and planning. Partner with the marketing technology team on tool adoption and contribute to the marketing organization's broader AI operationalization efforts.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required in Marketing, Communications, Business, or related field; a Master's degree or MBA is a plus
  • 10 - 15+ years of experience in project/program management or marketing operations, with strong executive communications and team leadership experience
  • Proven track record of building and scaling project management functions or PMOs within B2B technology or SaaS organizations; demonstrated ability to navigate ambiguity, make decisions with incomplete information, and drive projects to completion across competing priorities; Deep expertise in Marketing programs management, resource planning, and operational rigor within a B2B marketing environment;
  • Strong business acumen with the ability to connect execution to revenue and growth outcomes
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, and organizational change management skills
  • Advanced experience with project management and work management platforms; familiarity with AI-powered project and work management tools, and a track record of adopting new technologies to improve operational efficiency

As with all roles, Medidata sets ranges based on a number of factors including function, level, candidate expertise and experience, and geographic location. Pay ranges for candidates in locations other than New York City, may differ based on the local market data in that region.

The salary range for positions that will be physically based in New York is $135,000- $180,000

Base pay is one part of the Total Rewards that Medidata provides to compensate and recognize employees for their work. Most sales positions are eligible for a commission on the terms of applicable plan documents, and many of Medidata's non-sales positions are eligible for annual bonuses. Medidata believes that benefits should connect you to the support you need when it matters most and provides benefits, including medical, dental, life and disability insurance, 401(k) matching, family leave, flexible paid time off; and 10 paid holidays per year.

Equal Employment Opportunity

In order to provide equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals, employment decisions at Medidata are based on merit, qualifications and abilities. Medidata is committed to a policy of non-discrimination and equal opportunity for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical or common conditions related to pregnancy or childbirth), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, familial status, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, military service, application for military service, genetic information, receipt of free medical care, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Medidata will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

Salary Pay Transparency

Compensation for the role will be commensurate with experience. The total expected compensation range will be between $135000 and $180000, representing the base salary (or annualized salary based on estimated hourly compensation) and target bonus.
